# Bus (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/commands/command-bus)

The `CommandBus` is the [`EventBus`](/use/events/busses) used for emitting command events.

## Overriding [#overriding]

<Steps>
<Step>
## Creation and Registration [#creation-and-registration]

Create your own bus [in any way](/use/events/buses) and set it to the [`CommandManager`](/extend/commands/command-manager).

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { type CommandEventArgs, type NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import { Client, type ClientEvents } from 'discord.js';
declare const client: Client;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
import { BasicEventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyCommandBus extends BasicEventBus<CommandEventArgs> {
  /** Your overrides */
}

const commandBus = MyCommandBus.createAsync();

await bot.getCommandManager().setEventBus(commandBus);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { type CommandEventArgs, type NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import { Client, type ClientEvents } from 'discord.js';
declare const client: Client;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
import { BasicEventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyCommandBus extends BasicEventBus<CommandEventArgs> {
  /** Your overrides */
}

const commandBus = MyCommandBus.createAsync();

await bot.getCommandManager().setEventBus(commandBus);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { type CommandEventArgs, type NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import { Client, type ClientEvents } from 'discord.js';
declare const client: Client;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
import { BasicEventBus } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyCommandBus extends BasicEventBus<CommandEventArgs> {
  /** Your overrides */
}

const commandBus = MyCommandBus.createAsync();

await bot.getCommandManager().setEventBus(commandBus);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The <DocsLink pkg='base' name='BasicEventBus.createSync()' decorated={false} /> (or
<DocsLink pkg='base' name='BasicEventBus.createAsync()' decorated={false} />) method instantiates your custom bus,
not the default one.

</Step>
</Steps>


# CustomId Codec (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/commands/command-customidcodec)

The <DocsLink pkg='base' name='CommandCustomIdCodec' decorated={false} /> is responsible for de/serializing commands to/from customId strings, for the [Command Components](/use/commands/components) feature.

The default implementation (<DocsLink pkg='base' name='DefaultCommandCustomIdCodec' decorated={false} />) uses the [`@sapphire/string-store`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sapphire/string-store) package to efficiently de/serialize the data.

## When to override [#when-to-override]

| ✅ Override if you want to...         | ❌ Don't override if you want to...                                                                             |
|--------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Use a custom de/serialization logic. | De/serialize your extra data. You should do that on sending/receiving instead, as it'll be easier to maintain. |

## Overriding [#overriding]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation]

Create a custom codec by either:

* Extending <DocsLink pkg='base' name='DefaultCommandCustomIdCodec' decorated={false} /> (<BaseMention />'s implementation, recommended for less work).
* Implementing <DocsLink pkg='base' name='CommandCustomIdCodec' decorated={false} /> (<BaseMention />'s interface).

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandCustomIdCodec } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyCommandCustomIdCodec extends DefaultCommandCustomIdCodec {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandCustomIdCodec } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyCommandCustomIdCodec extends DefaultCommandCustomIdCodec {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandCustomIdCodec } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyCommandCustomIdCodec extends DefaultCommandCustomIdCodec {}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>
</Step>
<Step>
### Registration [#registration]

Create it and set it to the [`CommandManager`](/extend/commands/command-manager).

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut---
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
import { DefaultCommandCustomIdCodec } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyCommandCustomIdCodec extends DefaultCommandCustomIdCodec {
  /** Your overrides */
}

const customIdCodec = MyCommandCustomIdCodec.create();

bot.getCommandManager().setCustomIdCodec(customIdCodec);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut---
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
import { DefaultCommandCustomIdCodec } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyCommandCustomIdCodec extends DefaultCommandCustomIdCodec {
  /** Your overrides */
}

const customIdCodec = MyCommandCustomIdCodec.create();

bot.getCommandManager().setCustomIdCodec(customIdCodec);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut---
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
import { DefaultCommandCustomIdCodec } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyCommandCustomIdCodec extends DefaultCommandCustomIdCodec {
  /** Your overrides */
}

const customIdCodec = MyCommandCustomIdCodec.create();

bot.getCommandManager().setCustomIdCodec(customIdCodec);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The <DocsLink pkg='base' name='DefaultCommandCustomIdCodec.create()' decorated={false} /> method instantiates your custom codec, not the default one.

</Step>
</Steps>


# Deployer (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/commands/command-deployer)

The `CommandDeployer` is responsible for deploying commands to Discord and storing the [ApplicationCommand](https://discord.js.org/docs/packages/discord.js/stable/ApplicationCommand:Class) mappings.

## When to override [#when-to-override]

| ✅ Override if you want to...        | ❌ Don't override if you want to...                                                                                                                         |
|-------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Deploy commands in a different way. | Change command serialization. That is done in the command itself, you can override your `data` property or `getData()` method instead.                     |
|                                     | Deploy commands conditionally or manually. Instead, return `deployCommands: false` on `Bot.create()` and call `CommandManager#deploy()` when you want.     |

## Overriding [#overriding]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation]

Create a custom deployer by either:

* Extending `DefaultCommandDeployer` (recommended, less work).
* Implementing `CommandDeployer`.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandDeployer } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyCommandDeployer extends DefaultCommandDeployer {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandDeployer } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyCommandDeployer extends DefaultCommandDeployer {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandDeployer } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyCommandDeployer extends DefaultCommandDeployer {}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Registration [#registration]

Create it and set it to the [`CommandManager`](/extend/commands/command-manager).

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandDeployer } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import { Client } from 'discord.js';
import type { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const client: Client;
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut---
class MyCommandDeployer extends DefaultCommandDeployer {
  /** Your overrides */
}

bot.getCommandManager().setDeployer(MyCommandDeployer.create(client));
```

The <DocsLink pkg='djs' name='DefaultCommandDeployer.create()' decorated={false} /> method instantiates your custom deployer, not the default one.
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandDeployer, type Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { API, Snowflake } from '@discordjs/core';
declare const api: API;
declare const applicationId: Snowflake;
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut---
class MyCommandDeployer extends DefaultCommandDeployer {
  /** Your overrides */
}

bot.getCommandManager().setDeployer(MyCommandDeployer.create(api, applicationId));
```

The <DocsLink pkg='djs-core' name='DefaultCommandDeployer.create()' decorated={false} /> method instantiates your custom deployer, not the default one.
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandDeployer, type Bot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { API, Snowflake } from '@discordjs/core';
declare const api: API;
declare const applicationId: Snowflake;
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut---
class MyCommandDeployer extends DefaultCommandDeployer {
  /** Your overrides */
}

bot.getCommandManager().setDeployer(MyCommandDeployer.create(api, applicationId));
```

The <DocsLink pkg='djs-core' name='DefaultCommandDeployer.create()' decorated={false} /> method instantiates your custom deployer, not the default one.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
</Steps>


# Manager (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/commands/command-manager)

The `CommandManager` is the object that holds together the nyx command system. At a glance:

- Core services: owns the command building blocks, creating defaults in `create()` while still allowing targeted injections.
- State and deployment sync: add/remove operations update repository and deployer together with rollback on deploy failures, while edit/set keep both layers aligned for bulk updates.
- Interaction routing and execution: resolves incoming interactions to executable commands (including `customId` decoding for component interactions), then runs execute/autocomplete through the executor.
- Manager events: emits `CommandAdd`, `CommandRemove`, `CommandRun`, and `CommandAutocomplete` so other parts of the system can react to lifecycle and runtime actions.

In practice, this makes it the boundary where command registration, resolution, execution, deployment, subscriptions, events, and runtime metadata are coordinated.

## Overriding [#overriding]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation]
Create a custom command manager by either:

* Extending `DefaultCommandManager`.
* Implementing `CommandManager`.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandManager } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyCommandManager extends DefaultCommandManager {
  public myCustomPublicMethod() {
    return 'I work!' as const;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandManager } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyCommandManager extends DefaultCommandManager {
  public myCustomPublicMethod() {
    return 'I work!' as const;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandManager } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyCommandManager extends DefaultCommandManager {
  public myCustomPublicMethod() {
    return 'I work!' as const;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Registration [#registration]

Then you can pass it to your bot:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { Client } from 'discord.js';
import { DefaultCommandManager } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyCommandManager extends DefaultCommandManager {
  public myCustomPublicMethod() {
    return 'I work!' as const;
  }
}
// ---cut---
import { Bot, type NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

const myBot = Bot.create((bot: NyxBot) => ({
  // ---cut-start---
  token: 'TOKEN',
  client: new Client({ intents: [] }),
  logger: console,
  deployCommands: true,
  // @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
  // ---cut-end---
  // ... other options
  commandManager: new MyCommandManager(/** ... */),
}));

const manager = myBot.getCommandManager();
const result = manager.myCustomPublicMethod();
//     ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { Client, GatewayIntentBits } from '@discordjs/core';
import { REST } from '@discordjs/rest';
import { WebSocketManager } from '@discordjs/ws';
import { DefaultCommandManager } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

const rest = new REST({ version: '10' }).setToken('TOKEN');
const gateway = new WebSocketManager({ token: 'TOKEN', intents: GatewayIntentBits.Guilds, rest });
const client = new Client({ rest, gateway });

class MyCommandManager extends DefaultCommandManager {
  public myCustomPublicMethod() {
    return 'I work!' as const;
  }
}
// ---cut---
import { Bot, CoreNyxClient, type NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

const myBot = Bot.create((bot: NyxBot) => ({
  // ---cut-start---
  token: 'TOKEN',
  client: new CoreNyxClient(client, gateway, 'APPLICATION_ID'),
  logger: console,
  deployCommands: true,
  // @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
  // ---cut-end---
  // ... other options
  commandManager: new MyCommandManager(/** ... */),
}));

const manager = myBot.getCommandManager();
const result = manager.myCustomPublicMethod();
//     ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandManager } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyCommandManager extends DefaultCommandManager {
  public myCustomPublicMethod() {
    return 'I work!' as const;
  }
}
// ---cut---
import { HttpBot, type NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const myBot = HttpBot.create((bot: NyxBot) => ({
  // ---cut-start---
  applicationId: 'APPLICATION_ID',
  publicKey: 'PUBLIC_KEY',
  token: 'TOKEN',
  logger: console,
  deployCommands: true,
  // @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
  // ---cut-end---
  // ... other options
  commandManager: new MyCommandManager(/** ... */),
}));

const manager = myBot.getCommandManager();
const result = manager.myCustomPublicMethod();
//     ^?
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The class is able to infer the type of your custom manager, so accessing any custom method or property will work without errors.

If you ever want to use this custom bot type with your injected manager somewhere else, you can do so via the generic:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { Client } from 'discord.js';
import { DefaultCommandManager } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
class MyCommandManager extends DefaultCommandManager {
  public myCustomPublicMethod() {
    return 'I work!' as const;
  }
}
// ---cut---
import type { NyxBot, InjectableBotDependencies } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

type BotWithCustomManager = NyxBot<InjectableBotDependencies & { commandManager: MyCommandManager }>;

function functionOnlyForCustomManager(bot: BotWithCustomManager) {
  const manager = bot.getCommandManager();
  const result = manager.myCustomPublicMethod();
  //     ^?
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { Client } from 'discord.js';
import { DefaultCommandManager } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
class MyCommandManager extends DefaultCommandManager {
  public myCustomPublicMethod() {
    return 'I work!' as const;
  }
}
// ---cut---
import type { NyxBot, InjectableBotDependencies } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

type BotWithCustomManager = NyxBot<InjectableBotDependencies & { commandManager: MyCommandManager }>;

function functionOnlyForCustomManager(bot: BotWithCustomManager) {
  const manager = bot.getCommandManager();
  const result = manager.myCustomPublicMethod();
  //     ^?
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { Client } from 'discord.js';
import { DefaultCommandManager } from '@nyx-discord/http';
class MyCommandManager extends DefaultCommandManager {
  public myCustomPublicMethod() {
    return 'I work!' as const;
  }
}
// ---cut---
import type { NyxBot, InjectableBotDependencies } from '@nyx-discord/http';

type BotWithCustomManager = NyxBot<InjectableBotDependencies & { commandManager: MyCommandManager }>;

function functionOnlyForCustomManager(bot: BotWithCustomManager) {
  const manager = bot.getCommandManager();
  const result = manager.myCustomPublicMethod();
  //     ^?
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

For readability purposes, we recommend storing the type with the generic in a separate type, like in the example.

</Step>
</Steps>


# Repository (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/commands/command-repository)

The `CommandRepository` is responsible for storing all the currently registered commands.

## When to override [#when-to-override]

| ✅ Override if you want to...    | ❌ Don't override if you want to...                                                                                   |
|---------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Change how commands are stored. | Do something when commands are added, including decorating them. Use [Command Events](/use/commands/events) instead. |
|                                 | Change how commands are deployed. Override the [CommandDeployer](/extend/commands/command-deployer) instead.         |

## Overriding [#overriding]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation]

Create a custom command repository by either:

* Extending `DefaultCommandRepository` (recommended, less work).
* Implementing `CommandRepository`.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```  ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandRepository } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyCommandRepository extends DefaultCommandRepository {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandRepository } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyCommandRepository extends DefaultCommandRepository {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandRepository } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyCommandRepository extends DefaultCommandRepository {}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Registration [#registration]

Create it and set it to the [`CommandManager`](/extend/commands/command-manager).

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandRepository } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
class MyCommandRepository extends DefaultCommandRepository {
  /** Your overrides */
}

bot.getCommandManager().setRepository(MyCommandRepository.create());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandRepository } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
class MyCommandRepository extends DefaultCommandRepository {
  /** Your overrides */
}

bot.getCommandManager().setRepository(MyCommandRepository.create());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandRepository } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
class MyCommandRepository extends DefaultCommandRepository {
  /** Your overrides */
}

bot.getCommandManager().setRepository(MyCommandRepository.create());
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The <DocsLink pkg='base' name='DefaultCommandRepository.create()' decorated={false} /> method instantiates your custom repository, not the default one.

</Step>
</Steps>


# Resolver (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/commands/command-resolver)

The `CommandResolver` is responsible for locating commands given an interaction or `customId` context.

## When to override [#when-to-override]

| ✅ Override if you want to...                                                            | ❌ Don't override if you want to...                                                                           |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Customize how commands are located from the repository when an interaction is received. | Introduce other localization methods. It's easier to make your own method that uses the `CommandRepository`. |
| You need to perform extra logic while locating a command.                               | Deserialize `customIds` in different ways. That would be the [`CommandCustomIdCodec`](./command-customid-codec)'s job.                   |

## Overriding [#overriding]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation]
Create a custom command resolver by either:

* Extending `DefaultCommandResolver` (recommended, less work).
* Implementing `CommandResolver`.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandResolver } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyCommandResolver extends DefaultCommandResolver {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandResolver } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyCommandResolver extends DefaultCommandResolver {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandResolver } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyCommandResolver extends DefaultCommandResolver {}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Registration [#registration]

Create it and set it to the [`CommandManager`](/extend/commands/command-manager).

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandResolver } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
class MyCommandResolver extends DefaultCommandResolver {
  /** Your overrides */
}

bot.getCommandManager().setResolver(MyCommandResolver.create());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandResolver } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
class MyCommandResolver extends DefaultCommandResolver {
  /** Your overrides */
}

bot.getCommandManager().setResolver(MyCommandResolver.create());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandResolver } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
class MyCommandResolver extends DefaultCommandResolver {
  /** Your overrides */
}

bot.getCommandManager().setResolver(MyCommandResolver.create());
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The <DocsLink pkg='djs' name='DefaultCommandResolver.create()' decorated={false} /> method instantiates your custom resolver, not the default one.

</Step>
</Steps>


# Subscriptions Container (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/commands/command-subscriptions-container)

The `CommandSubscriptionsContainer` is responsible for storing the subscribers that are subscribed to the [Client's `EventBus`](/use/events) to listen for command interactions.

## Overriding [#overriding]

<Steps>
<Step>
## Creation and Registration [#creation-and-registration]

Create your own container by extending `DefaultCommandSubscriptionsContainer` and set it to the [`CommandManager`](/extend/commands/command-manager).

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandSubscriptionsContainer } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut---
import { DefaultCommandInteractionSubscriber, DefaultCommandAutocompleteSubscriber } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MySubscriptionsContainer extends DefaultCommandSubscriptionsContainer {
  /** Your overrides */
}


const container = MySubscriptionsContainer.create(
  bot.getClientEventBus(),
  new DefaultCommandInteractionSubscriber(),
  new DefaultCommandAutocompleteSubscriber(),
);

bot.getCommandManager().setSubscriptions(container);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandSubscriptionsContainer } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut---
import { DefaultCommandInteractionSubscriber, DefaultCommandAutocompleteSubscriber } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MySubscriptionsContainer extends DefaultCommandSubscriptionsContainer {
  /** Your overrides */
}


const container = MySubscriptionsContainer.create(
  bot.getClientEventBus(),
  new DefaultCommandInteractionSubscriber(),
  new DefaultCommandAutocompleteSubscriber(),
);

bot.getCommandManager().setSubscriptions(container);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandSubscriptionsContainer } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut---
import { DefaultCommandInteractionSubscriber, DefaultCommandAutocompleteSubscriber } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MySubscriptionsContainer extends DefaultCommandSubscriptionsContainer {
  /** Your overrides */
}


const container = MySubscriptionsContainer.create(
  bot.getClientEventBus(),
  new DefaultCommandInteractionSubscriber(),
  new DefaultCommandAutocompleteSubscriber(),
);

bot.getCommandManager().setSubscriptions(container);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The <DocsLink pkg='djs' name='DefaultCommandSubscriptionsContainer.create()' decorated={false} /> method instantiates your custom container, not the default one.

</Step>
</Steps>


# Error Handler (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/commands/executor/command-error-handler)

The `CommandErrorHandler` is responsible for handling errors thrown by middlewares and commands.

It's inside the [`CommandExecutor`](/extend/commands/executor) object, and will be used by it.

## When to override [#when-to-override]

| ✅ Override if you want to...              | ❌ Don't override if you want to...                                                 |
|-------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Resolve consumers with a different logic. | Add new consumers or a fallback one. The object already supports these operations. |

## Overriding [#overriding]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation]

Create a custom error handler by either:

* Extending `BasicErrorHandler<AnyExecutableCommand, CommandExecutionArgs>` (recommended, less work).
* Implementing `CommandErrorHandler`.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler, type AnyExecutableCommand, type CommandExecutionArgs } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyErrorHandler extends BasicErrorHandler<AnyExecutableCommand, CommandExecutionArgs> {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler, type AnyExecutableCommand, type CommandExecutionArgs } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyErrorHandler extends BasicErrorHandler<AnyExecutableCommand, CommandExecutionArgs> {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler, type AnyExecutableCommand, type CommandExecutionArgs } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyErrorHandler extends BasicErrorHandler<AnyExecutableCommand, CommandExecutionArgs> {}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Registration [#registration]

Create it and set it to the [`CommandExecutor`](/extend/commands/executor), then set the executor on the [`CommandManager`](/extend/commands/command-manager).

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler, type AnyExecutableCommand, type CommandExecutionArgs } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut---
import { DefaultCommandExecutor } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyErrorHandler extends BasicErrorHandler<AnyExecutableCommand, CommandExecutionArgs> {}

const executor = DefaultCommandExecutor.create({
  injections: {
    errorHandler: MyErrorHandler.create(),
  },
});

bot.getCommandManager().setExecutor(executor);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler, type AnyExecutableCommand, type CommandExecutionArgs } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut---
import { DefaultCommandExecutor } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyErrorHandler extends BasicErrorHandler<AnyExecutableCommand, CommandExecutionArgs> {}

const executor = DefaultCommandExecutor.create({
  injections: {
    errorHandler: MyErrorHandler.create(),
  },
});

bot.getCommandManager().setExecutor(executor);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler, type AnyExecutableCommand, type CommandExecutionArgs } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut---
import { DefaultCommandExecutor } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyErrorHandler extends BasicErrorHandler<AnyExecutableCommand, CommandExecutionArgs> {}

const executor = DefaultCommandExecutor.create({
  injections: {
    errorHandler: MyErrorHandler.create(),
  },
});

bot.getCommandManager().setExecutor(executor);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The `create()` method instantiates your custom error handler, not the default one.

<Callout type="warn" title="Using the Bot's logger">
The default error handler will use `console.error` as a fallback consumer. If you want to change it to the bot's logger, instantiate it this way:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyErrorHandler extends BasicErrorHandler<AnyExecutableCommand, CommandExecutionArgs> {}
// ---cut---
import { TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { AnyExecutableCommand, CommandExecutionArgs } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

const myHandler = MyErrorHandler.createWithFallbackLogger<AnyExecutableCommand, CommandExecutionArgs>(
  (_error, _command, [_interaction, metadata]) => {
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(metadata, true);
    return bot.getLogger();
  }
);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyErrorHandler extends BasicErrorHandler<AnyExecutableCommand, CommandExecutionArgs> {}
// ---cut---
import { TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { AnyExecutableCommand, CommandExecutionArgs } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

const myHandler = MyErrorHandler.createWithFallbackLogger<AnyExecutableCommand, CommandExecutionArgs>(
  (_error, _command, [_interaction, metadata]) => {
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(metadata, true);
    return bot.getLogger();
  }
);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyErrorHandler extends BasicErrorHandler<AnyExecutableCommand, CommandExecutionArgs> {}
// ---cut---
import { TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { AnyExecutableCommand, CommandExecutionArgs } from '@nyx-discord/http';

  (_error, _command, [_interaction, metadata]) => {
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(metadata, true);
    return bot.getLogger();
  }
);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Callout>

</Step>
</Steps>


# Middleware List (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/commands/executor/command-middleware-list)

The `CommandMiddlewareList` is responsible for holding and executing the middlewares that run before a command is executed.

It's inside the [`CommandExecutor`](/extend/commands/executor) object, and will be executed by it.

## When to override [#when-to-override]

| ✅ Override if you want to...                              | ❌ Don't override if you want to...                                        |
|-----------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Do something before, while or after checking middlewares. | Add new middlewares. The list already supports add and remove operations. |
| Check middlewares in a different way or order.            |                                                                           |

## Overriding [#overriding]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation]

Create a custom middleware list by either:

* Extending `CommandMiddlewareList` (recommended, less work).
* Implementing `MiddlewareList<CommandMiddlewareResolvable>`.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { CommandMiddlewareList } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyMiddlewareList extends CommandMiddlewareList {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { CommandMiddlewareList } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyMiddlewareList extends CommandMiddlewareList {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { CommandMiddlewareList } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyMiddlewareList extends CommandMiddlewareList {}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Registration [#registration]

Create it and set it to the [`CommandExecutor`](/extend/commands/executor), then set the executor on the [`CommandManager`](/extend/commands/command-manager).

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { CommandMiddlewareList } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut---
import { DefaultCommandExecutor } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyMiddlewareList extends CommandMiddlewareList {}

const executor = DefaultCommandExecutor.create({
  injections: {
    middleware: MyMiddlewareList.create(),
  },
});
bot.getCommandManager().setExecutor(executor);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { CommandMiddlewareList } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut---
import { DefaultCommandExecutor } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyMiddlewareList extends CommandMiddlewareList {}

const executor = DefaultCommandExecutor.create({
  injections: {
    middleware: MyMiddlewareList.create(),
  },
});
bot.getCommandManager().setExecutor(executor);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { CommandMiddlewareList } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut---
import { DefaultCommandExecutor } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyMiddlewareList extends CommandMiddlewareList {}

const executor = DefaultCommandExecutor.create({
  injections: {
    middleware: MyMiddlewareList.create(),
  },
});
bot.getCommandManager().setExecutor(executor);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The `create()` method instantiates your custom middleware list, not the default one.

</Step>
</Steps>


# Executor (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/commands/executor)

The `CommandExecutor` is responsible for executing commands, making sure the middleware passes and handling errors.

## When to override [#when-to-override]

| ✅ Override if you want to...                                      | ❌ Don't override if you want to...                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Customize how commands are executed.                               | Listen for command runs. [Use the `EventBus` in the `CommandManager` instead](/use/commands/events).                                                                              |
| Add advanced logic while executing a command, like delaying calls. | Add new middlewares or error consumers. You can interact with the [`MiddlewareList`](/use/commands/middlewares) and [`ErrorHandler`](/use/other/error-handling) objects directly, using the getter on the executor. |
|                                                                    | Override the default `MiddlewareList` or `ErrorHandler`. You can do that already from the `DefaultCommandExecutor.create()` options, as shown in the respective guide of the object you want to override. |

## Overriding [#overriding]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation]

Create a custom executor by either:

* Extending `DefaultCommandExecutor` (recommended, less work).
* Implementing `CommandExecutor`.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandExecutor } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyCommandExecutor extends DefaultCommandExecutor {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandExecutor } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyCommandExecutor extends DefaultCommandExecutor {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandExecutor } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyCommandExecutor extends DefaultCommandExecutor {}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Registration [#registration]

Create it and set it to the [`CommandManager`](/extend/commands/command-manager).

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandExecutor } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut---
class MyCommandExecutor extends DefaultCommandExecutor {}

bot.getCommandManager().setExecutor(MyCommandExecutor.create());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandExecutor } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut---
class MyCommandExecutor extends DefaultCommandExecutor {}

bot.getCommandManager().setExecutor(MyCommandExecutor.create());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { DefaultCommandExecutor } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut---
class MyCommandExecutor extends DefaultCommandExecutor {}

bot.getCommandManager().setExecutor(MyCommandExecutor.create());
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The `create()` method instantiates the executor with the default `ErrorHandler` and `MiddlewareList` (which are overridable, as described below). It'll also instantiate your custom class, not the base one.

</Step>
</Steps>

## Dependencies [#dependencies]

You can override the executor's dependencies (`ErrorHandler` and `MiddlewareList`) by passing them as options to the `DefaultCommandExecutor.create()` method. More details in the respective guides:

<Cards>
<Card title="Middleware List" href="/extend/commands/executor/command-middleware-list" icon={<LayersIcon />} external={false}>
  Holds and executes the command middlewares.
</Card>
<Card title="Error Handler" href="/extend/commands/executor/command-error-handler" icon={<AmbulanceIcon />} external={false}>
  Handles command-related errors.
</Card>
</Cards>


# Command Internals (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/commands)

The commands system is made up of several components that work together to store, resolve, execute commands and more.

## Command system components [#command-system-components]

Specifically, these components are:

- [`CommandManager`](/extend/commands/command-manager): The entry point for the command system, holding all the command-related objects and methods that use all of these objects. All objects below are contained here.
- [`CommandResolver`](/extend/commands/command-resolver): Resolves the command that a given command interaction refers to.
- [`CommandExecutor`](/extend/commands/executor): Executes commands, checking its `MiddlewareList` and passing errors to the `ErrorHandler`.
- [`CommandRepository`](/extend/commands/command-repository): Stores all the currently registered commands.
- [`CommandCustomIdCodec`](/extend/commands/command-customidcodec): De/serializes commands names to/from customId strings, for the [Command Components](/use/commands/components) feature.
- [`CommandDeployer`](/extend/commands/command-deployer): Deploys commands to Discord and stores the [ApplicationCommand](https://discord.js.org/docs/packages/discord.js/stable/ApplicationCommand:Class) mappings.
- [`Command EventBus`](/extend/commands/command-bus): An [`EventBus`](../events/event-bus) that emits command related events.
- [`CommandSubscriptionsContainer`](/extend/commands/command-subscriptions-container): Stores the subscribers that are subscribed to the client's `EventBus` to listen for command interactions.

## Execution Sequence [#execution-sequence]

The following diagrams show the flow of a command execution. You can check the guide of each component to see exactly how it works, or how to replace it.

<Callout title="Diagram usage">
- You can zoom and drag on the diagrams.
- A dashed step means it's executed through a non awaited (but caught) Promise, so the next one is inmediately executed if there's an I/O operation in the step.
- You can hover over steps with `(?)` to see extra details.
- If a step goes to a target, and that target doesn't continue the flow, then it's an immediate return, like a getter call.
</Callout>

<Steps>
<Step>
### Command event [#command-event]

For a command to be executed, you first receive a `interactionCreate` event, which is then passed to the [`CommandManager`](./command-manager.mdx):

<CommandEventDiagram />

</Step>
<Step>
### Command resolution [#command-resolution]

The [`CommandResolver`](./command-resolver.mdx) then resolves the command that the interaction refers to. For component interactions, this first needs an intermediate step through the [`CommandCustomIdCodec`](./command-customid-codec.mdx) to deserialize the customId.

#### Command Interactions [#command-interactions]

<CommandResolutionDiagram />

#### Component Interactions [#component-interactions]

<CommandComponentResolutionDiagram />

</Step>

<Step>
### Command execution [#command-execution]

Once the command is resolved, it's passed to the [`CommandExecutor`](./command-executor.mdx):

<CommandExecutionDiagram />

On which the execution ends.

</Step>
</Steps>

Next, see the documentation of each component, where you'll find what it does and how to replace it.


# Error Handler (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/events/dispatcher/event-error-handler)

The `EventSubscriberErrorHandler` handles errors thrown while checking middlewares or executing event subscribers.

It's inside the [`EventDispatcher`](/extend/events/dispatcher) object, and will be used by it.

## When to override [#when-to-override]

| ✅ Override if you want to... | ❌ Don't override if you want to... |
|---|---|
| Resolve error consumers with custom logic. | Add/remove subscribers from buses. That's done with `EventBus#subscribe()` and `EventBus#unsubscribe()`. |
| Change fallback behavior for uncaught errors (logging, telemetry, alerting). | Change middleware order. Use the dispatcher middleware list for that. |
| Route specific error classes to specialized consumers. | Replace dispatch flow entirely. If you only want custom error handling, replacing this dependency is enough. |

## Overriding [#overriding]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation]

Create a custom error handler by either:

* Extending `BasicErrorHandler<AnyEventSubscriber, EventDispatchArgs>` (recommended, less work).
* Implementing `EventSubscriberErrorHandler`.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler, type AnyEventSubscriber, type EventDispatchArgs } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyErrorHandler extends BasicErrorHandler<AnyEventSubscriber, EventDispatchArgs> {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler, type AnyEventSubscriber, type EventDispatchArgs } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyErrorHandler extends BasicErrorHandler<AnyEventSubscriber, EventDispatchArgs> {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler, type AnyEventSubscriber, type EventDispatchArgs } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyErrorHandler extends BasicErrorHandler<AnyEventSubscriber, EventDispatchArgs> {}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Registration [#registration]

Inject it directly when creating the dispatcher:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import {
  BasicErrorHandler,
  type AnyEventSubscriber,
  type EventDispatchArgs,
  type EventBus,
} from '@nyx-discord/djs';

declare const bus: EventBus<{ someEvent: [string] }>;

class MyErrorHandler extends BasicErrorHandler<AnyEventSubscriber, EventDispatchArgs> {}
// ---cut---
import { BasicSyncEventDispatcher } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

const dispatcher = BasicSyncEventDispatcher.create({
  injections: {
    errorHandler: MyErrorHandler.create(),
  },
});

bus.setDispatcher(dispatcher);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import {
  BasicErrorHandler,
  type AnyEventSubscriber,
  type EventDispatchArgs,
  type EventBus,
} from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyErrorHandler extends BasicErrorHandler<AnyEventSubscriber, EventDispatchArgs> {}
// ---cut---
import { BasicSyncEventDispatcher } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

const dispatcher = BasicSyncEventDispatcher.create({
  injections: {
    errorHandler: MyErrorHandler.create(),
  },
});

bus.setDispatcher(dispatcher);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import {
  BasicErrorHandler,
  type AnyEventSubscriber,
  type EventDispatchArgs,
  type EventBus,
} from '@nyx-discord/http';

declare const bus: EventBus<{ someEvent: [string] }>;

class MyErrorHandler extends BasicErrorHandler<AnyEventSubscriber, EventDispatchArgs> {}
// ---cut---
import { BasicSyncEventDispatcher } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const dispatcher = BasicSyncEventDispatcher.create({
  injections: {
    errorHandler: MyErrorHandler.create(),
  },
});

bus.setDispatcher(dispatcher);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Callout type="warn" title="Using the Bot's logger">
To use the bot logger as fallback, create a handler with `createWithFallbackLogger` and inject it:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import {
  BasicSyncEventDispatcher,
  BasicErrorHandler,
  TypedFields,
  type AnyEventSubscriber,
  type EventDispatchArgs,
  type EventBus,
} from '@nyx-discord/djs';

type MyEvents = {
  someEvent: [string];
};

declare const bus: EventBus<MyEvents>;

const errorHandler = BasicErrorHandler.createWithFallbackLogger<AnyEventSubscriber, EventDispatchArgs>(
  (_error, _subscriber, [metadata]) => TypedFields.Bot.get(metadata, true).getLogger(),
);

const dispatcher = BasicSyncEventDispatcher.create({
  injections: {
    errorHandler,
  },
});

bus.setDispatcher(dispatcher);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash

  BasicSyncEventDispatcher,
  BasicErrorHandler,
  TypedFields,

  type EventDispatchArgs,
  type EventBus,

  someEvent: [string];
};

declare const bus: EventBus<MyEvents>;

  (_error, _subscriber, [metadata]) => TypedFields.Bot.get(metadata, true).getLogger(),
);

  injections: {
    errorHandler,
  },
});
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Callout>

</Step>
</Steps>


# Middleware List (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/events/dispatcher/event-middleware-list)

The `SubscriberMiddlewareList` holds and executes the middlewares used by an `EventDispatcher` before each subscriber is called.

It's inside the [`CommandExecutor`](/extend/commands/executor) object, and will be used by it.

## When to override [#when-to-override]

| ✅ Override if you want to... | ❌ Don't override if you want to... |
|---|---|
| Add custom behavior before/after middleware checks. | Change subscriber execution order. That's controlled by the bus and its sorter. |
| Change how middleware errors are wrapped or reported. | Handle subscriber errors. Use the dispatcher's [`ErrorHandler`](/use/other/error-handling) for that. |
| Replace the default middleware chain globally for a dispatcher. | Override all dispatcher logic. If only middleware behavior changes, replacing the list is enough. |

## Overriding [#overriding]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation]

Create a custom middleware list by either:

* Extending `SubscriberMiddlewareList` (recommended, less work).
* Implementing `MiddlewareList<EventSubscriberMiddlewareResolvable>`.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { SubscriberMiddlewareList } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyMiddlewareList extends SubscriberMiddlewareList {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { SubscriberMiddlewareList } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyMiddlewareList extends SubscriberMiddlewareList {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { SubscriberMiddlewareList } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyMiddlewareList extends SubscriberMiddlewareList {}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Registration [#registration]

Inject it directly when creating the dispatcher:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import {
  SubscriberMiddlewareList,
  type EventBus,
} from '@nyx-discord/djs';

declare const bus: EventBus<{ someEvent: [string] }>;

class MyMiddlewareList extends SubscriberMiddlewareList {}
// ---cut---
import { BasicSyncEventDispatcher } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// Works the same with the async dispatcher
const dispatcher = BasicSyncEventDispatcher.create({
  injections: {
    middleware: MyMiddlewareList.create(),
  },
});

bus.setDispatcher(dispatcher);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import {
  SubscriberMiddlewareList,
  type EventBus,
} from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

declare const bus: EventBus<{ someEvent: [string] }>;

class MyMiddlewareList extends SubscriberMiddlewareList {}
// ---cut---
import { BasicSyncEventDispatcher } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// Works the same with the async dispatcher
const dispatcher = BasicSyncEventDispatcher.create({
  injections: {
    middleware: MyMiddlewareList.create(),
  },
});

bus.setDispatcher(dispatcher);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import {
  SubscriberMiddlewareList,
  type EventBus,
} from '@nyx-discord/http';

declare const bus: EventBus<{ someEvent: [string] }>;

class MyMiddlewareList extends SubscriberMiddlewareList {}
// ---cut---
import { BasicSyncEventDispatcher } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// Works the same with the async dispatcher
const dispatcher = BasicSyncEventDispatcher.create({
  injections: {
    middleware: MyMiddlewareList.create(),
  },
});

bus.setDispatcher(dispatcher);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

If you prefer, you can still wrap this in a custom dispatcher class and call `super.create(...)`.

</Step>
</Steps>


# Dispatcher (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/events/dispatcher)

The `EventDispatcher` is responsible for calling `EventSubscribers`, checking middlewares, and handling errors of each emitted event.

It's used by every `EventBus` through `EventBus#emit()`, and can be replaced at runtime with `EventBus#setDispatcher()`.

## When to override [#when-to-override]

| ✅ Override if you want to... | ❌ Don't override if you want to... |
|---|---|
| Change how subscribers are dispatched (batching, throttling, etc). | Add/remove event middlewares only. You can do that from the dispatcher's middleware list. |
| Add custom logic that modify execution (instrumentation, retries, etc). | Add/change error consumers only. You can do that from the dispatcher's error handler. |
| | Tune runtime behavior like sync timeout or async concurrency. The base dispatchers implementations [already allow that](/use/events/buses#subscriber-concurrency). |

## Overriding [#overriding]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation]

Create a custom dispatcher by either:

* Extending `BasicSyncEventDispatcher` or `BasicAsyncEventDispatcher` (recommended, less work).
* Implementing `EventDispatcher`.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicSyncEventDispatcher } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyEventDispatcher extends BasicSyncEventDispatcher {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicSyncEventDispatcher } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyEventDispatcher extends BasicSyncEventDispatcher {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { BasicSyncEventDispatcher } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyEventDispatcher extends BasicSyncEventDispatcher {}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Registration [#registration]

Set your dispatcher on any bus:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicSyncEventDispatcher, type EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

declare const bus: EventBus<{ someEvent: [string] }>;

class MyEventDispatcher extends BasicSyncEventDispatcher {}
// ---cut---
bus.setDispatcher(MyEventDispatcher.create());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicSyncEventDispatcher, type EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

declare const bus: EventBus<{ someEvent: [string] }>;

class MyEventDispatcher extends BasicSyncEventDispatcher {}
// ---cut---
bus.setDispatcher(MyEventDispatcher.create());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { BasicSyncEventDispatcher, type EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/http';

declare const bus: EventBus<{ someEvent: [string] }>;

class MyEventDispatcher extends BasicSyncEventDispatcher {}
// ---cut---
bus.setDispatcher(MyEventDispatcher.create());
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

You can do this for built-in buses too, for example the client bus:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { Client } from 'discord.js';
import { Bot, type NyxBot, BasicAsyncEventDispatcher } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

declare const client: Client;

class MyAsyncDispatcher extends BasicAsyncEventDispatcher {}
// @ts-expect-error incomplete example
// ---cut---
const bot = Bot.create((bot: NyxBot) => { /** options */ });

bot
  .getClientEventBus()
  .setDispatcher(MyAsyncDispatcher.create());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { Client } from 'discord.js';
import { Bot, type NyxBot, BasicAsyncEventDispatcher } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

declare const client: Client;

class MyAsyncDispatcher extends BasicAsyncEventDispatcher {}
// @ts-expect-error incomplete example
// ---cut---
const bot = Bot.create((bot: NyxBot) => { /** options */ });

bot
  .getClientEventBus()
  .setDispatcher(MyAsyncDispatcher.create());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { Client } from 'discord.js';
import { Bot, type NyxBot, BasicAsyncEventDispatcher } from '@nyx-discord/http';

declare const client: Client;

class MyAsyncDispatcher extends BasicAsyncEventDispatcher {}
// @ts-expect-error incomplete example
// ---cut---
const bot = Bot.create((bot: NyxBot) => { /** options */ });

bot
  .getClientEventBus()
  .setDispatcher(MyAsyncDispatcher.create());
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
</Steps>

## Dependencies [#dependencies]

The dispatcher has two core dependencies you can customize:

<Cards>
<Card title="Middleware List" href="/extend/events/dispatcher/event-middleware-list" icon={<LayersIcon />} external={false}>
  Holds and executes event subscriber middlewares.
</Card>
<Card title="Error Handler" href="/extend/events/dispatcher/event-error-handler" icon={<AmbulanceIcon />} external={false}>
  Handles middleware and subscriber execution errors.
</Card>
</Cards>


# Buses (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/events/event-bus)

The `EventBus` is the component that stores subscribers and allows events to be emitted to them.

## When to override [#when-to-override]

| ✅ Override if you want to... | ❌ Don't override if you want to... |
|---|---|
| Wrap a new event source (e.g. Redis, WebSockets). | Change how subscribers are called (use a [custom Dispatcher](/extend/events/dispatcher) instead). |
| Change how subscribers are stored or retrieved. | Filter events globally (use a [Middleware](/use/events/middlewares) instead). |

## Overriding [#overriding]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation]

Create a custom event bus by either:

* Extending `BasicEventBus` (recommended for general purpose).
* Extending `BasicEventEmitterBus` (recommended if wrapping a Node.js `EventEmitter`).
* Implementing `EventBus` from scratch.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicEventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyEventBus extends BasicEventBus<{ myEvent: [string] }> {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicEventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyEventBus extends BasicEventBus<{ myEvent: [string] }> {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { BasicEventBus } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyEventBus extends BasicEventBus<{ myEvent: [string] }> {}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Adapting external sources [#adapting-external-sources]

If you are wrapping an external source, you can listen to it and call `emit()`:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicEventBus, BasicSyncEventDispatcher, DefaultMetadataFactory } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { Identifier, MetadataFactory } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// Mock external source
declare const socket: { on: (event: string, cb: (data: string) => void) => void };

class MySocketBus extends BasicEventBus<{ message: [string] }> {
  constructor(
    metaFactory: MetadataFactory = new DefaultMetadataFactory(),
  ) {
    super(
        (a, b) => a.getPriority() - b.getPriority(),
        BasicSyncEventDispatcher.create(),
        metaFactory
    );

    // Listen to external source and emit internally
    socket.on('message', (data) => {
      this.emit('message', [data]);
    });
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicEventBus, BasicSyncEventDispatcher, DefaultMetadataFactory } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { Identifier, MetadataFactory } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

  ) {
    super(
        (a, b) => a.getPriority() - b.getPriority(),
        BasicSyncEventDispatcher.create(),
        metaFactory
    );

    // Listen to external source and emit internally
    socket.on('message', (data) => {
      this.emit('message', [data]);
    });
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash

      this.emit('message', [data]);

  }

```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
</Steps>


# Events Internals (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/events)

The events system is made up of several components that work together to detect and dispatch events.

## Event system components [#event-system-components]

Specifically, these components are:

- [`EventDispatcher`](/extend/events/dispatcher): Coordinates middleware checks and subscriber execution for each dispatch.
- [`EventBus`](/extend/events/bus): Stores subscribers and emits events.
- [`EventSubscriber`](/use/events/subscriber): Receives events and executes logic.

## Execution Sequence [#execution-sequence]

The following diagrams show the event flow in focused stages. You can check the guide of each component to see exactly how it works, or how to replace it.

<Callout title="Diagram usage">
- You can zoom and drag on the diagram.
- A dashed step means it's executed through a non awaited (but caught) Promise, so the next one is inmediately executed if there's an I/O operation in the step.
- You can hover over steps with `(?)` to see extra details.
- If a step goes to a target, and that target doesn't continue the flow, then it's an immediate return, like a getter call.
</Callout>

<Steps>
<Step>
### Event emit [#event-emit]

When an object emits an event through an [`EventBus`](/use/events/buses), the bus resolves subscribers and delegates execution to the dispatcher:

<EventEmitDiagram />

</Step>
<Step>
### Middleware gate [#middleware-gate]

Before subscribers are executed, the [`EventDispatcher`](/extend/events/dispatcher) checks the event middleware list:

<EventOverviewDiagram />

</Step>
<Step>
### Subscriber dispatch [#subscriber-dispatch]

If middleware allows the dispatch, each [`EventSubscriber`](/use/events/subscribers) is executed and thrown errors are forwarded to the error handler:

<EventSubscriberDispatchDiagram />

</Step>

</Steps>

Next, see the documentation of each component, where you'll find what it does and how to replace it.

# Schedule Internals (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/schedules)

The schedule system stores tasks, tracks when they should run, and executes them with middleware and error handling.

## Schedule system components [#schedule-system-components]

Specifically, these components are:

- [`ScheduleManager`](/extend/schedules/schedule-manager): The entry point for the schedule system, orchestrating the repository, executor, scheduler, and lifecycle events.
- [`ScheduleRepository`](/extend/schedules/schedule-repository): Stores all the currently registered schedules.
- [`ScheduleExecutionScheduler`](/extend/schedules/schedule-execution-scheduler): Determines *when* a schedule should run next and creates the job adapter.
- [`ScheduleJobAdapter`](/extend/schedules/schedule-job-adapter): Wraps the underlying job instance (e.g. a croner `Cron` object, or a timeout).
- [`ScheduleExecutor`](/extend/schedules/schedule-executor): Executes schedules, checking their middleware list and handling errors.
- [`ScheduleMiddlewareList`](/extend/schedules/schedule-executor/schedule-middleware-list): Manages middlewares for schedule execution, including filters.
- [`ScheduleErrorHandler`](/extend/schedules/schedule-executor/schedule-error-handler): Handles middleware and schedule execution errors.

## Execution flow [#execution-flow]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Registration and lifecycle [#registration-and-lifecycle]

When you add a schedule, the `ScheduleManager` stores it in the `ScheduleRepository`, asks the `ScheduleExecutionScheduler` to create a job, and then emits `ScheduleEventEnum.ScheduleAdd`. Removing a schedule follows the same coordination path in reverse and emits `ScheduleEventEnum.ScheduleRemove`.

<ScheduleRegistrationDiagram />

</Step>
<Step>
### Runtime execution [#runtime-execution]

When the job fires, the `ScheduleJobAdapter` hands control to the `ScheduleExecutor`, which checks middlewares, executes the schedule's `tick()` method, and forwards errors to the configured `ScheduleErrorHandler`.

<ScheduleExecutionDiagram />

</Step>
</Steps>

Next, see the documentation of each component, where you'll find what it does and how to replace it.


# Execution Scheduler (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/schedules/schedule-execution-scheduler)

The <DocsLink pkg='base' name='DefaultScheduleExecutionScheduler' decorated={false} /> is responsible for interpreting the schedule's interval (usually a cron string) and creating/managing the <DocsLink pkg='base' name='ScheduleJobAdapter' decorated={false} /> that will trigger execution.

It relies on the [`ScheduleJobAdapter`](/extend/schedules/schedule-job-adapter) to interface with the actual timing mechanism (e.g. `croner`), and the adapter is the one that waits for the scheduled time and invokes the execution.

## When to override [#when-to-override]

| ✅ Override if you want to... | ❌ Don't override if you want to... |
|---|---|
| Use a different timing library or job backend (e.g., not `croner`). | Just adjust the job adapter itself. Create a custom `ScheduleJobAdapter` instead. |
| Support a different interval format or next-run strategy (e.g., RRULE-like scheduling). | Change schedule execution logic (try/catch, retry, middleware behavior). That belongs to `ScheduleExecutor`. |
| Implement custom misfire/catch-up behavior for delayed or missed runs. | Change schedule persistence. That belongs to `ScheduleRepository`. |

## Overriding [#overriding]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation]

Create a custom scheduler extending <DocsLink pkg='base' name='DefaultScheduleExecutionScheduler' decorated={false} />.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultScheduleExecutionScheduler } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyScheduler extends DefaultScheduleExecutionScheduler {
  // Override internal methods
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultScheduleExecutionScheduler } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyScheduler extends DefaultScheduleExecutionScheduler {
  // Override internal methods
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { DefaultScheduleExecutionScheduler } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyScheduler extends DefaultScheduleExecutionScheduler {
  // Override internal methods
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Registration [#registration]

Create it and set it to the [`ScheduleManager`](/extend/schedules/schedule-manager).

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
import { DefaultScheduleExecutionScheduler } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyScheduler extends DefaultScheduleExecutionScheduler {
  /** Your overrides */
}

// @noErrors
bot.getScheduleManager().setScheduler(MyScheduler.create());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
import { DefaultScheduleExecutionScheduler } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyScheduler extends DefaultScheduleExecutionScheduler {
  /** Your overrides */
}

// @noErrors
bot.getScheduleManager().setScheduler(MyScheduler.create());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---

  /** Your overrides */
}

// @noErrors
bot.getScheduleManager().setScheduler(MyScheduler.create());
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The <DocsLink pkg='base' name='DefaultScheduleExecutionScheduler.create()' decorated={false} /> method instantiates your custom scheduler, not the default one.

</Step>
</Steps>


# Executor (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/schedules/schedule-executor)

The `ScheduleExecutor` is responsible for the actual execution of a schedule's logic.

It runs the schedule's `tick()` method, and also:

- Checks the [`ScheduleMiddlewareList`](/extend/schedules/schedule-executor/schedule-middleware-list).
- Wraps the execution in a try-catch block.
- Emits events for success or failure.

## When to override [#when-to-override]

| ✅ Override if you want to... | ❌ Don't override if you want to... |
|---|---|
| Customize execution behavior, including middleware injection or error handling. | Only change the middleware chain. Use `ScheduleMiddlewareList` for that. |
| Instrument executor-owned branches such as success/failure handling. | Only change how errors are consumed. Use `ScheduleErrorHandler` for that. |
| Implement custom retry/backoff or exception mapping for failed executions. | Change when schedules run. That belongs to `ScheduleExecutionScheduler` and `ScheduleJobAdapter`. |

## Overriding [#overriding]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation]

Create a custom executor by either:

* Extending `DefaultScheduleExecutor` (recommended, less work).
* Implementing <DocsLink pkg='base' name='ScheduleExecutor' decorated={false} />.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultScheduleExecutor } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyExecutor extends DefaultScheduleExecutor {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultScheduleExecutor } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyExecutor extends DefaultScheduleExecutor {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { DefaultScheduleExecutor } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyExecutor extends DefaultScheduleExecutor {}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Registration [#registration]

Create it and set it to the [`ScheduleManager`](/extend/schedules/schedule-manager).

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultScheduleExecutor } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
class MyExecutor extends DefaultScheduleExecutor {
  /** Your overrides */
}

bot.getScheduleManager().setExecutor(MyExecutor.create());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { DefaultScheduleExecutor } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---

  /** Your overrides */
}

```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash

import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// ---cut---

  /** Your overrides */
}

bot.getScheduleManager().setExecutor(MyExecutor.create());
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The <DocsLink pkg='base' name='DefaultScheduleExecutor.create()' decorated={false} /> method instantiates your custom executor, not the default one.

</Step>
</Steps>

## Dependencies [#dependencies]

The executor has two core dependencies you can customize:

<Cards>
  <Card title="Middleware List" href="/extend/schedules/schedule-executor/schedule-middleware-list" icon={<LayersIcon />} external={false}>
    Holds and executes schedule middlewares before `tick()` runs.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Error Handler" href="/extend/schedules/schedule-executor/schedule-error-handler" icon={<AmbulanceIcon />} external={false}>
    Handles middleware and schedule execution errors.
  </Card>
</Cards>


# Error Handler (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/schedules/schedule-executor/schedule-error-handler)

The `ScheduleErrorHandler` handles errors thrown while checking middlewares or executing schedule ticks.

It's inside the [`ScheduleExecutor`](/extend/schedules/schedule-executor) object, and will be used by it.

## When to override [#when-to-override]

| ✅ Override if you want to... | ❌ Don't override if you want to... |
|---|---|
| Resolve error consumers with custom logic. | Add or remove middlewares. That's done with the executor's middleware list. |
| Change fallback behavior for uncaught errors, such as logging or telemetry. | Change when schedules run. That's done with `ScheduleExecutionScheduler` and `ScheduleJobAdapter`. |
| Route specific error classes to specialized consumers. | Replace the dispatch flow entirely. If you only want custom error handling, replacing this dependency is enough. |

## Overriding [#overriding]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation]

Create a custom error handler by either:

* Extending `BasicErrorHandler<Schedule, ScheduleTickArgs>` (recommended, less work).
* Implementing `ScheduleErrorHandler`.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler, type Schedule, type ScheduleTickArgs } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyErrorHandler extends BasicErrorHandler<Schedule, ScheduleTickArgs> {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler, type Schedule, type ScheduleTickArgs } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyErrorHandler extends BasicErrorHandler<Schedule, ScheduleTickArgs> {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler, type Schedule, type ScheduleTickArgs } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyErrorHandler extends BasicErrorHandler<Schedule, ScheduleTickArgs> {}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Registration [#registration]

Inject it directly when creating the executor, then set that executor to the [`ScheduleManager`](/extend/schedules/schedule-manager):

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import {
  BasicErrorHandler,
  ScheduleMiddlewareList,
  DefaultScheduleExecutor,
  TypedFields,
  type Schedule,
  type ScheduleTickArgs,
} from '@nyx-discord/djs';
// ---cut---
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;

const errorHandler = BasicErrorHandler.createWithFallbackLogger<Schedule, ScheduleTickArgs>(
  (_error, _schedule, [metadata]) => TypedFields.Bot.get(metadata, true).getLogger(),
);

const executor = new DefaultScheduleExecutor(
  ScheduleMiddlewareList.create(),
  errorHandler,
);

bot.getScheduleManager().setExecutor(executor);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import {
  BasicErrorHandler,
  ScheduleMiddlewareList,
  DefaultScheduleExecutor,
  TypedFields,
  type Schedule,
  type ScheduleTickArgs,
} from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
// ---cut---
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: NyxBot;

const errorHandler = BasicErrorHandler.createWithFallbackLogger<Schedule, ScheduleTickArgs>(
  (_error, _schedule, [metadata]) => TypedFields.Bot.get(metadata, true).getLogger(),
);

const executor = new DefaultScheduleExecutor(
  ScheduleMiddlewareList.create(),
  errorHandler,
);

bot.getScheduleManager().setExecutor(executor);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import {
  BasicErrorHandler,
  ScheduleMiddlewareList,
  DefaultScheduleExecutor,
  TypedFields,
  type Schedule,
  type ScheduleTickArgs,
} from '@nyx-discord/http';
// ---cut---
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: NyxBot;

const errorHandler = BasicErrorHandler.createWithFallbackLogger<Schedule, ScheduleTickArgs>(
  (_error, _schedule, [metadata]) => TypedFields.Bot.get(metadata, true).getLogger(),
);

const executor = new DefaultScheduleExecutor(
  ScheduleMiddlewareList.create(),
  errorHandler,
);

bot.getScheduleManager().setExecutor(executor);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Callout type="warn" title="Using the Bot's logger">
To use the bot logger as fallback, create a handler with `createWithFallbackLogger` and inject it:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>

```ts twoslash
  (_error, _schedule, [metadata]) => TypedFields.Bot.get(metadata, true).getLogger(),

  ScheduleMiddlewareList.create(),
  errorHandler,
);
```
  </Tab>

# Middleware List (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/extend/schedules/schedule-executor/schedule-middleware-list)

The `ScheduleMiddlewareList` manages the middlewares that run before a schedule `tick()` is executed. It lives inside the [`ScheduleExecutor`](/extend/schedules/schedule-executor) and is used by it.

## Middleware Execution [#middleware-execution]

Middlewares are executed sequentially. If any middleware throws an error or returns without calling `next()`, the schedule execution is aborted and the executor forwards the error to its configured handler.

The `ScheduleFilterCheckMiddleware` is a built-in middleware that runs first by default (or as configured) to check if the schedule's `filter` method allows execution.

## When to override [#when-to-override]

| ✅ Override if you want to... | ❌ Don't override if you want to... |
|---|---|
| Customize how middlewares are stored or iterated. | Add middlewares to the existing list. Use a custom `ScheduleExecutor` if you only need different injections. |
| Add priority/group ordering semantics beyond simple insertion order. | Change error handling around `tick()` execution. That belongs to `ScheduleErrorHandler`. |
| Enforce middleware deduplication or identity-based replacement rules. | Change when schedules are triggered. That belongs to `ScheduleExecutionScheduler`. |

## Overriding [#overriding]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation]

Create a custom `ScheduleMiddlewareList` by either:

* Extending `ScheduleMiddlewareList` (recommended, less work).
* Implementing `MiddlewareList<ScheduleMiddlewareResolvable>`.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { ScheduleMiddlewareList } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyMiddlewareList extends ScheduleMiddlewareList {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { ScheduleMiddlewareList } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyMiddlewareList extends ScheduleMiddlewareList {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { ScheduleMiddlewareList } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyMiddlewareList extends ScheduleMiddlewareList {}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Registration [#registration]

Inject it into a custom `DefaultScheduleExecutor`, then set that executor to the [`ScheduleManager`](/extend/schedules/schedule-manager).

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler, DefaultScheduleExecutor, ScheduleMiddlewareList, TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyMiddlewareList extends ScheduleMiddlewareList {}
// ---cut---
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;

const executor = new DefaultScheduleExecutor(
  MyMiddlewareList.create(),
  BasicErrorHandler.createWithFallbackLogger((_error, _schedule, [metadata]) =>
    TypedFields.Bot.get(metadata, true).getLogger(),
  ),
);

bot.getScheduleManager().setExecutor(executor);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash

// ---cut---

  MyMiddlewareList.create(),
  BasicErrorHandler.createWithFallbackLogger((_error, _schedule, [metadata]) =>
    TypedFields.Bot.get(metadata, true).getLogger(),
  ),
);

bot.getScheduleManager().setExecutor(executor);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash

```
  </Tab>

</Step>
