  </Tab>
</Tabs>

For a more type-safe approach, you can use `TypedFields`. Check the [Metadata](/use/other/metadata) page for more information.


# Stage Pagination Session (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/session/types/stage-pagination-session)

<Callout type="warn">It's recommended to read the [Pagination Session](./pagination-session) page first, all of its features apply to this.</Callout>

A `StagePaginationSession` is a special type of pagination session made to paginate a list of stages.

## Stages [#stages]

A stage is an object inside a `StagePaginationSession` that represents a single page in the pagination. You can view them as a "nested" session.

Switching from one stage to another is the equivalent of switching pages on a pagination component.

A stage can:
* Be updated, similar to a `Session` update.
* Be switched to and reply to the interaction switching to it.
* Be left and perform some cleanup logic.
* Return a result, similar to a `Session` result.

The first stage is a `SessionStartStage`. It behaves exactly the same as any other, except it also has a `SessionStartStage#onStart()` method.

## Pagination [#pagination]

The pagination works in a similar way as in the `PaginationSession`. In essence:

- A customId not referring to a page is handled by `#update()` of the current stage.
- A customId referring to a page makes the session switch to that stage, calling `SessionStage#onSwitch()` on the new one and `SessionStage#onLeave()` on the old one.

## Creation [#creation]

There are three things you need to build to create a full `StagePaginationSession`:
1. The start stage
2. The stages (at least one)
3. The session

### Start stage creation [#start-stage-creation]

You'll first need to build the first stage of the session, a `SessionStartStage`.

<Steps>
<Step>

#### Class creation [#class-creation]

Extend the `AbstractSessionStartStage` class:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSessionStartStage } from '@nyx-discord/plugin-sessions/djs';
import type { ActionRowBuilder, ButtonBuilder } from 'discord.js';

// ---cut-start---
class MySessionStartStage extends AbstractSessionStartStage {
  public async onStart() {}
  public async onSwitch() { return true; }
  public async onLeave() {}
  protected generateRow() { return null as unknown as ActionRowBuilder<ButtonBuilder>; }
}
// ---cut-end---
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSessionStartStage } from '@nyx-discord/plugin-sessions/djs-core';
import type { APIActionRowComponent, APIButtonComponent } from '@discordjs/core';

// ---cut-start---
class MySessionStartStage extends AbstractSessionStartStage {
  public async onStart() {}
  public async onSwitch() { return true; }
  public async onLeave() {}
  protected generateRow() { return null as unknown as APIActionRowComponent<APIButtonComponent>; }
}
// ---cut-end---
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSessionStartStage } from '@nyx-discord/plugin-sessions/djs-core';
import type { APIActionRowComponent, APIButtonComponent } from '@discordjs/core';

// ---cut-start---
class MySessionStartStage extends AbstractSessionStartStage {
  public async onStart() {}
  public async onSwitch() { return true; }
  public async onLeave() {}
  protected generateRow() { return null as unknown as APIActionRowComponent<APIButtonComponent>; }
}
// ---cut-end---
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>

#### Implementation [#implementation]

Implement:
- `onStart()`: Replies to the start interaction.
- `onSwitch()`: Replies to the interaction when the user switches to this stage.
- `onLeave()`: Performs some cleanup logic when the user leaves the stage.

<Callout type="warn">You should not reply to the `onLeave()` interaction, as this will be done by the next stage.</Callout>

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import {
  AbstractSessionStartStage,
  type DjsSessionStartInteraction,
  type DjsSessionUpdateInteraction
} from '@nyx-discord/plugin-sessions/djs';
import type { ActionRowBuilder, ButtonBuilder } from 'discord.js';

class MySessionStartStage extends AbstractSessionStartStage {
// ---cut-start---
  protected generateRow() { return null as unknown as ActionRowBuilder<ButtonBuilder>; }
// ---cut-end---
  // Example property, not required
  protected userOnStage = true;

  public async onStart(interaction: DjsSessionStartInteraction): Promise<void> {
    await interaction.reply('Welcome to the session!');
  }

  public async onSwitch(interaction: DjsSessionUpdateInteraction): Promise<boolean> {
    await interaction.reply('Welcome to this stage!');
    this.userOnStage = true;
    return true;
  }

  public async onLeave(interaction: DjsSessionUpdateInteraction): Promise<void> {
    this.userOnStage = false;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import {
  AbstractSessionStartStage,
  type CoreSessionStartInteraction,
  type CoreSessionUpdateInteraction
} from '@nyx-discord/plugin-sessions/djs-core';
import type { APIActionRowComponent, APIButtonComponent } from '@discordjs/core';

class MySessionStartStage extends AbstractSessionStartStage {
// ---cut-start---
  protected generateRow() { return null as unknown as APIActionRowComponent<APIButtonComponent>; }
// ---cut-end---
  // Example property, not required
  protected userOnStage = true;

  public async onStart(interaction: CoreSessionStartInteraction): Promise<void> {
    await interaction.api.interactions.reply(
      interaction.data.id,
      interaction.data.token,
      { content: 'Welcome to the session!' }
    );
  }

  public async onSwitch(interaction: CoreSessionUpdateInteraction): Promise<boolean> {
    await interaction.api.interactions.reply(
      interaction.data.id,
      interaction.data.token,
      { content: 'Welcome to this stage!' }
    );
    this.userOnStage = true;
    return true;
  }

  public async onLeave(interaction: CoreSessionUpdateInteraction): Promise<void> {
    this.userOnStage = false;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

The type argument is the [return type](#stage-result) of your stage, which will be explained later.

</Step>

### Stages creation [#stages-creation]

After the first stage, you can create as many stages as you want.

<Steps>
<Step>

#### Class creation [#class-creation-1]

Extend the `AbstractSessionStage` class:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSessionStage } from '@nyx-discord/plugin-sessions/djs';
import type { ActionRowBuilder, ButtonBuilder } from 'discord.js';

// ---cut-start---
class MySessionStage extends AbstractSessionStage {
  public async onStart() {}
  public async onSwitch() { return true; }
  public async onLeave() {}
  protected generateRow() { return null as unknown as ActionRowBuilder<ButtonBuilder>; }
}
// ---cut-end---
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>

#### Implementation [#implementation-1]

Implement:
- `onSwitch()`: Replies to the interaction when the user switches to this stage.
- `onLeave()`: Performs some cleanup logic when the user leaves the stage.

<Callout type="warn">You should not reply to the `onLeave()` interaction, as this will be done by the next stage.</Callout>

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash

  }
```

### Session creation [#session-creation]

After all stages are created, you can create the session.

<Steps>
<Step>

#### Class creation [#class-creation-2]

Extend the `AbstractStagePaginationSession` class:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { DjsInteractionTypes } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import { AbstractStagePaginationSession, AbstractSessionStartStage, type SessionStageArray } from '@nyx-discord/plugin-sessions/djs';
import type { ActionRowBuilder, ButtonBuilder } from 'discord.js';

// ---cut-start---
class MySessionStartStage extends AbstractSessionStartStage<void> {
  public async onStart() {}
  public async onSwitch() { return true; }
  public async onLeave() {}
  protected generateRow() { return null as unknown as ActionRowBuilder<ButtonBuilder>; }
}
class MyStagePaginationSession extends AbstractStagePaginationSession<void> {
  protected readonly stages: SessionStageArray<DjsInteractionTypes> = [new MySessionStartStage(this)];
  public async onEnd() {}
}
// ---cut-end---
```
  </Tab>

#### Implementation [#implementation-2]

Implement `onEnd()` and `stages`:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { DjsInteractionTypes } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import { AbstractStagePaginationSession, type SessionStageArray } from '@nyx-discord/plugin-sessions/djs';
import type { ActionRowBuilder, ButtonBuilder } from 'discord.js';

// ---cut-start---
import { AbstractSessionStartStage, AbstractSessionStage } from '@nyx-discord/plugin-sessions/djs';
class MySessionStartStage extends AbstractSessionStartStage<void> {
  public async onStart() {}
  public async onSwitch() { return true; }
  public async onLeave() {}
  protected generateRow() { return null as unknown as ActionRowBuilder<ButtonBuilder>; }
}
class MySessionStage extends AbstractSessionStage<void> {
  public async onStart() {}
  public async onSwitch() { return true; }
  public async onLeave() {}
  protected generateRow() { return null as unknown as ActionRowBuilder<ButtonBuilder>; }
}
// ---cut-end---
class MyStagePaginationSession extends AbstractStagePaginationSession<void> {
  protected readonly stages: SessionStageArray<DjsInteractionTypes> = [
    new MySessionStartStage(this),
    new MySessionStage(this)
  ];

  public async onEnd(): Promise<void> {
    await this.startInteraction.editReply('Session ended!');
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { CoreInteractionTypes } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

    new MySessionStartStage(this),
    new MySessionStage(this)

    await this.startInteraction.api.interactions.editReply(
      this.startInteraction.data.application_id,
```

#### Initialization [#initialization]

Instantiate and start your session the same way as a regular one:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import type { DjsInteractionTypes, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import { AbstractStagePaginationSession, AbstractSessionStartStage, type DjsSessionStartInteraction, type SessionStageArray } from '@nyx-discord/plugin-sessions/djs';
import type { ActionRowBuilder, ButtonBuilder } from 'discord.js';

class MySessionStartStage extends AbstractSessionStartStage<void> {
  public async onStart() {}
  public async onSwitch() { return true; }
  public async onLeave() {}
  protected generateRow() { return null as unknown as ActionRowBuilder<ButtonBuilder>; }
}

class MyStagePaginationSession extends AbstractStagePaginationSession<void> {
  protected readonly stages: SessionStageArray<DjsInteractionTypes> = [new MySessionStartStage(this)];
  public async onEnd() {}
}

declare const startInteraction: DjsSessionStartInteraction;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
declare const id: string;
// ---cut-end---
const session = new MyStagePaginationSession({ bot, startInteraction, id });
await session.start();
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>

# Overview (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/typed-options)

The [`@nyx-discord/typed-options`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nyx-discord/typed-options) package types
the options of your slash commands from the command data itself, so a misspelled name, a wrong option kind or
a missing `null` check becomes a compile error.

Without it, `interaction.options.getString('reason')` accepts any name, ignores `required` and `choices`, and returns
`string | null` even for options Discord always sends. With it, the getters are checked against the data you already write.

<Callout>
  It doesn't depend on the rest of nyx: it only needs `discord-api-types`. You can use it in any bot that uses discord.js, `@discordjs/core` or raw API payloads, with or without nyx.
</Callout>

## Installation [#installation]

<Steps>
<Step>

### Installing [#installing]

```npm
npm i @nyx-discord/typed-options
```

It has `discord-api-types` as a peer dependency, and `discord.js` as an optional one for the `/djs` entry point.

</Step>
<Step>

### Defining the command [#defining-the-command]

Create the command data with `chatInput()` and one helper per option kind. The result is plain API JSON, so you register it with any library, or use it as the `data` of a nyx command:

```ts twoslash
import { chatInput, string, user } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options';

const data = chatInput({
  name: 'ban',
  description: 'Ban a member',
  options: {
    target: user({ description: 'Who to ban', required: true }),
    reason: string({ description: 'Why' }),
  },
});
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Reading the options [#reading-the-options]

Pass the data and the interaction to `typedOptions()`. The entry point you import it from depends on your library:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', 'Raw API']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { ChatInputCommandInteraction } from 'discord.js';
import { chatInput, string, user } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options';
declare const interaction: ChatInputCommandInteraction;

const data = chatInput({
  name: 'ban',
  description: 'Ban a member',
  options: {
    target: user({ description: 'Who to ban', required: true }),
    reason: string({ description: 'Why' }),
  },
});
// ---cut---
import { typedOptions } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options/djs';

const options = typedOptions(data, interaction);

const target = options.getUser('target');
//    ^?
const reason = options.getString('reason');
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction } from '@discordjs/core';
import { chatInput, string, user } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options';
declare const interaction: APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction;

const data = chatInput({
  name: 'ban',
  description: 'Ban a member',
  options: {
    target: user({ description: 'Who to ban', required: true }),
    reason: string({ description: 'Why' }),
  },
});
// ---cut---
import { typedOptions } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options/djs-core';

const options = typedOptions(data, interaction);

const target = options.getUser('target');
//    ^?
const reason = options.getString('reason');
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

A mistake in the name, or in the kind of option, doesn't compile:

```ts twoslash
import type { ChatInputCommandInteraction } from 'discord.js';
import { chatInput, string, user } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options';
import { typedOptions } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options/djs';
declare const interaction: ChatInputCommandInteraction;

const data = chatInput({
  name: 'ban',
  description: 'Ban a member',
  options: {
    target: user({ description: 'Who to ban', required: true }),
    reason: string({ description: 'Why' }),
  },
});
// ---cut---
const options = typedOptions(data, interaction);

// @errors: 2345
// Error! There is no option named "reasn"
options.getString('reasn');
// Error! "target" is a user option, not a string
options.getString('target');
```

</Step>
</Steps>

## Entry points [#entry-points]

| Entry point                           | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                  |
|---------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `@nyx-discord/typed-options`          | `chatInput()`, `subcommand()`, `group()`, the option helpers, and the types of the getters. Doesn't depend on any Discord library.                                       |
| `@nyx-discord/typed-options/djs`      | `typedOptions()` for discord.js. It returns `interaction.options` with narrower types, so it costs nothing at runtime.                                                    |
| `@nyx-discord/typed-options/djs-core` | `typedOptions()` for raw API payloads. It takes the `@discordjs/core` event props or a bare interaction payload, so it also covers the HTTP transport and other libraries. |

## Using it in a nyx command [#using-it-in-a-nyx-command]

Read the options from the command's own data:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', 'Raw API']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { ChatInputCommandInteraction } from 'discord.js';
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import { chatInput, string, user } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options';
import { typedOptions } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options/djs';

class BanCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  protected readonly data = chatInput({
    name: 'ban',
    description: 'Ban a member',
    options: {
      target: user({ description: 'Who to ban', required: true }),
      reason: string({ description: 'Why' }),
    },
  });

  public async execute(interaction: ChatInputCommandInteraction) {
    const options = typedOptions(this.data, interaction);
    await interaction.reply(`Banning ${options.getUser('target').username}`);
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction, ToEventProps } from '@discordjs/core';
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import { chatInput, string, user } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options';
import { typedOptions } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options/djs-core';

class BanCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  protected readonly data = chatInput({
    name: 'ban',
    description: 'Ban a member',
    options: {
      target: user({ description: 'Who to ban', required: true }),
      reason: string({ description: 'Why' }),
    },
  });

  public async execute(interaction: ToEventProps<APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction>) {
    const options = typedOptions(this.data, interaction);
    await interaction.api.interactions.reply(interaction.data.id, interaction.data.token, {
      content: `Banning ${options.getUser('target').username}`,
    });
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Callout>
  Builders like `SlashCommandBuilder` can't carry literal types, so they keep working but aren't typed. Use `chatInput()` for the commands whose options you want checked.
</Callout>


# Options (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/typed-options/options)

Each option is defined with a helper, under the name it will have in Discord. The helpers take the same fields as the [API](https://discord.com/developers/docs/interactions/application-commands#application-command-object-application-command-option-structure) (`description`, `required`, `choices`, `min_value`...), and `typedOptions()` gives you one getter per option kind.

| Helper          | Getter                                          | Returns                                |
|-----------------|-------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| `string()`      | `getString()`                                   | `string`                               |
| `integer()`     | `getInteger()`                                  | `number`                               |
| `number()`      | `getNumber()`                                   | `number`                               |
| `boolean()`     | `getBoolean()`                                  | `boolean`                              |
| `user()`        | `getUser()`, `getMember()`                      | The user, and the member               |
| `channel()`     | `getChannel()`                                  | The channel                            |
| `role()`        | `getRole()`                                     | The role                               |
| `mentionable()` | `getMentionable()`                              | A user, member or role                 |
| `attachment()`  | `getAttachment()`                               | The attachment                         |

Every getter only accepts the names of options of its own kind. What it returns is the same as in your library, so `getUser()` returns a `User` on discord.js and an `APIUser` with raw payloads.

## Required options [#required-options]

A getter returns `null` unless the option is `required: true`, in which case Discord always sends it and the type is not nullable:

```ts twoslash
import type { ChatInputCommandInteraction } from 'discord.js';
import { chatInput, string } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options';
import { typedOptions } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options/djs';
declare const interaction: ChatInputCommandInteraction;
// ---cut---
const data = chatInput({
  name: 'report',
  description: 'Report something',
  options: {
    title: string({ description: 'Title', required: true }),
    details: string({ description: 'Details' }),
  },
});

const options = typedOptions(data, interaction);

const title = options.getString('title');
//    ^?
const details = options.getString('details');
//    ^?
```

## Choices [#choices]

When an option has `choices`, the getter returns the union of their values:

```ts twoslash
import type { ChatInputCommandInteraction } from 'discord.js';
import { chatInput, integer, string } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options';
import { typedOptions } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options/djs';
declare const interaction: ChatInputCommandInteraction;
// ---cut---
const data = chatInput({
  name: 'ban',
  description: 'Ban a member',
  options: {
    mode: string({
      description: 'How',
      required: true,
      choices: [
        { name: 'Soft', value: 'soft' },
        { name: 'Hard', value: 'hard' },
      ],
    }),
    days: integer({
      description: 'Days of messages to delete',
      choices: [
        { name: 'None', value: 0 },
        { name: 'Week', value: 7 },
      ],
    }),
  },
});

const options = typedOptions(data, interaction);

const mode = options.getString('mode');
//    ^?
const days = options.getInteger('days');
//    ^?
```

## Users and members [#users-and-members]

A `user()` option resolves to a user, but the user might not be in the guild (or the command might run in a DM), so `getMember()` is **always** nullable, even for required options:

```ts twoslash
import type { ChatInputCommandInteraction } from 'discord.js';
import { chatInput, user } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options';
import { typedOptions } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options/djs';
declare const interaction: ChatInputCommandInteraction;
// ---cut---
const data = chatInput({
  name: 'kick',
  description: 'Kick a member',
  options: {
    target: user({ description: 'Who', required: true }),
  },
});

const options = typedOptions(data, interaction);

const target = options.getUser('target');
//    ^?
const member = options.getMember('target');
//    ^?
```

## Channels [#channels]

`channel_types` narrows the channel the getter returns:

```ts twoslash
import { ChannelType, type ChatInputCommandInteraction } from 'discord.js';
import { channel, chatInput } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options';
import { typedOptions } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options/djs';
declare const interaction: ChatInputCommandInteraction;
// ---cut---
const data = chatInput({
  name: 'log',
  description: 'Set the log channel',
  options: {
    target: channel({
      description: 'Where',
      required: true,
      channel_types: [ChannelType.GuildText],
    }),
  },
});

const options = typedOptions(data, interaction);

const target = options.getChannel('target');
//    ^?
```

## Mentionables [#mentionables]

`getMentionable()` returns the union of what a mentionable can be: a user, a member or a role. Use `getMember()` and `getRole()` for the other kinds' own options.

## Raw payloads [#raw-payloads]

With `@nyx-discord/typed-options/djs-core` there is no library to resolve the options for you, so `typedOptions()` reads them from the payload and looks up the users, members, channels, roles and attachments in `resolved` by their ID. Options missing from the payload are `null`:

```ts twoslash
import type { APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction } from '@discordjs/core';
import { chatInput, user } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options';
import { typedOptions } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options/djs-core';
declare const payload: APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction;
// ---cut---
const data = chatInput({
  name: 'kick',
  description: 'Kick a member',
  options: {
    target: user({ description: 'Who', required: true }),
  },
});

const options = typedOptions(data, payload);

const target = options.getUser('target');
//    ^?
```

It takes the interaction payload itself, or the `@discordjs/core` event props that wrap it as `data`, so it works the same for the gateway, for [HTTP bots](/use/http) and for any other library.


# Subcommands (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/typed-options/subcommands)

A command with subcommands has no options of its own, so `chatInput()` takes a list of `subcommands` instead. Create each one with `subcommand()`, and group them with `group()`:

```ts twoslash
import { chatInput, group, string, subcommand } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options';

const add = subcommand({
  name: 'add',
  description: 'Add a tag',
  options: {
    name: string({ description: 'The tag name', required: true }),
  },
});

const purge = subcommand({ name: 'purge', description: 'Delete every tag' });

const data = chatInput({
  name: 'tag',
  description: 'Manage tags',
  subcommands: [add, group({ name: 'admin', description: 'Admin tools', subcommands: [purge] })],
});
```

## Reading a subcommand's options [#reading-a-subcommands-options]

Subcommand and group names are typed as `string`, so which subcommand ran is not inferred from the interaction. Instead, pass **the subcommand's own data** to `typedOptions()` to type its options:

```ts twoslash
import type { ChatInputCommandInteraction } from 'discord.js';
import { string, subcommand } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options';
import { typedOptions } from '@nyx-discord/typed-options/djs';
declare const interaction: ChatInputCommandInteraction;
// ---cut---
const add = subcommand({
  name: 'add',
  description: 'Add a tag',
  options: {
    name: string({ description: 'The tag name', required: true }),
  },
});

const options = typedOptions(add, interaction);

const name = options.getString('name');
//    ^?
```

This fits nyx's [subcommands](/use/commands/types/parent/subcommand), which already live in their own class: define the subcommand's data there and read the options from it.

With raw payloads, `typedOptions()` finds the options inside the subcommand (and its group) for you.


# Components (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/commands/components)

You can make your components sent by your commands trigger a callback in the command itself, instead of having to listen to `interactionCreate` separately.

<Callout>
  This is only recommended for simple non complex components that originate directly from a command.
  For other cases, create an [`interactionCreate` subscriber](/use/events).
</Callout>

Given only these are executable, you can only use this in [Standalone Commands](./types/standalone), [SubCommands](./types/subcommand) and [Context Menu Commands](./types/context-menu).

## Usage [#usage]

In this example we'll use a standalone command, but the same applies to the rest.

<Steps>
<Step>

### Bot extraction [#bot-extraction]

You'll first need your bot instance, since it contains the codec used to de/serialize the customIds.

You can either instantiate your command with it, or get it from the execution metadata:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand, TypedFields, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { ChatInputCommandInteraction } from 'discord.js';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  public async execute(interaction: ChatInputCommandInteraction, meta: Metadata) {
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);
    //    ^?
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction, ToEventProps } from '@discordjs/core';
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand, TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  public async execute(interaction: ToEventProps<APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction>, meta: Metadata) {
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);
    //    ^?
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import type { APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction, ToEventProps } from '@discordjs/core';
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand, TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---

  public async execute(interaction: ToEventProps<APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction>, meta: Metadata) {
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);
    //    ^?
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

To learn more about TypedFields, check the [Metadata](../other/meta) page.

</Step>
<Step>

### Component creation [#component-creation]

Create your component the same way you'd normally do, but use the `bot` instance to create the customId:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { ButtonBuilder, ActionRowBuilder } from 'discord.js';
import type { ChatInputCommandInteraction } from 'discord.js';
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand, TypedFields, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  public async execute(interaction: ChatInputCommandInteraction, meta: Metadata) {
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);
    const customId = this.buildCustomId(bot); // [!code highlight]

    // Other properties omitted for brevity
    const button = new ButtonBuilder().setCustomId(customId);
    const row = new ActionRowBuilder<ButtonBuilder>().addComponents(button);

    await interaction.reply({ components: [row] });
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction, ToEventProps } from '@discordjs/core';
import { ComponentType, ButtonStyle } from '@discordjs/core';
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand, TypedFields, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  public async execute(interaction: ToEventProps<APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction>, meta: Metadata) {
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);
    const customId = this.buildCustomId(bot); // [!code highlight]

    await interaction.api.interactions.reply(
      interaction.data.id,
      interaction.data.token,
      {
        components: [{
          type: ComponentType.ActionRow,
          components: [{ type: ComponentType.Button, style: ButtonStyle.Success, custom_id: customId, label: 'Button' }]
        }]
      },
    );
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash

```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>

### Interaction handling [#interaction-handling]

When the component is clicked, the respective callback will be executed:

- `handleButton` for buttons
- `handleSelectMenu` for select menus
- `handleModal` for modals

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { ButtonInteraction } from 'discord.js';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  public async handleButton(interaction: ButtonInteraction) {
    await interaction.reply('You clicked the button!');
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { APIMessageComponentButtonInteraction, ToEventProps } from '@discordjs/core';
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  public async handleButton(interaction: ToEventProps<APIMessageComponentButtonInteraction>) {
    await interaction.api.interactions.reply(
      interaction.data.id,
      interaction.data.token,
      { content: 'You clicked the button!' },
    );
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash

    );
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
</Steps>

## Attaching extra data [#attaching-extra-data]

You can also attach an extra string to the customId, which will be sent back when the component is clicked. The `buildCustomId` method accepts an optional `data` parameter, which can be any string.

When the component is clicked, the metadata will contain the data you passed in the customId. It's cached there so you don't need to de-serialize it again.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand, TypedFields, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { ButtonInteraction, ChatInputCommandInteraction } from 'discord.js';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  public async execute(interaction: ChatInputCommandInteraction, meta: Metadata) {
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);
    const customId = this.buildCustomId(bot, 'my-data');
  }

  public async handleButton(interaction: ButtonInteraction, meta: Metadata) {
    const extra = TypedFields.CustomIdExtra.get(meta, true);
    await interaction.reply(extra) // Replies 'my-data'
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction, APIMessageComponentButtonInteraction, ToEventProps } from '@discordjs/core';
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand, TypedFields, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  public async execute(interaction: ToEventProps<APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction>, meta: Metadata) {
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);
    const customId = this.buildCustomId(bot, 'my-data');
  }

  public async handleButton(interaction: ToEventProps<APIMessageComponentButtonInteraction>, meta: Metadata) {
    const extra = TypedFields.CustomIdExtra.get(meta, true);
    await interaction.api.interactions.reply(
      interaction.data.id,
      interaction.data.token,
      { content: extra }, // Replies 'my-data'
    );
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import type { APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction, APIMessageComponentButtonInteraction, ToEventProps } from '@discordjs/core';

// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---

    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);
    const customId = this.buildCustomId(bot, 'my-data');
  }

  public async handleButton(interaction: ToEventProps<APIMessageComponentButtonInteraction>, meta: Metadata) {
    const extra = TypedFields.CustomIdExtra.get(meta, true);
    await interaction.api.interactions.reply(
      interaction.data.id,
      interaction.data.token,
      { content: extra }, // Replies 'my-data'
    );
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

### Complex data [#complex-data]

If you need to store a complex object as extra data you can consider using the [`@sapphire/string-store`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sapphire/string-store) package, which is what
the framework already uses for serialization to short strings:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand, TypedFields, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import { Schema, SchemaStore } from '@sapphire/string-store';
import { ButtonBuilder, ActionRowBuilder, type ButtonInteraction, type ChatInputCommandInteraction } from 'discord.js';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  protected static readonly Store = new SchemaStore()
    // Add an schema with a 'name' field stored as a string and an 'age' field stored as a int32:
    .add(new Schema(0).string('name').int32('age'));

  public async execute(interaction: ChatInputCommandInteraction, meta: Metadata) {
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);

    const extra = MyCommand.Store.serialize(0, { age: 25, name: 'amgelo563' }); // [!code highlight]
    const customId = this.buildCustomId(bot, extra);

    const button = new ButtonBuilder().setCustomId(customId);
    const row = new ActionRowBuilder<ButtonBuilder>().addComponents(button);
    await interaction.reply({ components: [row] });
  }

  protected async handleButton(interaction: ButtonInteraction, meta: Metadata) {
    // We can force the get here (`true`) since we know we passed an extra
    const extra = TypedFields.CustomIdExtra.get(meta, true);
    const deserialized = MyCommand.Store.deserialize(extra).data; // { age: 25, name: 'amgelo563' } // [!code highlight]

    await interaction.reply(`Name: ${deserialized.name}, Age: ${deserialized.age}`);
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction, APIMessageComponentButtonInteraction, ToEventProps } from '@discordjs/core';
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand, TypedFields, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import { Schema, SchemaStore } from '@sapphire/string-store';
import { ButtonBuilder, ActionRowBuilder } from '@discordjs/builders';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  protected static readonly Store = new SchemaStore()
    // Add an schema with a 'name' field stored as a string and an 'age' field stored as a int32:
    .add(new Schema(0).string('name').int32('age'));

  public async execute(interaction: ToEventProps<APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction>, meta: Metadata) {
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);

    const extra = MyCommand.Store.serialize(0, { age: 25, name: 'amgelo563' }); // [!code highlight]
    const customId = this.buildCustomId(bot, extra);

    const button = new ButtonBuilder().setCustomId(customId);
    const row = new ActionRowBuilder<ButtonBuilder>().addComponents(button);
    await interaction.api.interactions.reply(
      interaction.data.id,
      interaction.data.token,
      { components: [row.toJSON()] },
    );
  }

  protected async handleButton(interaction: ToEventProps<APIMessageComponentButtonInteraction>, meta: Metadata) {
    // We can force the get here (`true`) since we know we passed an extra
    const extra = TypedFields.CustomIdExtra.get(meta, true);
    const deserialized = MyCommand.Store.deserialize(extra).data; // { age: 25, name: 'amgelo563' } // [!code highlight]

    await interaction.api.interactions.reply(
      interaction.data.id,
      interaction.data.token,
      { content: `Name: ${deserialized.name}, Age: ${deserialized.age}` },
    );
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import type { APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction, APIMessageComponentButtonInteraction, ToEventProps } from '@discordjs/core';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---

  protected static readonly Store = new SchemaStore()
    // Add an schema with a 'name' field stored as a string and an 'age' field stored as a int32:
    .add(new Schema(0).string('name').int32('age'));

  public async execute(interaction: ToEventProps<APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction>, meta: Metadata) {
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);

    const extra = MyCommand.Store.serialize(0, { age: 25, name: 'amgelo563' }); // [!code highlight]
    const customId = this.buildCustomId(bot, extra);

    const button = new ButtonBuilder().setCustomId(customId);
    const row = new ActionRowBuilder<ButtonBuilder>().addComponents(button);
    await interaction.api.interactions.reply(
      interaction.data.id,
      interaction.data.token,
      { components: [row.toJSON()] },
    );
  }

  protected async handleButton(interaction: ToEventProps<APIMessageComponentButtonInteraction>, meta: Metadata) {
    // We can force the get here (`true`) since we know we passed an extra

    const deserialized = MyCommand.Store.deserialize(extra).data; // { age: 25, name: 'amgelo563' } // [!code highlight]

      interaction.data.id,
      interaction.data.token,
      { content: `Name: ${deserialized.name}, Age: ${deserialized.age}` },
    );

}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Check their documentation for more information and examples.

## Referring to other commands [#referring-to-other-commands]

You can also execute other commands callbacks by creating a customId that refers to them.

In order to do so, you'll need the command instance first. You can read how to obtain it in the [Command Location](./location) page.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { StandaloneCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const commandInstance: StandaloneCommand;
// ---cut-end---
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand, TypedFields, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { ChatInputCommandInteraction } from 'discord.js';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  public async execute(interaction: ChatInputCommandInteraction, meta: Metadata) {
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);

    /** Somehow get the command instance using one of the provided methods, eg: */
    const command = bot.getCommandManager().getRepository().getCommandByName('my-other-command');
    if (!command || command.isParent()) return;

    /** Then build the customId: */
    const customId = command.buildCustomId(bot);
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash

    /** Somehow get the command instance using one of the provided methods, eg: */
```

# Events (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/commands/events)

<Callout type="warn">It's recommended to read the [Events Overview](../events/index) and [Event Subscribers](../events/subscribers) pages first.</Callout>

The `CommandManager` has an `EventBus` that allows you to listen to events related to commands.

This is useful for monitoring, logging, or any other custom logic you want to execute when a command is executed.

## Events [#events]

The following events are available:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { CommandEventEnum } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// @noErrors
CommandEventEnum.
//               ^|
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { CommandEventEnum } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// @noErrors
CommandEventEnum.
//               ^|
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { CommandEventEnum } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// @noErrors
CommandEventEnum.
//               ^|
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Usage [#usage]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Subscriber creation [#subscriber-creation]

Create a subscriber that will listen to a given event, use the `CommandEventArgs` type for the arguments map. Check the [Event Subscribers](../events/subscribers) page for more information.

</Step>
<Step>
### Subscription [#subscription]

Subscribe to the event using the `CommandManager`'s `subscribe()` method.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { EventSubscriber, CommandEventArgs } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const subscriber: EventSubscriber<CommandEventArgs, keyof CommandEventArgs>;
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut-end---
await bot.getCommandManager().subscribe(subscriber);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { EventSubscriber, CommandEventArgs } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const subscriber: EventSubscriber<CommandEventArgs, keyof CommandEventArgs>;
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut-end---
await bot.getCommandManager().subscribe(subscriber);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:


  </Tab>
</Tabs>
</Step>
</Steps>


# Filters (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/commands/filters)

Filters restrict the execution of a given command. You may be familiar with them from other usages, like:
- A [cooldown filter](#cooldown-filter) that prevents a command from being executed too frequently
- A [permission filter](#permission-filter) that checks if a member has some required permissions.

They receive all the information about the command, the interaction that triggered it, and the execution metadata, and return a boolean indicating whether the command should be executed or not.

For more general information about filters, you must first read the general [Filters](/use/other/filters) guide.

Given only these are executable, you can only use this in [Standalone Commands](./types/standalone), [SubCommands](./types/subcommand) and [Context Menu Commands](./types/context-menu).

## Usage [#usage]

In this example we'll use a standalone command, but the same applies to the rest.

<Steps>
<Step>

### Creation [#creation]

<Callout type="warn" title="'Filter Denied' replies">
The command will simply not be called if the filter returns `false`, so if you want some kind of reply, you'll need to do it yourself in the filter.
</Callout>

Either:

- Create a class that extends `BaseCommandFilter` and implements the `check()` method.
 <Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BaseCommandFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { AnyExecutableCommand, CommandResolvableInteraction, DjsInteractionTypes, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyFilter extends BaseCommandFilter {
  public async check(
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    interaction: CommandResolvableInteraction<DjsInteractionTypes>,
    meta: Metadata
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    // Do some checks
    return true; // or false if the command should not be executed
  }
}
 ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BaseCommandFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { AnyExecutableCommand, CommandResolvableInteraction, CoreInteractionTypes, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyFilter extends BaseCommandFilter {
  public async check(
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    interaction: CommandResolvableInteraction<CoreInteractionTypes>,
    meta: Metadata
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    // Do some checks
    return true; // or false if the command should not be executed
  }
}
 ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash

 ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

- Create a function that returns a boolean or a Promise that resolves to a boolean.


</Step>

```ts twoslash
  protected override readonly filter = new MyFilter();
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Cooldown Filter [#cooldown-filter]

A simple cooldown filter that prevents a command from being executed too frequently, while also cleaning up expired cooldowns every minute:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BaseCommandFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { AnyExecutableCommand, CommandResolvableInteraction, DjsInteractionTypes, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class CooldownFilter extends BaseCommandFilter {
  protected readonly cooldowns = new Map<string, number>();

  protected readonly sweepInterval: NodeJS.Timeout;

  protected readonly timeout: number;

  constructor(timeout: number = 5000) {
    super();
    this.timeout = timeout;
    this.sweepInterval = setInterval(() => {
      const now = Date.now();
      for (const [userId, expiresAt] of this.cooldowns) {
        if (now >= expiresAt) {
          this.cooldowns.delete(userId);
        }
      }
    }, 60_000).unref();
  }

  public async check(
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    interaction: CommandResolvableInteraction<DjsInteractionTypes>,
    meta: Metadata
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    const userId = interaction.user.id;
    const now = Date.now();
    const cooldownUntil = this.cooldowns.get(userId) ?? 0;

    if (now < cooldownUntil) {
      // Ideally reply to the interaction, telling the user they are on cooldown
      return false;
    }

    this.cooldowns.set(userId, now + this.timeout);
    return true;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BaseCommandFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { AnyExecutableCommand, CommandResolvableInteraction, CoreInteractionTypes, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class CooldownFilter extends BaseCommandFilter {
  protected readonly cooldowns = new Map<string, number>();

  protected readonly sweepInterval: NodeJS.Timeout;

  protected readonly timeout: number;

  constructor(timeout: number = 5000) {
    super();
    this.timeout = timeout;
    this.sweepInterval = setInterval(() => {
      const now = Date.now();
      for (const [userId, expiresAt] of this.cooldowns) {
        if (now >= expiresAt) {
          this.cooldowns.delete(userId);
        }
      }
    }, 60_000).unref();
  }

  public async check(
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    interaction: CommandResolvableInteraction<CoreInteractionTypes>,
    meta: Metadata
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    const user = interaction.data.user ?? interaction.data.member?.user;
    const userId = user?.id ?? '';
    const now = Date.now();
    const cooldownUntil = this.cooldowns.get(userId) ?? 0;

    if (now < cooldownUntil) {
      // Ideally reply to the interaction, telling the user they are on cooldown
      return false;
    }

    this.cooldowns.set(userId, now + this.timeout);
    return true;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { BaseCommandFilter } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { AnyExecutableCommand, CommandResolvableInteraction, CoreInteractionTypes, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class CooldownFilter extends BaseCommandFilter {
  protected readonly cooldowns = new Map<string, number>();

  protected readonly sweepInterval: NodeJS.Timeout;

  protected readonly timeout: number;

  constructor(timeout: number = 5000) {
```
