```ts twoslash
    this.sweepInterval = setInterval(() => {
      const now = Date.now();
      for (const [userId, expiresAt] of this.cooldowns) {
        if (now >= expiresAt) {
          this.cooldowns.delete(userId);
        }
      }
    }, 60_000).unref();
  }

  public async check(
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    interaction: CommandResolvableInteraction<CoreInteractionTypes>,
    meta: Metadata
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    const user = interaction.data.user ?? interaction.data.member?.user;
    const userId = user?.id ?? '';
    const now = Date.now();
    const cooldownUntil = this.cooldowns.get(userId) ?? 0;

    if (now < cooldownUntil) {
      // Ideally reply to the interaction, telling the user they are on cooldown
      return false;
    }

    this.cooldowns.set(userId, now + this.timeout);
    return true;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

### Permission Filter [#permission-filter]

A permission filter that checks if a member has the required permissions to execute a command:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BaseCommandFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { AnyExecutableCommand, CommandResolvableInteraction, DjsInteractionTypes, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import { PermissionFlagsBits } from 'discord.js';

class PermissionFilter extends BaseCommandFilter {
  protected readonly requiredPermissions: bigint;

  constructor(requiredPermissions: bigint) {
    super();
    this.requiredPermissions = requiredPermissions;
  }

  public async check(
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    interaction: CommandResolvableInteraction<DjsInteractionTypes>,
    meta: Metadata
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    if (!interaction.member || !interaction.inCachedGuild()) {
      // This will depend on whether you want to allow outside of cached guilds or not
      return false;
    }

    if (!interaction.member.permissions.has(this.requiredPermissions)) {
      // Ideally reply to the interaction, telling the user they lack permissions
      return false;
    }

    return true;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BaseCommandFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { AnyExecutableCommand, CommandResolvableInteraction, CoreInteractionTypes, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import { PermissionFlagsBits } from 'discord.js';

class PermissionFilter extends BaseCommandFilter {
  protected readonly requiredPermissions: bigint;

  constructor(requiredPermissions: bigint) {
    super();
    this.requiredPermissions = requiredPermissions;
  }

  public async check(
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    interaction: CommandResolvableInteraction<CoreInteractionTypes>,
    meta: Metadata
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    const member = interaction.data.member;
    if (!member) {
      return false;
    }

    const permissions = BigInt(member.permissions);
    if ((permissions & this.requiredPermissions) !== this.requiredPermissions) {
      return false;
    }

    return true;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { BaseCommandFilter } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { AnyExecutableCommand, CommandResolvableInteraction, CoreInteractionTypes, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import { PermissionFlagsBits } from 'discord.js';

class PermissionFilter extends BaseCommandFilter {
  protected readonly requiredPermissions: bigint;

  constructor(requiredPermissions: bigint) {
    super();
    this.requiredPermissions = requiredPermissions;
  }

  public async check(
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    interaction: CommandResolvableInteraction<CoreInteractionTypes>,
    meta: Metadata
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    const member = interaction.data.member;
    if (!member) {
      return false;
    }

    const permissions = BigInt(member.permissions);
    if ((permissions & this.requiredPermissions) !== this.requiredPermissions) {
      return false;
    }

    return true;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>


# Commands Overview (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/commands)

Commands are how your bot responds to user interactions.

<Callout type="warn" title="About prefix/message content commands">
Nyx **only** supports application commands. It doesn't and won't support message content commands (like `!ping`).

If you really need such functionality, you can implement it yourself using the `messageCreate` event, but this isn't advised. Application commands improve DX and UX significantly, and don't require a privileged intent to work.
</Callout>

## Quick example [#quick-example]

Let's create a simple ping command:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { type NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
import { SlashCommandBuilder, type ChatInputCommandInteraction } from 'discord.js';
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class PingCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  protected readonly data = new SlashCommandBuilder()
    .setName('ping')
    .setDescription('Replies with Pong!')
    .toJSON();

  public async execute(interaction: ChatInputCommandInteraction) {
    await interaction.reply('Pong!');
  }
}

// Register the command
await bot.getCommandManager().addCommands(new PingCommand());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { type NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
import type { APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction, ToEventProps } from '@discordjs/core';
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class PingCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  protected readonly data = {
    name: 'ping',
    description: 'Replies with Pong!',
  };

  public async execute(interaction: ToEventProps<APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction>) {
    await interaction.api.interactions.reply(
      interaction.data.id,
      interaction.data.token,
      { content: 'Pong!' },
    );
  }
}

// Register the command
await bot.getCommandManager().addCommands(new PingCommand());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { type NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
import type { APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction, ToEventProps } from '@discordjs/core';
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class PingCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  protected readonly data = {
    name: 'ping',
    description: 'Replies with Pong!',
  };

  public async execute(interaction: ToEventProps<APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction>) {
    await interaction.api.interactions.reply(
      interaction.data.id,
      interaction.data.token,
      { content: 'Pong!' },
    );
  }
}

// Register the command
await bot.getCommandManager().addCommands(new PingCommand());
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

That's it! Your bot now has a `/ping` command that replies with "Pong!" when used.

The framework doesn't store any state in the instance, so you can reuse it across multiple bot instances without any problems.

## Command deployment [#command-deployment]

For commands to be deployed at Discord, you must either pass `deployCommands: true` when creating the bot, or deploy them manually.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { Client } from 'discord.js';
declare const client: Client<boolean>;
// ---cut---
import { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

const myBot = Bot.create((bot) => ({
  // ---cut-start---
  token: 'TOKEN', client: client, logger: console,
  // ---cut-end---
  // ... other options
  deployCommands: true,
}));
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { Client, GatewayIntentBits } from '@discordjs/core';
import { REST } from '@discordjs/rest';
import { WebSocketManager } from '@discordjs/ws';
const rest = new REST({ version: '10' }).setToken('TOKEN');
const gateway = new WebSocketManager({ token: 'TOKEN', intents: GatewayIntentBits.Guilds, rest });
const client = new Client({ rest, gateway });
// ---cut---
import { Bot, CoreNyxClient } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

const myBot = Bot.create((bot) => ({
  // ---cut-start---
  token: 'TOKEN', client: new CoreNyxClient(client, gateway, 'APPLICATION_ID'), logger: console,
  // ---cut-end---
  // ... other options
  deployCommands: true,
}));
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { HttpBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const myBot = HttpBot.create((bot) => ({
  // ---cut-start---
  applicationId: 'APPLICATION_ID', publicKey: 'PUBLIC_KEY', token: 'TOKEN', logger: console,
  // ---cut-end---
  // ... other options
  deployCommands: true,
}));
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Then, when starting the bot, it will automatically deploy them.

You can also deploy manually:

<Callout type="error">This will throw if you passed `deployCommands: true` or already called it before.</Callout>

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut---
await bot.getCommandManager().deploy();
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut---
await bot.getCommandManager().deploy();
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut---
await bot.getCommandManager().deploy();
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

### Add or deploy first? [#add-or-deploy-first]

If you add a command after commands have already been deployed, the framework will have to make an API call to register it.

This is not recommended due to ratelimits, so it's best to add all the commands *before* deploying (you can add commands before starting the bot).

## Command types [#command-types]

Commands are categorized into several types, depending on their purposes:

<Callout>Click on each card to learn more about that type.</Callout>

<Cards>
  <Card href="commands/types/standalone" title="Standalone Commands" icon={<CommandIcon />} external={false}>
    Slash commands with no children, like `/ping` or `/help`.
  </Card>
  <Card href="commands/types/parent" title="Parent Commands" icon={<FolderIcon />} external={false}>
    Slash commands that contain subcommands or subcommand groups, like `/user` with `/user info`.
  </Card>
  <Card href="commands/types/parent/subcommand" title="SubCommands" icon={<BabyIcon />} external={false}>
    Executable commands that live inside parents or subcommand groups, like `info` in a `/user` parent.
  </Card>
  <Card href="commands/types/parent/subcommand-group" title="SubCommand Groups" icon={<FoldersIcon />} external={false}>
    Non executable groups inside parent commands, like `settings` in a `/user settings view` command.
  </Card>
  <Card href="commands/types/context-menu" title="Context Menu Commands" icon={<PictureInPicture />} external={false}>
    Commands that appear when users right-click on messages or users.
  </Card>
</Cards>


# Location (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/commands/location)

Sometimes you may need a reference to a currently registered command. You can do so using the `CommandRepository` of your command manager.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut-end---
const repository = bot.getCommandManager().getRepository();
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
repository.locateBy
//                 ^|
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut-end---
const repository = bot.getCommandManager().getRepository();
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
repository.locateBy
//                 ^|
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut-end---
const repository = bot.getCommandManager().getRepository();
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
repository.locateBy
//                 ^|
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

### Location by name [#location-by-name]

Use the `locateByNameTree()` method to find a command by its name tree, which is a string representation of the command's hierarchy, e.g. `parent sub-command`.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { CommandRepository } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const repository: CommandRepository;
// ---cut-end---
const topLevel = repository.locateByNameTree('top-level-command');
//    ^?

const subCommandOrGroup = repository.locateByNameTree('parent', 'sub-command-or-group');
//    ^?

const subCommand = repository.locateByNameTree('parent', 'sub-command-group', 'sub-command');
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { CommandRepository } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const repository: CommandRepository;
// ---cut-end---
const topLevel = repository.locateByNameTree('top-level-command');
//    ^?

const subCommandOrGroup = repository.locateByNameTree('parent', 'sub-command-or-group');
//    ^?

const subCommand = repository.locateByNameTree('parent', 'sub-command-group', 'sub-command');
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { CommandRepository } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const repository: CommandRepository;
// ---cut-end---
const topLevel = repository.locateByNameTree('top-level-command');
//    ^?

const subCommandOrGroup = repository.locateByNameTree('parent', 'sub-command-or-group');
//    ^?

const subCommand = repository.locateByNameTree('parent', 'sub-command-group', 'sub-command');
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

This however only returns the generic base types, not a specific class instance. If you need a specific type, use the following method.

### Location by class [#location-by-class]

The `locateByClassTree()` method allows you to find a command by its class hierarchy, which is useful if you want to get a specific command type.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand, AbstractSubCommand, AbstractParentCommand, AbstractSubCommandGroup, CommandRepository } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
class MyStandaloneCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {}
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
class MySubCommand extends AbstractSubCommand {}
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
class MyParentCommand extends AbstractParentCommand {}
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
class MySubCommandGroup extends AbstractSubCommandGroup {}
declare const repository: CommandRepository;
// ---cut-end---
const standalone = repository.locateByClassTree(MyStandaloneCommand);
//    ^?

const subCommand = repository.locateByClassTree(MyParentCommand, MySubCommand);
//    ^?

const subCommandGroup = repository.locateByClassTree(MyParentCommand, MySubCommandGroup);
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand, AbstractSubCommand, AbstractParentCommand, AbstractSubCommandGroup, CommandRepository } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
class MyStandaloneCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {}
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
class MySubCommand extends AbstractSubCommand {}
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
class MyParentCommand extends AbstractParentCommand {}
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
class MySubCommandGroup extends AbstractSubCommandGroup {}
declare const repository: CommandRepository;
// ---cut-end---
const standalone = repository.locateByClassTree(MyStandaloneCommand);
//    ^?

const subCommand = repository.locateByClassTree(MyParentCommand, MySubCommand);
//    ^?

const subCommandGroup = repository.locateByClassTree(MyParentCommand, MySubCommandGroup);
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand, AbstractSubCommand, AbstractParentCommand, AbstractSubCommandGroup, CommandRepository } from '@nyx-discord/http';
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
class MyStandaloneCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {}
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
class MySubCommand extends AbstractSubCommand {}
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
class MyParentCommand extends AbstractParentCommand {}
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
class MySubCommandGroup extends AbstractSubCommandGroup {}
declare const repository: CommandRepository;
// ---cut-end---
const standalone = repository.locateByClassTree(MyStandaloneCommand);
//    ^?

const subCommand = repository.locateByClassTree(MyParentCommand, MySubCommand);
//    ^?

const subCommandGroup = repository.locateByClassTree(MyParentCommand, MySubCommandGroup);
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Notice how the return type of each call is the respective instance (or `null`), not the generic types.

## Getting commands [#getting-commands]

Alternatively, you can get all top level commands with the `getCommands()` method, which returns a `ReadonlyCollection` of them, keyed by name.

<Callout type="warn">This returns the local store, not a copy of it. Hence why it's typed as readonly. However, you may type assert and manipulate it, but it's not safe to do so.</Callout>

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { CommandRepository } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const repository: CommandRepository;
// ---cut-end---
const topLevels = repository.getCommands();
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { CommandRepository } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const repository: CommandRepository;
// ---cut-end---
const topLevels = repository.getCommands();
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { CommandRepository } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const repository: CommandRepository;
// ---cut-end---
const topLevels = repository.getCommands();
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>


# Middlewares (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/commands/middlewares)

Middlewares are objects or callbacks that run before any command is executed. They can do some pre-processing logic and store it in the metadata, or even prevent the command from being executed.

For general information about middlewares, you must first read the general [Middlewares](/use/other/middlewares) guide.

## Usage [#usage]

<Steps>
<Step>

### Creation [#creation]

Either:
- Create a class that extends `BaseCommandMiddleware` and implements the `check()` method.
<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BaseCommandMiddleware } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { AnyExecutableCommand, CommandResolvableInteraction, DjsInteractionTypes, Metadata, MiddlewareResponse } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyMiddleware extends BaseCommandMiddleware {
  public async check(
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    interaction: CommandResolvableInteraction<DjsInteractionTypes>,
    meta: Metadata
  ): Promise<MiddlewareResponse> {
    // Do some pre-processing logic
    return this.true();
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BaseCommandMiddleware } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { AnyExecutableCommand, CommandResolvableInteraction, CoreInteractionTypes, Metadata, MiddlewareResponse } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyMiddleware extends BaseCommandMiddleware {
  public async check(
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    interaction: CommandResolvableInteraction<CoreInteractionTypes>,
    meta: Metadata
  ): Promise<MiddlewareResponse> {
    // Do some pre-processing logic
    return this.true();
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { BaseCommandMiddleware } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { AnyExecutableCommand, CommandResolvableInteraction, CoreInteractionTypes, Metadata, MiddlewareResponse } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyMiddleware extends BaseCommandMiddleware {
  public async check(
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    interaction: CommandResolvableInteraction<CoreInteractionTypes>,
    meta: Metadata
  ): Promise<MiddlewareResponse> {
    // Do some pre-processing logic
    return this.true();
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

- Create a function that returns a `MiddlewareResponse`.
<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { type CommandMiddlewareResolvable, MiddlewareResponse } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

const myCallbackMiddleware: CommandMiddlewareResolvable = async (command, interaction, meta) => {
  // Do some pre-processing logic
  return {
    allowed: true,
    checkNext: true,
  };
};
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { type CommandMiddlewareResolvable, MiddlewareResponse } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

const myCallbackMiddleware: CommandMiddlewareResolvable = async (command, interaction, meta) => {
  // Do some pre-processing logic
  return {
    allowed: true,
    checkNext: true,
  };
};
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { type CommandMiddlewareResolvable, MiddlewareResponse } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const myCallbackMiddleware: CommandMiddlewareResolvable = async (command, interaction, meta) => {
  // Do some pre-processing logic
  return {
    allowed: true,
    checkNext: true,
  };
};
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>

### Registration [#registration]

Register it to the executor's `MiddlewareList`:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { NyxBot, BaseCommandMiddleware, CommandMiddlewareResolvable } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const MyMiddleware: new () => BaseCommandMiddleware;
declare const myCallbackMiddleware: CommandMiddlewareResolvable;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
bot.getCommandManager().getExecutor().getMiddleware().add(new MyMiddleware(), myCallbackMiddleware);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { NyxBot, BaseCommandMiddleware, CommandMiddlewareResolvable } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const MyMiddleware: new () => BaseCommandMiddleware;
declare const myCallbackMiddleware: CommandMiddlewareResolvable;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
bot.getCommandManager().getExecutor().getMiddleware().add(new MyMiddleware(), myCallbackMiddleware);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import type { NyxBot, BaseCommandMiddleware, CommandMiddlewareResolvable } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const MyMiddleware: new () => BaseCommandMiddleware;
declare const myCallbackMiddleware: CommandMiddlewareResolvable;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
bot.getCommandManager().getExecutor().getMiddleware().add(new MyMiddleware(), myCallbackMiddleware);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
</Steps>

## Examples [#examples]

### Logging middleware [#logging-middleware]

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BaseCommandMiddleware } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { AnyExecutableCommand, CommandResolvableInteraction, DjsInteractionTypes, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class LoggingMiddleware extends BaseCommandMiddleware {
  public async check(
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    interaction: CommandResolvableInteraction<DjsInteractionTypes>,
    meta: Metadata
  ) {
    console.log(`User ${interaction.user.tag} is executing command ${command.getData().name}`);
    return this.true();
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BaseCommandMiddleware } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { AnyExecutableCommand, CommandResolvableInteraction, CoreInteractionTypes, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class LoggingMiddleware extends BaseCommandMiddleware {
  public async check(
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    interaction: CommandResolvableInteraction<CoreInteractionTypes>,
    meta: Metadata
  ) {
    const user = interaction.data.user ?? interaction.data.member?.user;
    console.log(`User ${user?.username} is executing command ${command.getData().name}`);
    return this.true();
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { BaseCommandMiddleware } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { AnyExecutableCommand, CommandResolvableInteraction, CoreInteractionTypes, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class LoggingMiddleware extends BaseCommandMiddleware {
  public async check(
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    interaction: CommandResolvableInteraction<CoreInteractionTypes>,
    meta: Metadata
  ) {
    const user = interaction.data.user ?? interaction.data.member?.user;
    console.log(`User ${user?.username} is executing command ${command.getData().name}`);
    return this.true();
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>


# Context Menu Commands (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/commands/types/context-menu)

Context menu commands are commands executed on special menus. Currently Discord has two types of context menus:

* [Message Context Menus](https://discord.com/developers/docs/interactions/application-commands#message-commands), shown when right clicking on a message.
* [User Context Menus](https://discord.com/developers/docs/interactions/application-commands#user-commands), shown when right clicking on a user.

## Creation [#creation]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation-1]

Extend the `AbstractContextMenuCommand` class:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractContextMenuCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyContextMenuCommand extends AbstractContextMenuCommand {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractContextMenuCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyContextMenuCommand extends AbstractContextMenuCommand {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractContextMenuCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyContextMenuCommand extends AbstractContextMenuCommand {}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Implementation [#implementation]

Implement `data` that stores the command's data, and the respective `executeX()` method:

- `executeMessage()` for message context menus.
- `executeUser()` for user context menus.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { ApplicationCommandType, ContextMenuCommandBuilder, type MessageContextMenuCommandInteraction } from 'discord.js';
import { AbstractContextMenuCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyContextMenuCommand extends AbstractContextMenuCommand {
  protected readonly data = new ContextMenuCommandBuilder()
    .setName('My Context Menu')
    .setType(ApplicationCommandType.User) // or ApplicationCommandType.Message
    .toJSON();

  public async executeMessage(interaction: MessageContextMenuCommandInteraction) {
    await interaction.reply('Hello!');
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { ApplicationCommandType } from '@discordjs/core';
import type { APIMessageApplicationCommandInteraction, ToEventProps } from '@discordjs/core';
import { AbstractContextMenuCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyContextMenuCommand extends AbstractContextMenuCommand {
  protected readonly data = {
    name: 'My Context Menu',
    type: ApplicationCommandType.User, // or ApplicationCommandType.Message
  } as const;

  public async executeMessage(interaction: ToEventProps<APIMessageApplicationCommandInteraction>) {
    await interaction.api.interactions.reply(
      interaction.data.id,
      interaction.data.token,
      { content: 'Hello!' },
    );
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { ApplicationCommandType } from '@discordjs/core';
import type { APIMessageApplicationCommandInteraction, ToEventProps } from '@discordjs/core';
import { AbstractContextMenuCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyContextMenuCommand extends AbstractContextMenuCommand {
  protected readonly data = {
    name: 'My Context Menu',
    type: ApplicationCommandType.User, // or ApplicationCommandType.Message
  } as const;

  public async executeMessage(interaction: ToEventProps<APIMessageApplicationCommandInteraction>) {
    await interaction.api.interactions.reply(
      interaction.data.id,
      interaction.data.token,
      { content: 'Hello!' },
    );
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Registration [#registration]

Instantiate and register it to a bot's `CommandManager`.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { ContextMenuCommand, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const MyContextMenuCommand: new () => ContextMenuCommand;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
await bot.getCommandManager().addCommands(new MyContextMenuCommand());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { ContextMenuCommand, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const MyContextMenuCommand: new () => ContextMenuCommand;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
await bot.getCommandManager().addCommands(new MyContextMenuCommand());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import type { ContextMenuCommand, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const MyContextMenuCommand: new () => ContextMenuCommand;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
await bot.getCommandManager().addCommands(new MyContextMenuCommand());
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
</Steps>


## Guild deployment [#guild-deployment]

By default, all commands will be deployed in the global scope. If you want to deploy them in a specific guild, you can do so by implementing the `getGuilds()` method.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractContextMenuCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractContextMenuCommand {
  public getGuilds() {
    return ['GUILD_ID', 'ANOTHER_GUILD_ID'];
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractContextMenuCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractContextMenuCommand {
  public getGuilds() {
    return ['GUILD_ID', 'ANOTHER_GUILD_ID'];
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractContextMenuCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractContextMenuCommand {
  public getGuilds() {
    return ['GUILD_ID', 'ANOTHER_GUILD_ID'];
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Execution Meta [#execution-meta]

The second argument of the execute methods is a `Metadata` object, which is a `Record` that stores metadata about the command call.

Apart from the keys saved by the caller or the middleware, the dispatch meta contains:

* The execution ID, via the `TypedFields.Id` field.
* The execution start date, via the `TypedFields.CreationDate` field.
* The bot whose `Client` sent the interaction, via the `TypedFields.Bot` field.

To learn more about TypedFields, check the [Metadata](/use/other/meta) page.

## Metadata [#metadata]

When extending nyx with plugins, you may want to specify extra data for them. You can do so with the `Metadata` object, saved on the command.

<Callout>
While commands internally save a `Metadata`, the return type of `#getMeta()` is a `ReadonlyMetadata`,
meaning that external objects can read the object, but not modify it.
</Callout>

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractContextMenuCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractContextMenuCommand {
  protected override readonly meta = {
    someKey: 'someValue',
  };
}

const command = new MyCommand();
const meta = command.getMeta();
const value = meta['someKey']; // 'someValue'
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractContextMenuCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractContextMenuCommand {
  protected override readonly meta = {
    someKey: 'someValue',
  };
}

const command = new MyCommand();
const meta = command.getMeta();
const value = meta['someKey']; // 'someValue'
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractContextMenuCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractContextMenuCommand {
  protected override readonly meta = {
    someKey: 'someValue',
  };
}

const command = new MyCommand();
const meta = command.getMeta();
const value = meta['someKey']; // 'someValue'
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

For a more type-safe approach, you can use `TypedFields`. Check the [Metadata](/use/other/meta) page for more information.

## Advanced features [#advanced-features]

<Callout>Click on each card to learn more about that feature.</Callout>

<Cards>
  <Card title="Command components" icon={<MousePointerClickIcon />} href="../components">
    Handle components interactions directly in the subcommand that sent them, without a separate `interactionCreate` listener.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Filters" icon={<LockIcon />} href="../filters">
    Add pre-execution checks to your subcommand, like permissions or cooldowns.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Middlewares" icon={<LayersIcon />} href="../middlewares">
    Run code before every command's execution, like logging or pre-conditions.
  </Card>
</Cards>


# Parent Commands (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/commands/types/parent)

<Callout type="warn">It's recommended to read the [Commands Overview](../../index) page first.</Callout>

Parent commands are top-level, non executable commands that can have children, which can be either subcommands commands or subcommand groups.

## Creation [#creation]

<Steps>
<Step>

### Creation [#creation-1]

Extend the `AbstractParentCommand` class:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractParentCommand {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractParentCommand {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractParentCommand {}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>

### Implementation [#implementation]

Implement `data` that stores the command's data.

<Callout type= "warn">The `data` field must not contain any option, only the base values (name, description, etc). If they are included, they will be ignored.</Callout>

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { SlashCommandBuilder } from 'discord.js';
import { AbstractParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyCommand extends AbstractParentCommand {
  protected readonly data = new SlashCommandBuilder()
    .setName('my-command')
    .setDescription('My command')
    .toJSON();
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyCommand extends AbstractParentCommand {
  protected readonly data = {
    name: 'my-command',
    description: 'My command',
  };
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyCommand extends AbstractParentCommand {
  protected readonly data = {
    name: 'my-command',
    description: 'My command',
  };
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>

### Registration [#registration]

Instantiate and register it to a bot's `CommandManager`.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { ParentCommand, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const MyCommand: new () => ParentCommand;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
await bot.getCommandManager().addCommands(new MyCommand());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { ParentCommand, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const MyCommand: new () => ParentCommand;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
await bot.getCommandManager().addCommands(new MyCommand());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import type { ParentCommand, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const MyCommand: new () => ParentCommand;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
await bot.getCommandManager().addCommands(new MyCommand());
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
</Steps>

## Guild deployment [#guild-deployment]

By default, all commands will be deployed in the global scope. If you want to deploy them in a specific guild, you can do so by implementing the `getGuilds()` method.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractParentCommand {
  public getGuilds() {
    return ['GUILD_ID', 'ANOTHER_GUILD_ID'];
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractParentCommand {
  public getGuilds() {
    return ['GUILD_ID', 'ANOTHER_GUILD_ID'];
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractParentCommand {
  public getGuilds() {
    return ['GUILD_ID', 'ANOTHER_GUILD_ID'];
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

If you're ever overriding from another base command, you can return `null` to make it global again, this is the default implementation.

## Children management [#children-management]

Children aren't static: they can be added and removed in runtime.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { ParentCommand, SubCommand, SubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const parent: ParentCommand;
declare const subCommand: SubCommand;
declare const subCommandGroup: SubCommandGroup;
// ---cut-end---
parent.addChildren(subCommand, subCommandGroup);
parent.removeChildByInstance(subCommand);
parent.removeChildByName('sub-command-group-name');
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { ParentCommand, SubCommand, SubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const parent: ParentCommand;
declare const subCommand: SubCommand;
declare const subCommandGroup: SubCommandGroup;
// ---cut-end---
parent.addChildren(subCommand, subCommandGroup);
parent.removeChildByInstance(subCommand);
parent.removeChildByName('sub-command-group-name');
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { ParentCommand, SubCommand, SubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const parent: ParentCommand;
declare const subCommand: SubCommand;
declare const subCommandGroup: SubCommandGroup;
// ---cut-end---
parent.addChildren(subCommand, subCommandGroup);
parent.removeChildByInstance(subCommand);
parent.removeChildByName('sub-command-group-name');
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

However, for the changes to be reflected in Discord, you must edit the command afterwards:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import type { NyxBot, ParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
declare const parent: ParentCommand;
// ---cut-end---
await bot.getCommandManager().editCommands(parent);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import type { NyxBot, ParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
declare const parent: ParentCommand;
// ---cut-end---
await bot.getCommandManager().editCommands(parent);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import type { NyxBot, ParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
declare const parent: ParentCommand;
// ---cut-end---
await bot.getCommandManager().editCommands(parent);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

You can also query them by name, class or `Collection`:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { ParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const parent: ParentCommand;
// ---cut-end---
import { AbstractSubCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

const byName = parent.findChildByName('sub-command-name');
//    ^?

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubCommandClass extends AbstractSubCommand { /** */ }

const byClass = parent.findChildByClass(MySubCommandClass);
//    ^?

const allChildren = parent.getChildren();
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { ParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const parent: ParentCommand;
// ---cut-end---
import { AbstractSubCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

const byName = parent.findChildByName('sub-command-name');
//    ^?

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubCommandClass extends AbstractSubCommand { /** */ }

const byClass = parent.findChildByClass(MySubCommandClass);
//    ^?

const allChildren = parent.getChildren();
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { ParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const parent: ParentCommand;
// ---cut-end---
import { AbstractSubCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';

//    ^?

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---

const byClass = parent.findChildByClass(MySubCommandClass);
//    ^?

const allChildren = parent.getChildren();
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>


# SubCommand Groups (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/commands/types/parent/subcommand-group)

<Callout type="warn">It's recommended to read the [Commands Overview](../../index), [Parent Commands](./) and [SubCommands](./subcommand) pages first.</Callout>

Subcommand groups are non executable commands that have subcommand children. They are stored inside a [Parent Command](./).

While they don't depend on a specific bot, they do depend on their parent (a parent command).

## Creation [#creation]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation-1]
Extend the `AbstractSubCommandGroup` class:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubCommandGroup extends AbstractSubCommandGroup {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubCommandGroup extends AbstractSubCommandGroup {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/http';
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubCommandGroup extends AbstractSubCommandGroup {}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Implementation [#implementation]
Implement `data` that stores the command's data. The group's `children` collection is provided by the base class.
<Callout type="warn">The `data` field must not contain any option, only the base values (name, description, etc). If they are included, they will be ignored.</Callout>

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { SlashCommandSubcommandGroupBuilder } from 'discord.js';
import { AbstractSubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MySubCommandGroup extends AbstractSubCommandGroup {
  protected readonly data = new SlashCommandSubcommandGroupBuilder()
    .setName('my-group')
    .setDescription('My group')
    .toJSON();
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import { ApplicationCommandOptionType } from '@discordjs/core';

class MySubCommandGroup extends AbstractSubCommandGroup {
  protected readonly data = {
    name: 'my-group',
    description: 'My group',
    type: ApplicationCommandOptionType.SubcommandGroup as const,
  };
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import { ApplicationCommandOptionType } from '@discordjs/core';

class MySubCommandGroup extends AbstractSubCommandGroup {
  protected readonly data = {
    name: 'my-group',
    description: 'My group',
    type: ApplicationCommandOptionType.SubcommandGroup as const,
  };
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Addition to its parent [#addition-to-its-parent]

Instantiate and add it to a parent command.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import type { ParentCommand, SubCommandGroup, SubCommand, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const MySubCommandGroup: new (parent: ParentCommand) => SubCommandGroup;
declare const parent: ParentCommand;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut-end---
const subCommandGroup = new MySubCommandGroup(parent);
parent.addChildren(subCommandGroup);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import type { ParentCommand, SubCommandGroup, SubCommand, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const MySubCommandGroup: new (parent: ParentCommand) => SubCommandGroup;
declare const parent: ParentCommand;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut-end---
const subCommandGroup = new MySubCommandGroup(parent);
parent.addChildren(subCommandGroup);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import type { ParentCommand, SubCommandGroup, SubCommand, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const MySubCommandGroup: new (parent: ParentCommand) => SubCommandGroup;
declare const parent: ParentCommand;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut-end---
const subCommandGroup = new MySubCommandGroup(parent);
parent.addChildren(subCommandGroup);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Or do it in the parent's class:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractParentCommand, AbstractSubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import { SlashCommandBuilder } from 'discord.js';
// ---cut-start---
import type { ParentCommand, SubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const MySubCommandGroup: new (parent: ParentCommand) => SubCommandGroup;
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---

class MyCommand extends AbstractParentCommand {
  constructor() {
    super();
    this.addChildren(new MySubCommandGroup(this));
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractParentCommand, AbstractSubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import { SlashCommandBuilder } from 'discord.js';
// ---cut-start---
import type { ParentCommand, SubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const MySubCommandGroup: new (parent: ParentCommand) => SubCommandGroup;
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---

class MyCommand extends AbstractParentCommand {
  constructor() {
    super();
    this.addChildren(new MySubCommandGroup(this));
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractParentCommand, AbstractSubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import { SlashCommandBuilder } from 'discord.js';
// ---cut-start---
import type { ParentCommand, SubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const MySubCommandGroup: new (parent: ParentCommand) => SubCommandGroup;
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---

class MyCommand extends AbstractParentCommand {
  constructor() {
    super();
    this.addChildren(new MySubCommandGroup(this));
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Then it'll show up when the top-level parent command is registered.

</Step>
</Steps>

## Children management [#children-management]

Children aren't static: they can be added and removed in runtime.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { SubCommand, SubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const subCommand: SubCommand;
declare const subCommandGroup: SubCommandGroup;
// ---cut-end---
subCommandGroup.addChildren(subCommand);
subCommandGroup.removeChildByInstance(subCommand);
subCommandGroup.removeChildByName('sub-command-name');
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { SubCommand, SubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const subCommand: SubCommand;
declare const subCommandGroup: SubCommandGroup;
// ---cut-end---
subCommandGroup.addChildren(subCommand);
subCommandGroup.removeChildByInstance(subCommand);
subCommandGroup.removeChildByName('sub-command-name');
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { SubCommand, SubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/http';

declare const subCommandGroup: SubCommandGroup;
// ---cut-end---
subCommandGroup.addChildren(subCommand);
subCommandGroup.removeChildByInstance(subCommand);
subCommandGroup.removeChildByName('sub-command-name');
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

However, for the changes to be reflected in Discord, you must edit the **parent command** afterwards:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import type { NyxBot, ParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
declare const parentCommand: ParentCommand;
// ---cut-end---
await bot.getCommandManager().editCommands(parentCommand);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>

  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash

// ---cut-end---

```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

You can also query them by name, class or `Collection`:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>

```ts twoslash
//    ^?
```

## Metadata [#metadata]

When extending nyx with plugins, you may want to specify extra data for them. You can do so with the `Metadata` object, saved on the group.

<Callout>
While groups internally save a `Metadata`, the return type of `#getMeta()` is a `ReadonlyMetadata`,
meaning that external objects can read the object, but not modify it.
</Callout>

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// ---cut-start---
import { ParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const parent: ParentCommand;
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubCommandGroup extends AbstractSubCommandGroup {
  protected override readonly meta = {
    someKey: 'someValue',
  };
}

const group = new MySubCommandGroup(parent);
const meta = group.getMeta();
const value = meta['someKey']; // 'someValue'
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// ---cut-start---
import { ParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const parent: ParentCommand;
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubCommandGroup extends AbstractSubCommandGroup {
  protected override readonly meta = {
    someKey: 'someValue',
  };
}

const group = new MySubCommandGroup(parent);
const meta = group.getMeta();
const value = meta['someKey']; // 'someValue'
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// ---cut-start---
import { ParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const parent: ParentCommand;
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubCommandGroup extends AbstractSubCommandGroup {
  protected override readonly meta = {
    someKey: 'someValue',
  };
}

const group = new MySubCommandGroup(parent);
const meta = group.getMeta();
const value = meta['someKey']; // 'someValue'
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

For a more type-safe approach, you can use `TypedFields`. Check the [Metadata](/use/other/meta) page for more information.


# SubCommands (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/commands/types/parent/subcommand)

<Callout type="warn">It's recommended to read the [Commands Overview](../../index) and [Parent Commands](./) pages first.</Callout>

Subcommands are executable commands stored inside a [Parent Command](./) or a [SubCommand Group](./subcommand-group).

While they don't depend on a specific bot, they do depend on their parent (a parent command or a group).

## Creation [#creation]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation-1]
Extend the `AbstractSubCommand` class:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSubCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubCommand extends AbstractSubCommand {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSubCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubCommand extends AbstractSubCommand {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash

// ---cut-end---
```

  </Tab>

</Step>
<Step>
### Implementation [#implementation]
Implement `data` that stores the command's data, and `execute()` that executes the command.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { SlashCommandSubcommandBuilder, type ChatInputCommandInteraction } from 'discord.js';
import { AbstractSubCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MySubCommand extends AbstractSubCommand {
  protected readonly data = new SlashCommandSubcommandBuilder()
    .setName('my-command')
    .setDescription('My command')
    .toJSON();

  public async execute(interaction: ChatInputCommandInteraction) {
    await interaction.reply('Hello!');
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { type APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction, ApplicationCommandOptionType, type ToEventProps } from '@discordjs/core';
import { AbstractSubCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MySubCommand extends AbstractSubCommand {
  protected readonly data = {
    name: 'my-command',
    description: 'My command',
    type: ApplicationCommandOptionType.Subcommand,
  } as const;

  public async execute(interaction: ToEventProps<APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction>) {
    await interaction.api.interactions.reply(
      interaction.data.id,
      interaction.data.token,
      { content: 'Hello!' },
    );
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash

```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Addition to its parent [#addition-to-its-parent]
Instantiate and add it to a parent command or a subcommand group.
<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import type { ParentCommand, SubCommandGroup, SubCommand, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const MySubCommand: new (parent: ParentCommand | SubCommandGroup) => SubCommand;
declare const parent: ParentCommand | SubCommandGroup;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut-end---
const subCommand = new MySubCommand(parent);
parent.addChildren(subCommand);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import type { ParentCommand, SubCommandGroup, SubCommand, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const MySubCommand: new (parent: ParentCommand | SubCommandGroup) => SubCommand;
declare const parent: ParentCommand | SubCommandGroup;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut-end---
const subCommand = new MySubCommand(parent);
parent.addChildren(subCommand);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import type { ParentCommand, SubCommandGroup, SubCommand, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';

declare const parent: ParentCommand | SubCommandGroup;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut-end---
const subCommand = new MySubCommand(parent);
parent.addChildren(subCommand);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>
Or do it in the parent or group's class:
<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractParentCommand, AbstractSubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import { SlashCommandBuilder } from 'discord.js';

// ---cut-start---
import type { ParentCommand, SubCommand, SubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const MySubCommand: new (parent: ParentCommand | SubCommandGroup) => SubCommand;
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
// On a parent command:
class MyCommand extends AbstractParentCommand {
  constructor() {
    super();
    this.addChildren(new MySubCommand(this));
  }
}

// Or on a subcommand group:
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyGroup extends AbstractSubCommandGroup {
  constructor(parent: ParentCommand) {
    super(parent);
    this.addChildren(new MySubCommand(this));
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractParentCommand, AbstractSubCommandGroup } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// ---cut-start---

declare const MySubCommand: new (parent: ParentCommand | SubCommandGroup) => SubCommand;
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
// On a parent command:
class MyCommand extends AbstractParentCommand {
  constructor() {
    super();
    this.addChildren(new MySubCommand(this));
  }
}

// Or on a subcommand group:
// ---cut-start---

// ---cut-end---

  constructor(parent: ParentCommand) {
    super(parent);
    this.addChildren(new MySubCommand(this));
  }

```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Then it'll show up when the top-level parent command is registered.

</Step>
</Steps>

## Execution Meta [#execution-meta]

The second argument of the execute method is a `Metadata` object, which is a `Record` that stores metadata about the command call.

Apart from the keys saved by the caller or the middleware, the dispatch meta contains:

* The execution ID, via the `TypedFields.Id` field.
* The execution start date, via the `TypedFields.CreationDate` field.
* The bot whose `Client` sent the interaction, via the `TypedFields.Bot` field.

To learn more about TypedFields, check the [Metadata](/use/other/meta) page.

## Autocompletion [#autocompletion]

If your subcommand has autocompletable options, you can implement the `autocomplete()` method.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSubCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { AutocompleteInteraction } from 'discord.js';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubCommand extends AbstractSubCommand {
  public async autocomplete(interaction: AutocompleteInteraction) {
    await interaction.respond([
      { name: 'First option', value: 'first' },
      { name: 'Second option', value: 'second' },
    ]);
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSubCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { APIApplicationCommandAutocompleteInteraction, ToEventProps } from '@discordjs/core';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubCommand extends AbstractSubCommand {
  public async autocomplete(interaction: ToEventProps<APIApplicationCommandAutocompleteInteraction>) {
    await interaction.api.interactions.createAutocompleteResponse(
      interaction.data.id,
      interaction.data.token,
      {
        choices: [
          { name: 'First option', value: 'first' },
          { name: 'Second option', value: 'second' },
        ],
      },
    );
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSubCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { APIApplicationCommandAutocompleteInteraction, ToEventProps } from '@discordjs/core';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubCommand extends AbstractSubCommand {
  public async autocomplete(interaction: ToEventProps<APIApplicationCommandAutocompleteInteraction>) {
    await interaction.api.interactions.createAutocompleteResponse(
      interaction.data.id,
      interaction.data.token,
      {
        choices: [
          { name: 'First option', value: 'first' },
          { name: 'Second option', value: 'second' },
        ],
      },
    );
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Metadata [#metadata]

When extending nyx with plugins, you may want to specify extra data for them. You can do so with the `Metadata` object, saved on the subcommand.

<Callout>
While subcommands internally save a `Metadata`, the return type of `#getMeta()` is a `ReadonlyMetadata`,
meaning that external objects can read the object, but not modify it.
</Callout>

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSubCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// ---cut-start---
import { ParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const parent: ParentCommand;
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubCommand extends AbstractSubCommand {
  protected override readonly meta = {
    someKey: 'someValue',
  };
}

const subcommand = new MySubCommand(parent);
const meta = subcommand.getMeta();
const value = meta['someKey']; // 'someValue'
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSubCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// ---cut-start---
import { ParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const parent: ParentCommand;
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubCommand extends AbstractSubCommand {
  protected override readonly meta = {
    someKey: 'someValue',
  };
}

const subcommand = new MySubCommand(parent);
const meta = subcommand.getMeta();
const value = meta['someKey']; // 'someValue'
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSubCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// ---cut-start---
import { ParentCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const parent: ParentCommand;
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubCommand extends AbstractSubCommand {
  protected override readonly meta = {
    someKey: 'someValue',
  };
}

const subcommand = new MySubCommand(parent);
const meta = subcommand.getMeta();
const value = meta['someKey']; // 'someValue'
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

For a more type-safe approach, you can use `TypedFields`. Check the [Metadata](/use/other/meta) page for more information.

## Advanced features [#advanced-features]

<Callout>Click on each card to learn more about that feature.</Callout>

<Cards>
  <Card title="Command components" icon={<MousePointerClickIcon />} href="../../components">
    Handle components interactions directly in the subcommand that sent them, without a separate `interactionCreate` listener.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Filters" icon={<LockIcon />} href="../../filters">
    Add pre-execution checks to your subcommand, like permissions or cooldowns.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Middlewares" icon={<LayersIcon />} href="../../middlewares">
    Run code before every command's execution, like logging or pre-conditions.
  </Card>
</Cards>


# Standalone Commands (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/commands/types/standalone)

<Callout type="warn">It's recommended to read the [Commands Overview](../index) page first.</Callout>

Standalone commands are fully executable, top level commands that don't store any children. In Discord, they are
triggered on Slash Commands.

## Creation [#creation]

<Steps>
<Step>

### Creation [#creation-1]

Extend the `AbstractStandaloneCommand` class:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---

```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>

### Implementation [#implementation]

Implement `data` that stores the command's data, and `execute()` that executes the command.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash

    .setName('my-command')
    .setDescription('My command')
    .toJSON();

  public async execute(interaction: ChatInputCommandInteraction) {
    await interaction.reply('Hello!');
  }
```

  </Tab>

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>

### Registration [#registration]

Instantiate and register it to a bot's `CommandManager`.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { StandaloneCommand, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const MyCommand: new () => StandaloneCommand;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
await bot.getCommandManager().addCommands(new MyCommand());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>

  </Tab>

```ts twoslash

// ---cut---
await bot.getCommandManager().addCommands(new MyCommand());
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
</Steps>

## Guild deployment [#guild-deployment]

By default, all commands will be deployed in the global scope. If you want to deploy them in a specific guild, you can do so by implementing the `getGuilds()` method.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  public getGuilds() {
    return ['GUILD_ID', 'ANOTHER_GUILD_ID'];
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  public getGuilds() {
    return ['GUILD_ID', 'ANOTHER_GUILD_ID'];
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  public getGuilds() {
    return ['GUILD_ID', 'ANOTHER_GUILD_ID'];
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

If you're ever overriding from another base command, you can return `null` to make it global again, this is the default implementation.

## Execution Meta [#execution-meta]

The second argument of the execute method is a `Metadata` object, which is a `Record` that stores metadata about the command call.

Apart from the keys saved by the caller or the middleware, the dispatch meta contains:

* The execution ID, via the `TypedFields.Id` field.
* The execution start date, via the `TypedFields.CreationDate` field.
* The bot whose `Client` sent the interaction, via the `TypedFields.Bot` field.

To learn more about TypedFields, check the [Metadata](/use/other/meta) page.

## Metadata [#metadata]

<Callout>

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>

# Buses (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/events/buses)

Event buses are objects that store and notify their `EventSubscribers` when an event is called either internally, typically via an EventEmitter, or externally, via `EventBus#emit()`.

## Main features [#main-features]

An event bus can be un/subscribed to:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { EventBus, EventSubscriber } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
type EventArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<EventArgs>;
declare const subscriber: EventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'>;
// ---cut-end---
await bus.subscribe(subscriber);
await bus.unsubscribe(subscriber);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { EventBus, EventSubscriber } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
type EventArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<EventArgs>;
declare const subscriber: EventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'>;
// ---cut-end---
await bus.subscribe(subscriber);
await bus.unsubscribe(subscriber);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { EventBus, EventSubscriber } from '@nyx-discord/http';
type EventArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<EventArgs>;
declare const subscriber: EventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'>;
// ---cut-end---
await bus.subscribe(subscriber);
await bus.unsubscribe(subscriber);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Can be used to emit an event type-safely:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
// ---cut-end---
type EventArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};

declare const bus: EventBus<EventArgs>;

await bus.emit('someEvent', ['hello', 123]);
// @errors: 2322
// Error! Argument missmatch
await bus.emit('someEvent', [true, 123]);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
// ---cut-end---

};

await bus.emit('someEvent', ['hello', 123]);
// @errors: 2322
// Error! Argument missmatch
await bus.emit('someEvent', [true, 123]);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

It can be iterated and its subscribers can be obtained:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

  someEvent: [string, number];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<EventArgs>;
// ---cut-end---
const subscribers = bus.getSubscribers();
//    ^?

for (const [id, subscriber] of bus) {
  //            ^?
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>

  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

And other features you might find useful. Check the <DocsLink pkg="base" name="EventBus" /> for more details.

## Subscriber concurrency [#subscriber-concurrency]

An event bus has complete freedom over how to execute its subscribers, however the framework has normalized two patterns for ease of use (though it's not hardcoded):

### Async buses [#async-buses]

It calls its subscribers asynchronously, meaning that it doesn't wait for the current subscriber to finish before executing the next.

| Advantages                                                                                                                            | Disadvantages                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Can be faster, especially for events with many subscribers, since it executes them in bulk.                                           | Multiple subscribers running may hog the event loop and decrease performance.                                                                                                                         |
| Less prone to blocking or delaying the system, since it can move on to the next subscriber while the previous one is still executing. | May lead to calling subscribers in an order different than their priority. For example, subscribers with `PriorityEnum.Normal` may execute before subscribers with `PriorityEnum.High` have finished. |
|                                                                                                                                       | Since subscribers are executed in bulk, it can be harder to trace when an error occurs.                                                                                                          |

#### Concurrency Limit [#concurrency-limit]

To tackle the mentioned disadvantages, it has a concurrency limit functionality. This allows you to set how many subscribers are being checked or executed at the same time.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
type EventArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<EventArgs>;
// ---cut-end---
import { AsyncEventDispatcher } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

const dispatcher = bus.getDispatcher() as AsyncEventDispatcher;
dispatcher.setConcurrencyLimit(5);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
type EventArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<EventArgs>;
// ---cut-end---
import { AsyncEventDispatcher } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

const dispatcher = bus.getDispatcher() as AsyncEventDispatcher;
dispatcher.setConcurrencyLimit(5);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/http';
type EventArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<EventArgs>;
// ---cut-end---
import { AsyncEventDispatcher } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const dispatcher = bus.getDispatcher() as AsyncEventDispatcher;
dispatcher.setConcurrencyLimit(5);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Callout>
* Setting this limit to `1` effectively turns the dispatcher into a sync one.
* The default concurrency limit is `3`.
</Callout>

### Sync buses [#sync-buses]

It calls its subscribers synchronously, meaning that it waits for the current subscriber to finish before executing the next.

| Advantages                                                                   | Disadvantages                                                                                                                                          |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Ensures that subscribers are only executed in the order of their `Priority`. | May be slower for events with many subscribers, as it has to wait for each subscriber (and its middleware) to finish before moving on to the next one. |
| Easier to debug and to trace when and on which state an error occurs.        | If one subscriber takes a long time to execute, it can cause a delay for others.                                                                       |

#### Sync Timeout [#sync-timeout]

To tackle the mentioned disadvantages, it has a sync timeout functionality. This allows you to set "timeframe" for any subscriber to finish, before the dispatcher stops waiting and calls the next subscriber.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
type EventArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<EventArgs>;
// ---cut-end---
import { SyncEventDispatcher } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

const dispatcher = bus.getDispatcher() as SyncEventDispatcher;
dispatcher.setSyncTimeout(50_000);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
type EventArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<EventArgs>;
// ---cut-end---
import { SyncEventDispatcher } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

const dispatcher = bus.getDispatcher() as SyncEventDispatcher;
dispatcher.setSyncTimeout(50_000);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/http';
type EventArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<EventArgs>;
// ---cut-end---
import { SyncEventDispatcher } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const dispatcher = bus.getDispatcher() as SyncEventDispatcher;
dispatcher.setSyncTimeout(50_000);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>
<Callout>The default is of 10000 ms (10 seconds).</Callout>

## Known buses [#known-buses]

### Client bus [#client-bus]

The `Client` event bus is a built-in bus that wraps its events:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut-end---
const bus = bot.getClientEventBus();
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash

// ---cut-end---
```

  </Tab>
