<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { Bot, EventSubscriber } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import { Events, ClientEvents } from 'discord.js';
declare const bot: Bot;
declare const eventSubscriber: EventSubscriber<ClientEvents, 'interactionCreate'>;
// ---cut-end---
await bot.subscribeToClient(eventSubscriber);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>

### Manager buses [#manager-buses]

Each manager holds a bus that wraps events related to the feature they manage:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut-end---
const commandBus = bot.getCommandManager().getEventBus();
//    ^?

const scheduleBus = bot.getScheduleManager().getEventBus();
//    ^?

const pluginBus = bot.getPluginManager().getEventBus();
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>

## Custom buses [#custom-buses]

You can create your own event bus for your building an event-based bot.

<Steps>
<Step>
### Arguments type [#arguments-type]

You'll first need an arguments type for your events, for example:

```ts twoslash
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
  anotherEvent: [boolean];
};
```

This type's keys are the event names, and their values are the arguments of that event.

</Step>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation]

#### Manual emits [#manual-emits]

If you want a bus whose `emit()` method is manually called, either:

- Use `BasicEventBus.createSync()` to create a sync bus.
- Use `BasicEventBus.createAsync()` to create an async bus.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicEventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
// ---cut-start---
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
  anotherEvent: [boolean];
};
// ---cut-end---

const syncBus = BasicEventBus.createSync<MyEventsArgs>();
const asyncBus = BasicEventBus.createAsync<MyEventsArgs>();
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicEventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
// ---cut-start---
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
  anotherEvent: [boolean];
};
// ---cut-end---

const syncBus = BasicEventBus.createSync<MyEventsArgs>();
const asyncBus = BasicEventBus.createAsync<MyEventsArgs>();
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { BasicEventBus } from '@nyx-discord/http';
// ---cut-start---
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
  anotherEvent: [boolean];
};
// ---cut-end---

const syncBus = BasicEventBus.createSync<MyEventsArgs>();
const asyncBus = BasicEventBus.createAsync<MyEventsArgs>();
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

#### From an EventEmitter [#from-an-eventemitter]

You can also create a bus that will wrap an existent `EventEmitter`, or a class that extends it:

- Use `BasicEventBus.createSync()` to create a sync bus.
- Use `BasicEventBus.createAsync()` to create an async bus.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { EventEmitter } from 'node:events';
import { BasicEventEmitterBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
// ---cut-start---
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
  anotherEvent: [boolean];
};
// ---cut-end---

const emitter = new EventEmitter();
const syncBus = BasicEventEmitterBus.createSyncWithEmitter<MyEventsArgs, EventEmitter>(emitter);
const asyncBus = BasicEventEmitterBus.createAsyncWithEmitter<MyEventsArgs, EventEmitter>(emitter);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { EventEmitter } from 'node:events';
import { BasicEventEmitterBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
// ---cut-start---
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
  anotherEvent: [boolean];
};
// ---cut-end---

const emitter = new EventEmitter();
const syncBus = BasicEventEmitterBus.createSyncWithEmitter<MyEventsArgs, EventEmitter>(emitter);
const asyncBus = BasicEventEmitterBus.createAsyncWithEmitter<MyEventsArgs, EventEmitter>(emitter);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { EventEmitter } from 'node:events';
import { BasicEventEmitterBus } from '@nyx-discord/http';
// ---cut-start---
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
  anotherEvent: [boolean];
};
// ---cut-end---

const emitter = new EventEmitter();
const syncBus = BasicEventEmitterBus.createSyncWithEmitter<MyEventsArgs, EventEmitter>(emitter);
const asyncBus = BasicEventEmitterBus.createAsyncWithEmitter<MyEventsArgs, EventEmitter>(emitter);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
</Steps>

## Bus events [#bus-events]

Apart from the events specified in the type, the bus also emits extra events related to the bus itself:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { EventBusEventEnum } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
// @noErrors
EventBusEventEnum.
//                ^|
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { EventBusEventEnum } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
// @noErrors
EventBusEventEnum.
//                ^|
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { EventBusEventEnum } from '@nyx-discord/http';
// @noErrors
EventBusEventEnum.
//                ^|
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

You can subscribe to these events in any bus, like any other event they'd manage.


# Filters (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/events/filters)

Filters restrict the execution of a given subscriber. For example:
- A [bot filter](#bot-filter) that ignores events triggered by bots
- A [guild filter](#guild-filter) that restricts the execution to a specific guild.

They receive all the information about the subscriber, the event arguments that triggered it, and the execution metadata, and return a boolean indicating whether the subscriber should be executed or not.

For more general information about filters, you must first read the general [Filters](/use/other/filters) guide.

## Usage [#usage]

<Steps>
<Step>

### Creation [#creation]

Either:

- Create a class that extends `AbstractEventSubscriberFilter` and implements the `check()` method.
 <Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
// ---cut---
import { AbstractEventSubscriberFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { EventSubscriber, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyFilter extends AbstractEventSubscriberFilter<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  public async check(
    subscriber: EventSubscriber<MyEventsArgs>,
    meta: Metadata,
    ...args: MyEventsArgs['someEvent']
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    // Do some checks
    return true; // or false if the subscriber should not be executed
  }
}
 ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
// ---cut---
import { AbstractEventSubscriberFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { EventSubscriber, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyFilter extends AbstractEventSubscriberFilter<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  public async check(
    subscriber: EventSubscriber<MyEventsArgs>,
    meta: Metadata,
    ...args: MyEventsArgs['someEvent']
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    // Do some checks
    return true; // or false if the subscriber should not be executed
  }
}
 ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
// ---cut---
import { AbstractEventSubscriberFilter } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { EventSubscriber, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyFilter extends AbstractEventSubscriberFilter<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  public async check(
    subscriber: EventSubscriber<MyEventsArgs>,
    meta: Metadata,
    ...args: MyEventsArgs['someEvent']
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    // Do some checks
    return true; // or false if the subscriber should not be executed
  }
}
 ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

- Create a function that returns a boolean or a Promise that resolves to a boolean.
 <Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
// ---cut---
import { type EventSubscriberFilterResolvable } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

const myFilter: EventSubscriberFilterResolvable<
  MyEventsArgs,
  'someEvent'
> = async (subscriber, meta, ...args) => {
  // Do some checks
  return true; // or false if the subscriber should not be executed
};
 ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
// ---cut---
import { type EventSubscriberFilterResolvable } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

const myFilter: EventSubscriberFilterResolvable<
  MyEventsArgs,
  'someEvent'
> = async (subscriber, meta, ...args) => {
  // Do some checks
  return true; // or false if the subscriber should not be executed
};
 ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
// ---cut---

  MyEventsArgs,
  'someEvent'
> = async (subscriber, meta, ...args) => {
  // Do some checks
  return true; // or false if the subscriber should not be executed
};
 ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Callout title="Generic filter">
  You can also write a filter that will work regardless of the event being handled, by omitting the event name in the type arguments:

  <Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriberFilter, type EventSubscriberFilterResolvable, type Metadata, type EventSubscriber } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
// ---cut---
  type MyEventsArgs = {
    someEvent: [string, number];
    otherEvent: [boolean];
  };

// With a class:
  class MyFilter extends AbstractEventSubscriberFilter<MyEventsArgs> {
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
    public async check(
      subscriber: EventSubscriber<MyEventsArgs>,
      meta: Metadata,
      ...args: MyEventsArgs[keyof MyEventsArgs]
      // ^?
    ) { /** ... */ }
  }

// Or with a function:
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
  const myFilter: EventSubscriberFilterResolvable<MyEventsArgs> = async (
    subscriber,
    ...args
  //   ^?
  ) => { /** ... */ };
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>

  Notice how `args` accepts a union of the possible event arguments for any event in the `MyEventsArgs` type.
</Callout>

</Step>
<Step>

### Filter usage [#filter-usage]

Override the `filter` property in your subscriber:

- If you created a class, instantiate it:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriber } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// ---cut-start---
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
import { AbstractEventSubscriberFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
class MyFilter extends AbstractEventSubscriberFilter<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'> {}
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubscriber extends AbstractEventSubscriber<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected override readonly filter = new MyFilter();
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriber } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// ---cut-start---
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
import { AbstractEventSubscriberFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
class MyFilter extends AbstractEventSubscriberFilter<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'> {}
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubscriber extends AbstractEventSubscriber<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected override readonly filter = new MyFilter();
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriber } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// ---cut-start---

  someEvent: [string, number];

// ---cut-end---

```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

- If you created a function, assign it:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriber } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

  someEvent: [string, number];

// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySubscriber extends AbstractEventSubscriber<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected override readonly filter = myFilter;
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>

```ts twoslash
    // Do some checks
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Bot Filter [#bot-filter]

A simple filter that ignores events triggered by bots. This example assumes the event argument is a `Message`.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriberFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { EventSubscriber, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { Message, ClientEvents } from 'discord.js';

class BotFilter extends AbstractEventSubscriberFilter<ClientEvents, 'messageCreate'> {
  public async check(
    subscriber: EventSubscriber<ClientEvents, 'messageCreate'>,
    meta: Metadata,
    message: Message
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    return !message.author.bot;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriberFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { EventSubscriber, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { Message, ClientEvents } from 'discord.js';

class BotFilter extends AbstractEventSubscriberFilter<ClientEvents, 'messageCreate'> {
  public async check(
    subscriber: EventSubscriber<ClientEvents, 'messageCreate'>,
    meta: Metadata,
    message: Message
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    return !message.author.bot;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriberFilter } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { EventSubscriber, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { Message, ClientEvents } from 'discord.js';

class BotFilter extends AbstractEventSubscriberFilter<ClientEvents, 'messageCreate'> {
  public async check(
    subscriber: EventSubscriber<ClientEvents, 'messageCreate'>,
    meta: Metadata,
    message: Message
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    return !message.author.bot;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

### Guild Filter [#guild-filter]

A filter that restricts the execution to a specific guild. This example assumes the event argument has a `guildId` property (like an Interaction or Message).

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriberFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { EventSubscriber, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { ClientEvents } from 'discord.js';

class GuildFilter extends AbstractEventSubscriberFilter<ClientEvents, 'interactionCreate' | 'messageCreate'> {
  protected readonly guildId: string;

  constructor(guildId: string) {
    super();
    this.guildId = guildId;
  }

  public async check(
    subscriber: EventSubscriber<ClientEvents, 'interactionCreate' | 'messageCreate'>,
    meta: Metadata,
    object: { guildId: string | null }
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    return object.guildId === this.guildId;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriberFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { EventSubscriber, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { ClientEvents } from 'discord.js';

class GuildFilter extends AbstractEventSubscriberFilter<ClientEvents, 'interactionCreate' | 'messageCreate'> {
  protected readonly guildId: string;

  constructor(guildId: string) {
    super();
    this.guildId = guildId;
  }

  public async check(
    subscriber: EventSubscriber<ClientEvents, 'interactionCreate' | 'messageCreate'>,
    meta: Metadata,
    object: { guildId: string | null }
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    return object.guildId === this.guildId;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriberFilter } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { EventSubscriber, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { ClientEvents } from 'discord.js';

class GuildFilter extends AbstractEventSubscriberFilter<ClientEvents, 'interactionCreate' | 'messageCreate'> {
  protected readonly guildId: string;

  constructor(guildId: string) {
    super();
    this.guildId = guildId;
  }

  public async check(
    subscriber: EventSubscriber<ClientEvents, 'interactionCreate' | 'messageCreate'>,
    meta: Metadata,
    object: { guildId: string | null }
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    return object.guildId === this.guildId;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>


# Events Overview (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/events)

The event system in nyx is powered by [EventBuses](/use/events/buses). These are objects that store and notify their [EventSubscribers](/use/events/subscribers) when an event is called either internally or from another source.

You can see them as a more batteries-included way of handling events than using the native Node.js `EventEmitter`.

<Callout>
  HTTP bots (`@nyx-discord/http`) have no gateway connection, so their client only emits `InteractionCreate`, plus
  [webhook events](/use/http/webhook-events) if you set them up. Subscribers to other client events never fire.
</Callout>

## Quick example [#quick-example]

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractDJSClientSubscriber, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import { Events, type Interaction } from 'discord.js';

class InteractionCreateLogger extends AbstractDJSClientSubscriber<typeof Events.InteractionCreate> {
  protected readonly event = Events.InteractionCreate;

  public async handleEvent(meta: Metadata, interaction: Interaction) {
    console.log(`Interaction created: ${interaction.id}`);
  }
}

// ---cut-start---
import type { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut-end---
await bot.subscribeToClient(new InteractionCreateLogger());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractCoreClientSubscriber, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import { GatewayDispatchEvents, type ToEventProps, type APIInteraction } from '@discordjs/core';

class InteractionCreateLogger extends AbstractCoreClientSubscriber<GatewayDispatchEvents.InteractionCreate> {
  protected readonly event = GatewayDispatchEvents.InteractionCreate;

  public async handleEvent(meta: Metadata, payload: ToEventProps<APIInteraction>) {
    console.log(`Interaction created: ${payload.data.id}`);
  }
}

// ---cut-start---
import type { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut-end---
await bot.subscribeToClient(new InteractionCreateLogger());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractCoreClientSubscriber, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import { GatewayDispatchEvents, type ToEventProps, type APIInteraction } from '@discordjs/core';

class InteractionCreateLogger extends AbstractCoreClientSubscriber<GatewayDispatchEvents.InteractionCreate> {
  protected readonly event = GatewayDispatchEvents.InteractionCreate;

  public async handleEvent(meta: Metadata, payload: ToEventProps<APIInteraction>) {
    console.log(`Interaction created: ${payload.data.id}`);
  }
}

// ---cut-start---
import type { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut-end---
await bot.subscribeToClient(new InteractionCreateLogger());
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

That's it! Your bot will now log every interaction.

## Client Bus [#client-bus]

The client is wrapped under an event bus, which you can get:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut-end---
const bus = bot.getClientEventBus();
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut-end---
const bus = bot.getClientEventBus();
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: Bot;
// ---cut-end---
const bus = bot.getClientEventBus();
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

And you can directly subscribe to it:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { Bot, AbstractDJSClientSubscriber } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import { Events } from 'discord.js';
declare const bot: Bot;
class InteractionCreateLogger extends AbstractDJSClientSubscriber<typeof Events.InteractionCreate> {
  protected readonly event = Events.InteractionCreate;

  public async handleEvent() {}
}

// ---cut-end---
await bot.subscribeToClient(new InteractionCreateLogger());
// Equivalent to:
await bot.getClientEventBus().subscribe(new InteractionCreateLogger());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { Bot, AbstractCoreClientSubscriber } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import { GatewayDispatchEvents } from '@discordjs/core';
declare const bot: Bot;
class InteractionCreateLogger extends AbstractCoreClientSubscriber<GatewayDispatchEvents.InteractionCreate> {
  protected readonly event = GatewayDispatchEvents.InteractionCreate;

  public async handleEvent() {}
}

// ---cut-end---
await bot.subscribeToClient(new InteractionCreateLogger());
// Equivalent to:
await bot.getClientEventBus().subscribe(new InteractionCreateLogger());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---

  protected readonly event = GatewayDispatchEvents.InteractionCreate;

  public async handleEvent() {}

// Equivalent to:
await bot.getClientEventBus().subscribe(new InteractionCreateLogger());
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Custom buses [#custom-buses]

You can create and directly use any bus you want:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { BasicEventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
  anotherEvent: [boolean];
};
// ---cut-end---
const syncBus = BasicEventBus.createSync<MyEventsArgs>(); // Waits for its subscribers to finish, with a timeout
const asyncBus = BasicEventBus.createAsync<MyEventsArgs>(); // Executes a pool of subscribers at once
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { BasicEventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
  anotherEvent: [boolean];
};
// ---cut-end---
const syncBus = BasicEventBus.createSync<MyEventsArgs>(); // Waits for its subscribers to finish, with a timeout
const asyncBus = BasicEventBus.createAsync<MyEventsArgs>(); // Executes a pool of subscribers at once
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { BasicEventBus } from '@nyx-discord/http';
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
  anotherEvent: [boolean];
};
// ---cut-end---
const syncBus = BasicEventBus.createSync<MyEventsArgs>(); // Waits for its subscribers to finish, with a timeout
const asyncBus = BasicEventBus.createAsync<MyEventsArgs>(); // Executes a pool of subscribers at once
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

You can check more information about bus creation in the [Event Buses](/use/events/buses) page.

# Middlewares (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/events/middlewares)

Middlewares are objects or callbacks that run before any subscriber is executed. They can do some pre-processing logic and store it in the metadata, or even prevent the subscriber from being executed.

For general information about middlewares, you must first read the general [Middlewares](/use/other/middlewares) guide.

## Usage [#usage]

<Steps>
<Step>

### Creation [#creation]

Either:
- Create a class that extends `AbstractEventSubscriberMiddleware` and implements the `check()` method.
<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriberMiddleware } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { AnyEventSubscriber, Metadata, MiddlewareResponse } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyMiddleware extends AbstractEventSubscriberMiddleware {
  public async check(
    subscriber: AnyEventSubscriber,
    meta: Metadata
  ): Promise<MiddlewareResponse> {
    // Do some pre-processing logic
    return this.true();
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriberMiddleware } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { AnyEventSubscriber, Metadata, MiddlewareResponse } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyMiddleware extends AbstractEventSubscriberMiddleware {
  public async check(
    subscriber: AnyEventSubscriber,
    meta: Metadata
  ): Promise<MiddlewareResponse> {
    // Do some pre-processing logic
    return this.true();
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriberMiddleware } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { AnyEventSubscriber, Metadata, MiddlewareResponse } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyMiddleware extends AbstractEventSubscriberMiddleware {
  public async check(
    subscriber: AnyEventSubscriber,
    meta: Metadata
  ): Promise<MiddlewareResponse> {
    // Do some pre-processing logic
    return this.true();
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

- Create a function that returns a `MiddlewareResponse`.
<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { type EventSubscriberMiddlewareResolvable } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

const myCallbackMiddleware: EventSubscriberMiddlewareResolvable = async (subscriber, meta) => {
  // Do some pre-processing logic
  return {
    allowed: true,
    checkNext: true,
  };
};
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { type EventSubscriberMiddlewareResolvable } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

const myCallbackMiddleware: EventSubscriberMiddlewareResolvable = async (subscriber, meta) => {
  // Do some pre-processing logic
  return {
    allowed: true,
    checkNext: true,
  };
};
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { type EventSubscriberMiddlewareResolvable } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const myCallbackMiddleware: EventSubscriberMiddlewareResolvable = async (subscriber, meta) => {
  // Do some pre-processing logic
  return {
    allowed: true,
    checkNext: true,
  };
};
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>

### Registration [#registration]

Register it to the dispatcher's `MiddlewareList`:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { EventBus, AbstractEventSubscriberMiddleware, EventSubscriberMiddlewareResolvable } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const MyMiddleware: new () => AbstractEventSubscriberMiddleware;
declare const myCallbackMiddleware: EventSubscriberMiddlewareResolvable;
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
  anotherEvent: [boolean];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<MyEventsArgs>;
// ---cut---
bus.getDispatcher().getMiddleware().add(new MyMiddleware(), myCallbackMiddleware);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { EventBus, AbstractEventSubscriberMiddleware, EventSubscriberMiddlewareResolvable } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const MyMiddleware: new () => AbstractEventSubscriberMiddleware;
declare const myCallbackMiddleware: EventSubscriberMiddlewareResolvable;
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
  anotherEvent: [boolean];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<MyEventsArgs>;
// ---cut---
bus.getDispatcher().getMiddleware().add(new MyMiddleware(), myCallbackMiddleware);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import type { EventBus, AbstractEventSubscriberMiddleware, EventSubscriberMiddlewareResolvable } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const MyMiddleware: new () => AbstractEventSubscriberMiddleware;
declare const myCallbackMiddleware: EventSubscriberMiddlewareResolvable;
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
  anotherEvent: [boolean];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<MyEventsArgs>;
// ---cut---
bus.getDispatcher().getMiddleware().add(new MyMiddleware(), myCallbackMiddleware);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
</Steps>


# Subscribers (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/events/subscribers)

Subscribers are objects that are notified by an `EventBus` when an event they are subscribed to is emitted.

## Creation [#creation]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Creation [#creation-1]

<Callout>You'll first need a type for your events arguments, here we'll use `MyEventsArgs`.</Callout>

Either:

- Extend `AbstractEventSubscriber` class and implement `handleEvent()` and `event`:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriber, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};

class MySubscriber extends AbstractEventSubscriber<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected readonly event = 'someEvent';

  public async handleEvent(meta: Metadata, ...args: MyEventsArgs['someEvent']) {
    // Handle event
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriber, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};

class MySubscriber extends AbstractEventSubscriber<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected readonly event = 'someEvent';

  public async handleEvent(meta: Metadata, ...args: MyEventsArgs['someEvent']) {
    // Handle event
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriber, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/http';

type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};

class MySubscriber extends AbstractEventSubscriber<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected readonly event = 'someEvent';

  public async handleEvent(meta: Metadata, ...args: MyEventsArgs['someEvent']) {
    // Handle event
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

- Use `SubscriberCallbackWrapper` to create a subscriber from a generic callback:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { SubscriberCallbackWrapper, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};

export const mySubscriber = new SubscriberCallbackWrapper<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'>(
  'someEvent',
  (meta: Metadata, ...args: MyEventsArgs['someEvent']) => {
    // Handle event
  }
);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { SubscriberCallbackWrapper, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};

export const mySubscriber = new SubscriberCallbackWrapper<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'>(
  'someEvent',
  (meta: Metadata, ...args: MyEventsArgs['someEvent']) => {
    // Handle event
  }
);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { SubscriberCallbackWrapper, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/http';

type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};

export const mySubscriber = new SubscriberCallbackWrapper<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'>(
  'someEvent',
  (meta: Metadata, ...args: MyEventsArgs['someEvent']) => {
    // Handle event
  }
);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>
### Subscription [#subscription]

Register the subscriber to an `EventBus`:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import type { NyxBot, EventSubscriber, EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<MyEventsArgs>;
declare const mySubscriber: EventSubscriber<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'>;
// ---cut-end---
await bus.subscribe(mySubscriber);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import type { NyxBot, EventSubscriber, EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<MyEventsArgs>;
declare const mySubscriber: EventSubscriber<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'>;
// ---cut-end---
await bus.subscribe(mySubscriber);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import type { NyxBot, EventSubscriber, EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/http';
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<MyEventsArgs>;
declare const mySubscriber: EventSubscriber<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'>;
// ---cut-end---
await bus.subscribe(mySubscriber);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
</Steps>

<Callout>
  If you want to create a listener for the `Client` bus, you can extend the `AbstractDJSClientSubscriber` (or `AbstractCoreClientSubscriber` for `@discordjs/core`) utility class instead, and you won't have to type out the client's event map generic. Check the [Events Overview](./index) page for an example.
</Callout>

## Priorities [#priorities]

The priority determines the order in which they are executed:

- Higher priorities are executed first.
- Monitors are specifically meant for monitoring (e.g. metrics), though that's not enforced.
  - `HighMonitor` is the first priority to be executed.
  - `LowMonitor` is the last priority to be executed.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { PriorityEnum } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// @noErrors
PriorityEnum.
//           ^|
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { PriorityEnum } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// @noErrors
PriorityEnum.
//           ^|
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { PriorityEnum } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// @noErrors
PriorityEnum.
//           ^|
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The default priority is `Normal`, it's changed by overriding the `priority` property in classes. It can't be changed for callback-based subscribers.

## Subscription notification [#subscription-notification]

The subscriber will be notified when its un/subscribed to an `EventBus`, and when said bus is unregistered:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { EventBus, EventSubscriber, AbstractEventSubscriber, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
type EventArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<EventArgs>;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
declare const subscriber: EventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'>;
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class Subscriber extends AbstractEventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  public override onSubscribe(bus: EventBus<EventArgs>) {
    console.log('I was subscribed!');
  }

  public override onUnsubscribe(bus: EventBus<EventArgs>) {
    console.log('I was unsubscribed!');
  }

  public override onBusUnregister(bus: EventBus<EventArgs>) {
    console.log('My bus was unregistered!');
  }
}

await bus.subscribe(subscriber);
// console: I was subscribed!
await bus.unsubscribe(subscriber);
// console: I was unsubscribed!
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { EventBus, EventSubscriber, AbstractEventSubscriber, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
type EventArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];

    console.log('I was unsubscribed!');
  }

  public override onBusUnregister(bus: EventBus<EventArgs>) {
    console.log('My bus was unregistered!');
  }
}

await bus.subscribe(subscriber);
// console: I was subscribed!
await bus.unsubscribe(subscriber);
// console: I was unsubscribed!
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash

// console: I was unsubscribed!
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Event Meta [#event-meta]

The first argument of the `handleEvent()` is an `Metadata` object, which is a `Record` that stores metadata about the event call.

Apart from the keys saved by the caller or the middleware, the dispatch meta contains:

* The execution ID, via the `TypedFields.Id` field.
* The execution start date, via the `TypedFields.CreationDate` field.
* The bot that called the event, via the `TypedFields.Bot` field.
* The bus where the event was emitted, via the `TypedFields.EventBus` field.
* Whether the event has been marked as handled by another subscriber, via the `TypedFields.EventHandled` field, which will be explained later.

To learn more about TypedFields, check the [Metadata](/use/other/meta) page.

### Event handling [#event-handling]

By default, when a subscriber marks an event as "handled" with `this.setHandled(meta)`, it won't be received by the rest of the subscribers.

This is useful for events that only need to be "executed once", for example, replying to an `Interaction`.

However, you can make your subscriber to be always called, even when the event is handled, overriding the `ignoreHandled` property:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { AbstractEventSubscriber, PriorityEnum, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import { EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
type EventArgs = {
  someEvent: [];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<EventArgs>;
// ---cut-end---
// A subscriber with priority Highest marks the event as handled
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class Highest extends AbstractEventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected readonly priority = PriorityEnum.Highest;

  public handleEvent(meta: Metadata) {
    console.log('Highest');
    this.setHandled(meta);
  }
}

// A subscriber with priority Lowest doesn't receive the event
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class Lowest extends AbstractEventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected readonly priority = PriorityEnum.Lowest;

  public handleEvent() {
    console.log('Lowest');
  }
}

// A subscriber with priority Lowest but `ignoreHandled = false` receives the event
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class LowestNotIgnored extends AbstractEventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected readonly priority = PriorityEnum.Lowest;

  protected readonly ignoreHandled = false;

  public handleEvent() {
    console.log('Lowest with ignoreHandled = false');
  }
}

await bus.subscribe(new Lowest(), new Highest(), new LowestNotIgnored());
await bus.emit('someEvent', []);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { AbstractEventSubscriber, PriorityEnum, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import { EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
type EventArgs = {
  someEvent: [];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<EventArgs>;
// ---cut-end---
// A subscriber with priority Highest marks the event as handled
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class Highest extends AbstractEventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected readonly priority = PriorityEnum.Highest;

  public handleEvent(meta: Metadata) {
    console.log('Highest');
    this.setHandled(meta);
  }
}

// A subscriber with priority Lowest doesn't receive the event
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class Lowest extends AbstractEventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected readonly priority = PriorityEnum.Lowest;

  public handleEvent() {
    console.log('Lowest');
  }
}

// A subscriber with priority Lowest but `ignoreHandled = false` receives the event
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class LowestNotIgnored extends AbstractEventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected readonly priority = PriorityEnum.Lowest;

  protected readonly ignoreHandled = false;

  public handleEvent() {
    console.log('Lowest with ignoreHandled = false');
  }
}

await bus.subscribe(new Lowest(), new Highest(), new LowestNotIgnored());
await bus.emit('someEvent', []);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { AbstractEventSubscriber, PriorityEnum, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import { EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/http';
type EventArgs = {
  someEvent: [];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<EventArgs>;
// ---cut-end---
// A subscriber with priority Highest marks the event as handled
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class Highest extends AbstractEventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected readonly priority = PriorityEnum.Highest;

  public handleEvent(meta: Metadata) {
    console.log('Highest');
    this.setHandled(meta);
  }
}

// A subscriber with priority Lowest doesn't receive the event
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class Lowest extends AbstractEventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected readonly priority = PriorityEnum.Lowest;

  public handleEvent() {
    console.log('Lowest');
  }
}

// A subscriber with priority Lowest but `ignoreHandled = false` receives the event
// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class LowestNotIgnored extends AbstractEventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected readonly priority = PriorityEnum.Lowest;

  protected readonly ignoreHandled = false;

  public handleEvent() {
    console.log('Lowest with ignoreHandled = false');
  }
}

await bus.subscribe(new Lowest(), new Highest(), new LowestNotIgnored());
await bus.emit('someEvent', []);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Would log:
```
Highest
Lowest with ignoreHandled = false
```

Notice how the `Lowest` subscriber is not called, because it has a lower priority than the `Highest` one, which marked the event as handled, and it has `ignoreHandled = true` by default.

## Lifetime [#lifetime]

Subscribers can specify its "lifetime", which determines how much it lasts registered on the bus. This is similar to using Node's `EventEmitter#on()` vs `EventEmitter#once()`.

This can be done overriding the `lifetime` property. Currently available lifetimes are:

* `On` to "permanently" subscribe to the bus until manually unsubscribed (default).
* `Once` to subscribe for a single call (The `EventSubscriberMiddleware` must allow the execution).

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { AbstractEventSubscriber, PriorityEnum, EventSubscriberLifetimeEnum, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import { EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
type EventArgs = {
  someEvent: [];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<EventArgs>;
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class Once extends AbstractEventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected readonly lifetime = EventSubscriberLifetimeEnum.Once;

  public handleEvent() {
    console.log('Once');
  }
}

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class On extends AbstractEventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected readonly lifetime = EventSubscriberLifetimeEnum.On;

  public handleEvent() {
    console.log('On');
  }
}

await bus.subscribe(new Once(), new On());
await bus.emit('someEvent', []);
await bus.emit('someEvent', []);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { AbstractEventSubscriber, PriorityEnum, EventSubscriberLifetimeEnum, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import { EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
type EventArgs = {
  someEvent: [];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<EventArgs>;
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class Once extends AbstractEventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected readonly lifetime = EventSubscriberLifetimeEnum.Once;

  public handleEvent() {
    console.log('Once');
  }
}

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class On extends AbstractEventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected readonly lifetime = EventSubscriberLifetimeEnum.On;

  public handleEvent() {
    console.log('On');
  }
}

await bus.subscribe(new Once(), new On());
await bus.emit('someEvent', []);
await bus.emit('someEvent', []);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { AbstractEventSubscriber, PriorityEnum, EventSubscriberLifetimeEnum, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import { EventBus } from '@nyx-discord/http';
type EventArgs = {
  someEvent: [];
};
declare const bus: EventBus<EventArgs>;
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class Once extends AbstractEventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected readonly lifetime = EventSubscriberLifetimeEnum.Once;

  public handleEvent() {
    console.log('Once');
  }
}

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class On extends AbstractEventSubscriber<EventArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected readonly lifetime = EventSubscriberLifetimeEnum.On;

  public handleEvent() {
    console.log('On');
  }
}

await bus.subscribe(new Once(), new On());
await bus.emit('someEvent', []);
await bus.emit('someEvent', []);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Would log:
```
Once
On
On
```

Notice how the `Once` subscriber is called only once, while the `On` subscriber is called twice (as many times as the event is emitted).

## Metadata [#metadata]

When extending nyx with plugins, you may want to specify extra data for them. You can do so with the `Metadata` object, saved on the subscriber.

<Callout>
While subscribers internally save a `Metadata`, the return type of `#getMeta()` is a `ReadonlyMetadata`,
meaning that external objects can read the object, but not modify it.
</Callout>

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriber } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// ---cut-start---
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyEventSubscriber extends AbstractEventSubscriber<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected override readonly meta = {
    someKey: 'someValue',
  };
}

const myEventSubscriber = new MyEventSubscriber();
const meta = myEventSubscriber.getMeta();
const value = meta['someKey']; // 'someValue'
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriber } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// ---cut-start---
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyEventSubscriber extends AbstractEventSubscriber<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected override readonly meta = {
    someKey: 'someValue',
  };
}

const myEventSubscriber = new MyEventSubscriber();
const meta = myEventSubscriber.getMeta();
const value = meta['someKey']; // 'someValue'
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractEventSubscriber } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// ---cut-start---
type MyEventsArgs = {
  someEvent: [string, number];
};
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyEventSubscriber extends AbstractEventSubscriber<MyEventsArgs, 'someEvent'> {
  protected override readonly meta = {
    someKey: 'someValue',
  };
}

const myEventSubscriber = new MyEventSubscriber();
const meta = myEventSubscriber.getMeta();
const value = meta['someKey']; // 'someValue'
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

For a more type-safe approach, you can use `TypedFields`. Check the [Metadata](/use/other/meta) page for more information.


# Start (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/first-start)

## First Start [#first-start]

A minimum version of Node.js 18 is required to run, though we recommend latest LTS. Although they should work, nyx is
not tested on other runtimes, such as Deno or Bun.

We also recommend using a formatter like [Prettier](https://www.prettier.io/) and a linter like [ESLint](https://eslint.org/) or [TypeScript ESLint](https://typescript-eslint.io/).

<Steps>
<Step>

### Installing [#installing]

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```npm
npm i @nyx-discord/djs discord.js
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```npm
npm i @nyx-discord/djs-core @discordjs/core @discordjs/rest @discordjs/ws
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```npm
npm i @nyx-discord/http @discordjs/core
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>

### Creating a Client [#creating-a-client]

You'll need a client, which will depend on the adapter you're using. It can be any client, as long as it's not logged in or destroyed.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { Client, GatewayIntentBits } from 'discord.js';

const client = new Client({ intents: [GatewayIntentBits.Guilds] });
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { Client, GatewayIntentBits } from '@discordjs/core';
import { REST } from '@discordjs/rest';
import { WebSocketManager } from '@discordjs/ws';

const rest = new REST({ version: '10' }).setToken('TOKEN');
const gateway = new WebSocketManager({
  token: 'TOKEN',
  intents: GatewayIntentBits.Guilds,
  rest,
});
const client = new Client({ rest, gateway });
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
    No client needed: `HttpBot` creates it for you in the next step, from your application's ID and public key.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>

### Creating a Bot [#creating-a-bot]

Next up, we'll create a new instance of `Bot`. This is the main entry point of the framework, and it will handle the lifecycle
of your bot, including loading commands, managing events, and more.

<Callout>There's no global state, so you can create multiple bots and they'll all work independently with no issues!</Callout>

Create one with `Bot.create()`, which takes a function that gets passed the currently constructing bot
instance, and should return the options that you want for the bot.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { Bot, type NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
// ---cut-start---
import { Client, GatewayIntentBits } from 'discord.js';
declare const client: Client<boolean>;
// ---cut-end---

const myBot = Bot.create((bot: NyxBot) => ({
  token: 'TOKEN',
  client,
  logger: console, // Can be your own logger, see the NyxLogger docs
  deployCommands: true, // Whether to deploy commands to Discord on start
}));
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { Bot, CoreNyxClient, type NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
// ---cut-start---
import { Client, GatewayIntentBits } from '@discordjs/core';
import { REST } from '@discordjs/rest';
import { WebSocketManager } from '@discordjs/ws';
const rest = new REST({ version: '10' }).setToken('TOKEN');
const gateway = new WebSocketManager({ token: 'TOKEN', intents: GatewayIntentBits.Guilds, rest });
declare const client: Client;
// ---cut-end---

const myBot = Bot.create((bot: NyxBot) => ({
  token: 'TOKEN',
  client: new CoreNyxClient(client, gateway, 'APPLICATION_ID'),
  logger: console, // Can be your own logger, see the NyxLogger docs
  deployCommands: true, // Whether to deploy commands to Discord on start
}));
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { HttpBot, type NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const myBot = HttpBot.create((bot: NyxBot) => ({
  applicationId: 'APPLICATION_ID',
  publicKey: 'PUBLIC_KEY', // From the Developer Portal, used to verify requests
  token: 'TOKEN',
  logger: console, // Can be your own logger, see the NyxLogger docs
  deployCommands: true, // Whether to deploy commands to Discord on start
}));
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Accordions type="single">
  <Accordion title={<p>About <code>new Bot()</code></p>}>
    You can also instantiate with the [`new`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/new) operator, but in order to allow dependency
    injection, this constructor requires every manager on its options, including default ones.

    You would need to instantiate and pass every manager to it:

```ts twoslash
import { Client, GatewayIntentBits } from 'discord.js';
declare const client: Client<boolean>;
// ---cut---
import { Bot, DefaultScheduleManager, DjsNyxClient, DefaultPluginManager } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Other managers missing for brevity
// ---cut-end---
const myBot = new Bot((bot) => ({
  token: 'TOKEN',
  client: new DjsNyxClient(client),
  logger: console,
  deployCommands: true,

  scheduleManager: DefaultScheduleManager.create({ bot }),
  pluginManager: DefaultPluginManager.create({ bot }),
  // and so on
}));
```

    You'll find this pattern in other `@base` objects, where you can use either
    `new Object(depA, ...)` specifying every dependency, or `Object.create()` which uses default dependencies, and you can
    optionally inject your own to that method (while still keeping other defaults).
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

</Step>
<Step>

### Starting the Bot [#starting-the-bot]

Finally, to start it, simply call `.start()`. This will log in the client, set up event listeners, and get everything ready:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const myBot: Bot;
// ---cut-end---
await myBot.start();
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { Bot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const myBot: Bot;
// ---cut-end---
await myBot.start();
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>

This example uses `node:http`, but you can use any backend you want, including serverless!
Check out the [HTTP Bots](/use/http) section for more details.

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { HttpBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const myBot: HttpBot;
// ---cut-end---
import { createServer } from 'node:http';
import { toNodeListener } from '@nyx-discord/http';

await myBot.start();

// then pass Discord's requests to the client, see the HTTP Mounting page for other servers
createServer(toNodeListener(myBot.getClient())).listen(3000);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Callout type="warn">
  If the start errors, it'll reject the promise, and the bot will enter in a `BotStatusEnum.Killed` state, meaning it won't
  be able to be used anymore. You can create a new bot instance and start it again, but you cannot recover the previous one.

  To get a bot's status at any time, you can use `Bot#getStatus()`.
</Callout>

</Step>
</Steps>

</Card>
