  Learn how to subscribe to Client or custom events.
</Card>
<Card title="Schedules" href="/use/schedules" icon={<AlarmClockIcon />} external={false}>
  Learn how to schedule tasks to be executed at specific times.
</Card>
<Card title="Plugins" href="/use/plugins" icon={<PuzzleIcon />} external={false}>
  Learn how to create and use plugins to extend your bot's functionality.
</Card>
</Cards>


# Configuration (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/http/configuration)

Every part of the client can be replaced through `clientInjections` (or `injections`, when calling `HttpNyxClient.create()` yourself):

| Injection            | Default                                                    | Description                                                                       |
|----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `verifier`           | `DefaultSignatureVerifier`                                 | Verifies Discord's Ed25519 signatures.                                            |
| `rest`               | A `REST` with the bot's token                              | The REST client used by `api`.                                                    |
| `api`                | An `API` over `rest`                                       | The API passed to commands and subscribers.                                       |
| `emitter`            | A `BasicAwaitableEventEmitter`                             | The emitter interactions and webhook events are emitted on. Its `emit()` resolves when the listeners finish, which is what `handled` waits for. |
| `acknowledgeTimeout` | `3_000`                                                    | How long to wait for an interaction to be acknowledged, in milliseconds.          |
| `maxTimestampAge`    | `300_000`                                                  | How old (or how far in the future) a request can be before it's rejected, in ms.  |

```ts twoslash
declare const env: Record<string, string>;
// ---cut---
import { HttpBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const bot = HttpBot.create(() => ({
  applicationId: env.APP_ID,
  publicKey: env.DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY,
  token: env.TOKEN,
  logger: console,
  deployCommands: true,
  clientInjections: {
    acknowledgeTimeout: 2_500,
    maxTimestampAge: 60_000,
  },
}));
```

## Signature verification [#signature-verification]

The default verifier checks signatures with the [Web Crypto API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Crypto_API)
(`crypto.subtle`), so it needs no dependencies and works on Node.js, Bun, Deno and Cloudflare Workers.

On runtimes without a global `crypto.subtle`, like older Node.js versions, pass one yourself:

```ts twoslash
declare const env: Record<string, string>;
// ---cut---
import { webcrypto } from 'node:crypto';
import { DefaultSignatureVerifier, HttpBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const bot = HttpBot.create(() => ({
  applicationId: env.APP_ID,
  publicKey: env.DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY,
  token: env.TOKEN,
  logger: console,
  deployCommands: true,
  clientInjections: {
    verifier: DefaultSignatureVerifier.create({
      publicKey: env.DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY,
      subtle: webcrypto.subtle as SubtleCrypto,
    }),
  },
}));
```

Or implement <DocsLink pkg="http" name="SignatureVerifier" /> to use any other library. For example, with [tweetnacl](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tweetnacl):

```ts twoslash
declare const env: Record<string, string>;
// ---cut---
import nacl from 'tweetnacl';
import { HttpBot, type SignatureVerifier } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class NaclVerifier implements SignatureVerifier {
  protected readonly publicKey: Uint8Array;

  protected readonly encoder = new TextEncoder();

  constructor(publicKey: string) {
    this.publicKey = Buffer.from(publicKey, 'hex');
  }

  public async verify(body: string | Uint8Array, signature: string, timestamp: string) {
    // Discord signs the timestamp followed by the raw body
    const bodyBytes = typeof body === 'string' ? this.encoder.encode(body) : body;
    const message = Buffer.concat([this.encoder.encode(timestamp), bodyBytes]);

    try {
      return nacl.sign.detached.verify(message, Buffer.from(signature, 'hex'), this.publicKey);
    } catch {
      // tweetnacl throws on malformed signatures, which are just invalid requests
      return false;
    }
  }
}

const bot = HttpBot.create(() => ({
  applicationId: env.APP_ID,
  publicKey: env.DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY,
  token: env.TOKEN,
  logger: console,
  deployCommands: true,
  clientInjections: {
    verifier: new NaclVerifier(env.DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY),
  },
}));
```


# HTTP Overview (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/http)

The [`@nyx-discord/http`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nyx-discord/http) package lets an `@discordjs/core` bot receive [interactions](https://discord.com/developers/docs/interactions/overview)
and [webhook events](https://discord.com/developers/docs/events/webhook-events) over HTTP, instead of through a gateway connection.

Discord sends each interaction as a `POST` request to your app's Interactions Endpoint URL, so a bot that only handles
commands and components doesn't need a long-lived connection at all. It can run on a regular server, or on serverless
platforms like Cloudflare Workers or Vercel.

The framework doesn't ship a server and never opens a port. Our client takes a request and returns a response, and you pass
requests to it from the server you already use: `node:http`, Express, Fastify, Hono, Next.js, Bun, Deno, Workers...

## Installation [#installation]

<Steps>
<Step>

### Installing [#installing]

```npm
npm i @nyx-discord/http @discordjs/core
```

The package re-exports `@nyx-discord/djs-core`, so commands, events, schedules and everything else are imported from `@nyx-discord/http`. Everything in this guide that applies to `@discordjs/core` applies here too.

</Step>
<Step>

### Creating the bot [#creating-the-bot]

`HttpBot.create()` works like `@nyx-discord/djs-core`'s `Bot.create()`, but takes your application's ID and public key (both on the [Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications)) instead of a client, and creates the client for you. `Bot` from `@nyx-discord/http` is `HttpBot`, so examples using `Bot.create()` or the `Bot` type work as-is:

```ts twoslash
declare const env: Record<string, string>;
// ---cut---
import { HttpBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const bot = HttpBot.create(() => ({
  applicationId: env.APP_ID,
  publicKey: env.DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY,
  token: env.TOKEN,
  logger: console,
  deployCommands: true,
}));

await bot.start();

const client = bot.getClient();
//    ^?
```

Requests are answered with `503` until `bot.start()` finishes, so nothing reaches your commands before they're registered.

</Step>
<Step>

### Mounting the client [#mounting-the-client]

Pass incoming requests to the client from your server. See [Mounting](/use/http/mounting) for each backend:

```ts twoslash
import { HttpBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: HttpBot;
// ---cut---
import { createServer } from 'node:http';
import { toNodeListener } from '@nyx-discord/http';

createServer(toNodeListener(bot.getClient())).listen(3000);
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Setting the endpoint [#setting-the-endpoint]

On the Developer Portal, set your app's **Interactions Endpoint URL** to the public URL of that route. Discord sends a `PING` to check it, which the client answers by itself.

</Step>
</Steps>

## What's different from the gateway [#whats-different-from-the-gateway]

- Only interactions (`InteractionCreate`) and [webhook events](/use/http/webhook-events) are emitted. Subscribers to any other gateway event (messages, members, guilds...) never fire.
- Commands work unchanged: they reply through `api.interactions.reply()` and friends, as they do on the gateway. See [Handling requests](/use/http/requests).
- Schedules run while the process is alive. On serverless platforms, triggering them (e.g. with Workers cron triggers) is up to you.
- Only the `@discordjs/core` adapter is supported, since discord.js structures need a gateway-backed `Client`.

## Getting the bot [#getting-the-bot]

Inside commands, subscribers and schedules, `TypedFields.HttpBot` gets the bot from the metadata, typed so its client is the `HttpNyxClient`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSchedule, TypedFields, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class CleanupSchedule extends AbstractSchedule {
  protected readonly interval = '0 * * * *';

  public async tick(meta: Metadata) {
    const bot = TypedFields.HttpBot.get(meta, true);
    const client = bot.getClient();
    //    ^?
  }
}
```

`@nyx-discord/http` exports its own `TypedFields`, without `@nyx-discord/djs-core`'s `GatewayCoreBot`, since HTTP bots have no gateway client.


# Mounting (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/http/mounting)

Discord sends requests to two URLs, which you set on the Developer Portal:

- The **Interactions Endpoint URL**, handled by the client itself.
- The **Webhook Events URL**, handled by `client.getWebhookEventHandler()`. It's optional, see [Webhook events](/use/http/webhook-events).

Both are handlers with one method, `handle()`, which takes a request and returns the response to send. The package also includes two adapters for the most common signatures:

| Adapter          | Signature                                                                        | Use it with                                       |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| `toNodeListener` | `(req: IncomingMessage, res: ServerResponse) => Promise<void>`                    | `node:http`, Express                              |
| `toFetchHandler` | `(request: Request, context?: { waitUntil?(promise): void }) => Promise<Response>` | Hono, Cloudflare Workers, Bun, Deno, Next.js      |

Both answer non-`POST` requests with `405`.

<Callout type="warn">
  Discord's signature is checked against the **raw** request body. Make sure nothing parses the body before the client sees it, like `express.json()` or Fastify's default JSON parser.
</Callout>

## node:http [#nodehttp]

```ts twoslash
import type { HttpNyxClient } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const client: HttpNyxClient;
// ---cut---
import { createServer } from 'node:http';
import { toNodeListener } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const interactions = toNodeListener(client);
const webhookEvents = toNodeListener(client.getWebhookEventHandler());

createServer((req, res) => {
  const listener =
    req.url === '/interactions' ? interactions
    : req.url === '/webhook-events' ? webhookEvents
    : null;
  if (!listener) return void res.writeHead(404).end();

  listener(req, res).catch(console.error);
}).listen(3000);
```

## Express [#express]

```ts twoslash
import type { HttpNyxClient } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { RequestListener } from 'node:http';
declare const client: HttpNyxClient;
declare const app: { post(path: string, handler: RequestListener): void };
// ---cut---
import { toNodeListener } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// no express.json() on these routes
app.post('/interactions', toNodeListener(client));
app.post('/webhook-events', toNodeListener(client.getWebhookEventHandler()));
```

## Fastify [#fastify]

Fastify parses JSON by default, so register a parser that keeps the body as a `Buffer`, and call `handle()` directly. Passing Fastify's request as `raw` makes it available to your handlers through [`TypedFields.HttpRequest`](/use/http/requests#reading-the-request):

```ts twoslash
import type { HttpNyxClient } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const client: HttpNyxClient;
type Request = { body: unknown; headers: Record<string, string | undefined> };
type Reply = { code(status: number): Reply; headers(headers: Record<string, string>): Reply; send(body: string): Reply };
declare const app: {
  addContentTypeParser(type: string, options: { parseAs: 'buffer' }, parser: (req: Request, body: Buffer, done: (error: null, body: Buffer) => void) => void): void;
  post(path: string, handler: (req: Request, reply: Reply) => Promise<Reply>): void;
};
// ---cut---
app.addContentTypeParser('application/json', { parseAs: 'buffer' }, (_req, body, done) => done(null, body));

const endpoints = [
  ['/interactions', client],
  ['/webhook-events', client.getWebhookEventHandler()],
] as const;

for (const [path, handler] of endpoints) {
  app.post(path, async (req, reply) => {
    const result = await handler.handle({
      body: req.body as Buffer,
      signature: req.headers['x-signature-ed25519'],
      timestamp: req.headers['x-signature-timestamp'],
      raw: req,
    });

    return reply.code(result.status).headers(result.headers).send(result.body);
  });
}
```

## Hono [#hono]

```ts twoslash
import type { HttpNyxClient } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const client: HttpNyxClient;
declare const app: { post(path: string, handler: (c: { req: { raw: Request } }) => Promise<Response>): void };
// ---cut---
import { toFetchHandler } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const interactions = toFetchHandler(client);
const webhookEvents = toFetchHandler(client.getWebhookEventHandler());

app.post('/interactions', (c) => interactions(c.req.raw));
app.post('/webhook-events', (c) => webhookEvents(c.req.raw));
```

When Hono runs on Cloudflare Workers, pass `c.executionCtx` as the second argument too, so the worker stays alive until your handlers finish.

## Cloudflare Workers [#cloudflare-workers]

Pass the worker's `ctx` as the handler's second argument, so the worker stays alive until your handlers finish (see [Serverless platforms](/use/http/requests#serverless-platforms)):

```ts twoslash
import type { HttpNyxClient } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const client: HttpNyxClient;
type ExecutionContext = { waitUntil(promise: Promise<unknown>): void };
// ---cut---
import { toFetchHandler } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const interactions = toFetchHandler(client);
const webhookEvents = toFetchHandler(client.getWebhookEventHandler());

export default {
  fetch(request: Request, env: unknown, ctx: ExecutionContext) {
    const { pathname } = new URL(request.url);
    const handler = pathname === '/webhook-events' ? webhookEvents : interactions;

    return handler(request, ctx);
  },
};
```

## Bun and Deno [#bun-and-deno]

Both accept a default export with a `fetch` handler:

```ts twoslash
import type { HttpNyxClient } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const client: HttpNyxClient;
// ---cut---
import { toFetchHandler } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const interactions = toFetchHandler(client);
const webhookEvents = toFetchHandler(client.getWebhookEventHandler());

export default {
  fetch(request: Request) {
    const { pathname } = new URL(request.url);
    return pathname === '/webhook-events' ? webhookEvents(request) : interactions(request);
  },
};
```

## Next.js [#nextjs]

Use a route handler for each URL, passing [`after()`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/after) as `waitUntil`, so the function stays alive until your handlers finish:

```ts twoslash title="app/interactions/route.ts"
import type { HttpNyxClient } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const client: HttpNyxClient;
// ---cut---
import { after } from 'next/server';
import { toFetchHandler } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const interactions = toFetchHandler(client);

export const POST = (request: Request) => interactions(request, { waitUntil: after });
```

```ts twoslash title="app/webhook-events/route.ts"
import type { HttpNyxClient } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const client: HttpNyxClient;
// ---cut---
import { after } from 'next/server';
import { toFetchHandler } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const webhookEvents = toFetchHandler(client.getWebhookEventHandler());

export const POST = (request: Request) => webhookEvents(request, { waitUntil: after });
```

## Anything else [#anything-else]

Call `handle()` with the raw body (a `string` or `Uint8Array`) and the two signature headers, then send back what it returns. The webhook event handler works the same way:

```ts twoslash
import type { HttpNyxClient } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const client: HttpNyxClient;
declare const rawBody: Uint8Array;
declare const headers: Record<string, string | undefined>;
declare const originalRequest: unknown;
// ---cut---
const result = await client.handle({
  body: rawBody,
  signature: headers['x-signature-ed25519'],
  timestamp: headers['x-signature-timestamp'],
  raw: originalRequest, // optional, for TypedFields.HttpRequest
});

result.status; // the status code
result.headers; // the headers to set
result.body; // the body, empty when there's none
result.handled; // settles once the handlers finish, for waitUntil()
```


# Handling requests (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/http/requests)

## Responses [#responses]

Every request goes through the same checks before it reaches your bot:

| Request                                           | Response               |
|---------------------------------------------------|------------------------|
| Before `bot.start()` finishes                     | `503`                  |
| Missing or invalid signature                      | `401`                  |
| Timestamp older (or newer) than `maxTimestampAge` | `401`                  |
| Body that isn't valid JSON                        | `400`                  |
| Interaction `PING` (Discord checking your URL)    | `200` with a `PONG`    |
| Any other interaction                             | `202` with no body     |
| [Webhook event](/use/http/webhook-events) or its `PING` | `204` with no body   |

Rejecting old timestamps protects against replayed requests: someone who captured a valid request can't send it again later. The window is 5 minutes by default, see [Configuration](/use/http/configuration).

## Replying to interactions [#replying-to-interactions]

Over the gateway, commands reply by calling Discord's REST API, like `api.interactions.reply()`. Over HTTP they do exactly the same: Discord accepts interaction responses through the REST callback endpoint, as long as the HTTP request itself is answered with a `202`.

This means commands, components and autocompletes written for `@discordjs/core` work unchanged:

```ts twoslash
import type { APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction, RESTPostAPIChatInputApplicationCommandsJSONBody, ToEventProps } from '@discordjs/core';
// ---cut---
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class PingCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  // ---cut-start---
  protected readonly data = {} as RESTPostAPIChatInputApplicationCommandsJSONBody;
  // ---cut-end---
  public async execute({ data, api }: ToEventProps<APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction>) {
    await api.interactions.reply(data.id, data.token, { content: 'Pong!' });
  }
}
```

The client doesn't answer Discord's request right away. It waits until the interaction is acknowledged (any reply, defer, update, modal or autocomplete response), until the handlers finish without acknowledging it (for example, when no command matches), or until `acknowledgeTimeout` passes (3 seconds by default), and then returns the `202`. Discord requires the first response within 3 seconds, so slow commands should defer first, exactly like on the gateway.

## Reading the request [#reading-the-request]

`TypedFields.HttpRequest` gets the HTTP request an interaction or webhook event came from, from the metadata of commands, components and subscribers. Its `raw` property is the original request from your server or runtime, so you can read anything else from it, like headers:

```ts twoslash
import type { APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction, RESTPostAPIChatInputApplicationCommandsJSONBody, ToEventProps } from '@discordjs/core';
// ---cut---
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand, TypedFields, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class WhereAmICommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  // ---cut-start---
  protected readonly data = {} as RESTPostAPIChatInputApplicationCommandsJSONBody;
  // ---cut-end---
  public async execute({ data, api }: ToEventProps<APIChatInputApplicationCommandInteraction>, meta: Metadata) {
    const request = TypedFields.HttpRequest.get(meta);
    //    ^?

    // raw is a fetch Request with toFetchHandler, or a node:http IncomingMessage with toNodeListener
    const country = request?.raw instanceof Request ? request.raw.headers.get('cf-ipcountry') : null;

    await api.interactions.reply(data.id, data.token, { content: `You're in ${country ?? 'somewhere'}` });
  }
}
```

`HttpBot` sets this up for you. If you create the `HttpNyxClient` yourself, add the field to the client event bus once the bot is created:

```ts twoslash
import type { CoreNyxBot, HttpNyxClient } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: CoreNyxBot;
declare const client: HttpNyxClient;
// ---cut---
import { TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/http';

bot.getClientEventBus().getMetadataFactory().addDefaultField(TypedFields.HttpRequest, () => client.getCurrentRequest());
```

<Callout>
  The client only knows which request it's emitting while its listeners are being called, so this relies on the bus creating its metadata as soon as it receives an event, before awaiting anything. nyx's default buses do. A custom bus that doesn't would see `null`.
</Callout>

## Serverless platforms [#serverless-platforms]

On serverless platforms, the runtime may stop once the response is sent. Anything your command does after its first reply (follow-ups, edits, other API calls) can then be cut off.

Every result from the client has a `handled` promise, which settles once the request's handlers finish: your commands, components and subscribers. Pass it to your platform's tool for keeping work alive, like [`ctx.waitUntil()`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/context/#waituntil) on Cloudflare Workers or [`after()`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/after) on Next.js.

`toFetchHandler()` does it for you when you pass a context with `waitUntil` as its second argument, see [Mounting](/use/http/mounting). When calling `handle()` yourself:

```ts twoslash
import type { HttpNyxClient, HttpEndpointRequest } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const client: HttpNyxClient;
declare const request: HttpEndpointRequest;
declare const ctx: { waitUntil(promise: Promise<unknown>): void };
// ---cut---
const result = await client.handle(request);
ctx.waitUntil(result.handled);
```

Webhook events need this the most: the client answers them right away, before any subscriber runs.


# Webhook events (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/http/webhook-events)

Besides interactions, Discord can send some events about your app over HTTP: [webhook events](https://discord.com/developers/docs/events/webhook-events). For example, when a user authorizes or deauthorizes your app, or when an entitlement is created.

They're sent to a separate URL, the **Webhook Events URL**, which you set on the Developer Portal under **Webhooks**, along with the events you want to receive.

## Mounting [#mounting]

`client.getWebhookEventHandler()` returns a handler for that URL, which works with the same [adapters](/use/http/mounting) as the client:

```ts twoslash
import type { HttpNyxClient } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { RequestListener } from 'node:http';
declare const client: HttpNyxClient;
declare const app: { post(path: string, handler: RequestListener): void };
// ---cut---
import { toNodeListener } from '@nyx-discord/http';

app.post('/interactions', toNodeListener(client));
app.post('/webhook-events', toNodeListener(client.getWebhookEventHandler()));
```

The handler verifies requests like the client does, and answers every event (and Discord's `PING`) with a `204`.

## Subscribing [#subscribing]

Each event is emitted on the client's emitter under its type, one of the [`ApplicationWebhookEventType`](https://discord-api-types.dev/api/discord-api-types-v10/enum/ApplicationWebhookEventType) values. An `HttpBot`'s client event bus accepts them, so write an `AbstractWebhookEventSubscriber` and subscribe it like any other client subscriber:

```ts twoslash
import type { HttpBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: HttpBot;
// ---cut---
import type { APIWebhookEventApplicationAuthorizedData } from '@discordjs/core';
import { ApplicationWebhookEventType } from '@discordjs/core';
import { AbstractWebhookEventSubscriber, type Metadata, type WebhookEventProps } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class AuthorizedSubscriber extends AbstractWebhookEventSubscriber<ApplicationWebhookEventType.ApplicationAuthorized> {
  protected readonly event = ApplicationWebhookEventType.ApplicationAuthorized;

  public handleEvent(
    _meta: Metadata,
    { data, timestamp }: WebhookEventProps<APIWebhookEventApplicationAuthorizedData>,
  ) {
    console.log(`${data.user.username} authorized the app at ${timestamp}`);
    //                     ^?
  }
}

await bot.subscribeToClient(new AuthorizedSubscriber());
```

Since they're client subscribers, the [event loader](/loaders/events) picks them up too, and their metadata has the same fields as other client events, like [`TypedFields.HttpRequest`](/use/http/requests#reading-the-request).

The payload is the usual `{ data, api, shardId }`, where `data` is the event's data (`APIWebhookEvent...Data` from `discord-api-types`), plus the event's `timestamp`. Webhook events aren't realtime and can arrive late or out of order, so use the timestamp when order matters.

<Callout>
  Discord retries an event for up to 10 minutes if your endpoint doesn't answer, and stops sending events if it fails too often. Since the handler answers as soon as the event is emitted, slow subscribers don't delay the response.
</Callout>


# Introduction (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use)

![nyx](/nyx_guide.png)

<GithubInfo owner="nyx-discord" repo="nyx" />

Hello there 👋! Welcome to official guide for using nyx, a TypeScript bot framework for Discord.

Here, you'll discover what nyx is, how to create your own bot and how to customize it.

## What is nyx? [#what-is-nyx]

Nyx is a framework to build Discord bots in TypeScript, with adapters for [discord.js](https://discord.js.org),
[@discordjs/core](https://discord.js.org/docs/packages/core/main) and HTTP-only bots with [`@nyx-discord/http`](/use/http),
built on top of `@discordjs/core`.

The main ideas behind the framework are:

<Cards>
  <Card icon={<BlocksIcon />} title="Fully extendable">
    Every single internal component is documented and can be easily swapped by your own. We want you to know how your
    bot fully works.
  </Card>
  <Card icon={<CircleDotDashedIcon />} title="Bare-bones">
    As little runtime dependencies as possible, which you can also replace.
  </Card>
  <Card icon={<LockOpenIcon />} title="Architecture freedom">
    Nyx doesn't enforce any specific way to do things. Choose your own folder structure, way to load commands/events,
    databases, naming conventions, etc.
  </Card>
  <Card icon={<SmileIcon />} title="Easy to understand and setup">
    Hacky code is avoided, like changing Discord.js typings or internals.
    Type safety, error handling and extensibility are prioritized over convenience and magic.
  </Card>
  <Card icon={<SiDiscorddotjs />} title="Native objects">
    Use the objects you already know from your Discord library without needing to learn new wrappers.
  </Card>
  <Card icon={<LayersIcon />} title="A presentation layer, not the whole system">
    Nyx doesn't own your bot's logic, build step or runtime. It's the layer that connects Discord to your design, so
    your core logic stays independent and testable.
  </Card>
</Cards>

<Callout type="warn" title="Warnings">
  - We assume you have some level of understanding of TypeScript.
  - The framework doesn't come with any commands, events or filters (like cooldowns). To avoid being too opinionated,
  we only ship the things required for you to be able to build such features. Our optional packages provide some utilities,
  but you can also build your own.
</Callout>

## Key Features [#key-features]

1. **[Commands](/use/commands)**, for Discord application commands. Includes support for context menu commands, subcommands, and more.
2. **[Events](/use/events)**, for subscribing to events, either from Discord.js or your own.
3. **[Schedules](/use/schedules)**, for timed tasks.
4. **[Plugins](/use/plugins)**, for pieces that extend nyx.

All of these features are documented in detail in their respective sections, which we'll cover next.

Through optional packages, it also supports:
1. **[Sessions](/session)**, for stateful interaction conversations, similar to collectors.
2. **[Loaders](/loaders)**, for scanning directories to load commands, events, and schedules.
3. **[Type-safe Options](/typed-options)**, for creating commands with type-safe options.

<Callout title="Codeblocks">
The codeblocks in this guide are powered by [Twoslash](https://twoslash.netlify.app/guide/), meaning:

- You can hover over variables, functions, etc. to see their documentation.
- Every example (only often skipping trivial or already mentioned declarations) will work, otherwise this guide wouldn't compile!
</Callout>

# Error Handling (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/other/error-handling)

Every executor holds an `ErrorHandler`, where errors thrown by middlewares and executed objects are handled.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { NyxBot, AnyEventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
declare const bus: AnyEventBus;
// ---cut---
const commandErrorHandler = bot.getCommandManager().getExecutor().getErrorHandler();
const eventErrorHandler = bus.getDispatcher().getErrorHandler();
const scheduleErrorHandler = bot.getScheduleManager().getExecutor().getErrorHandler();
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { NyxBot, AnyEventBus } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
declare const bus: AnyEventBus;
// ---cut---
const commandErrorHandler = bot.getCommandManager().getExecutor().getErrorHandler();
const eventErrorHandler = bus.getDispatcher().getErrorHandler();
const scheduleErrorHandler = bot.getScheduleManager().getExecutor().getErrorHandler();
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { NyxBot, AnyEventBus } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
declare const bus: AnyEventBus;
// ---cut---
const commandErrorHandler = bot.getCommandManager().getExecutor().getErrorHandler();
const eventErrorHandler = bus.getDispatcher().getErrorHandler();
const scheduleErrorHandler = bot.getScheduleManager().getExecutor().getErrorHandler();
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

It holds a map of consumers, where each handle a specific error class. It also receives the erroring object, and the arguments that were used to call it.

## Manipulating consumers [#manipulating-consumers]

<Callout>This example will use the `CommandManager`'s handler, but it works the same for other executors.</Callout>

To add a consumer, use `ErrorHandler#setConsumer()`:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
const errorHandler = bot.getCommandManager().getExecutor().getErrorHandler();
// ---cut---
import { TypedFields, CommandError } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { CommandExecutionArgs, AnyExecutableCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

errorHandler.setConsumer(
  CommandError,
  (
    error: CommandError,
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    args: CommandExecutionArgs,
  ) => {
    const [_interaction, meta] = args;
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);
    const { name } = command.getData();

    bot.getLogger().error(
      `MyError occurred while executing ${name} with args: ${args}`,
      error
    );
  }
);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
const errorHandler = bot.getCommandManager().getExecutor().getErrorHandler();
// ---cut---
import { TypedFields, CommandError } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { CommandExecutionArgs, AnyExecutableCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

errorHandler.setConsumer(
  CommandError,
  (
    error: CommandError,
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    args: CommandExecutionArgs,
  ) => {
    const [_interaction, meta] = args;
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);
    const { name } = command.getData();

    bot.getLogger().error(
      `MyError occurred while executing ${name} with args: ${args}`,
      error
    );
  }
);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
const errorHandler = bot.getCommandManager().getExecutor().getErrorHandler();
// ---cut---
import { TypedFields, CommandError } from '@nyx-discord/http';

  CommandError,
  (
    error: CommandError,
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    args: CommandExecutionArgs,
  ) => {
    const [_interaction, meta] = args;
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);
    const { name } = command.getData();

    bot.getLogger().error(
      `MyError occurred while executing ${name} with args: ${args}`,
      error
    );
  }
);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

You can also remove consumers:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
const errorHandler = bot.getCommandManager().getExecutor().getErrorHandler();
import { CommandError } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { CommandExecutionArgs, AnyExecutableCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
// ---cut---
errorHandler.removeConsumerOf(CommandError);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
const errorHandler = bot.getCommandManager().getExecutor().getErrorHandler();
import { CommandError } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { CommandExecutionArgs, AnyExecutableCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
// ---cut---
errorHandler.removeConsumerOf(CommandError);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
const errorHandler = bot.getCommandManager().getExecutor().getErrorHandler();
import { CommandError } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { CommandExecutionArgs, AnyExecutableCommand } from '@nyx-discord/http';
// ---cut---
errorHandler.removeConsumerOf(CommandError);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

And set a fallback consumer, for all errors that don't have a consumer:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
const errorHandler = bot.getCommandManager().getExecutor().getErrorHandler();
import { CommandError } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { CommandExecutionArgs, AnyExecutableCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
// ---cut---
import { TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

errorHandler.setFallbackConsumer(
  (
    error: object,
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    args: CommandExecutionArgs,
  ) => {
    const [_interaction, meta] = args;
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);
    const { name } = command.getData();

    bot.getLogger().error(
      `An unhandled error occurred while executing ${name} with args: ${args}`,
      error
    );
  }
);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
const errorHandler = bot.getCommandManager().getExecutor().getErrorHandler();
import { CommandError } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { CommandExecutionArgs, AnyExecutableCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
// ---cut---
import { TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

errorHandler.setFallbackConsumer(
  (
    error: object,
    command: AnyExecutableCommand,
    args: CommandExecutionArgs,
  ) => {
    const [_interaction, meta] = args;
    const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);
    const { name } = command.getData();

    bot.getLogger().error(
      `An unhandled error occurred while executing ${name} with args: ${args}`,
      error
    );
  }
);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';

    const { name } = command.getData();

    bot.getLogger().error(
      `An unhandled error occurred while executing ${name} with args: ${args}`,
      error
    );
  }
);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Consumer resolution [#consumer-resolution]

The error handler resolves a consumer based on the error prototype, going from the top to the bottom.

For instance:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
const errorHandler = BasicErrorHandler.create<object, unknown[]>();
// ---cut---
class MyError extends Error {}

class MyError2 extends MyError {}

errorHandler.setConsumer(MyError, () => {
  console.log('MyError');
});
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
const errorHandler = BasicErrorHandler.create<object, unknown[]>();
// ---cut---
class MyError extends Error {}

class MyError2 extends MyError {}

errorHandler.setConsumer(MyError, () => {
  console.log('MyError');
});
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { BasicErrorHandler } from '@nyx-discord/http';
const errorHandler = BasicErrorHandler.create<object, unknown[]>();
// ---cut---
class MyError extends Error {}

class MyError2 extends MyError {}

errorHandler.setConsumer(MyError, () => {
  console.log('MyError');
});
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

This will log `MyError` when an instance of `MyError2` is thrown, because it's a subclass.

If no consumer is found, the fallback consumer is used, whose error type is simply `object`.


# Filters (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/other/filters)

Filters are objects or callbacks that can restrict the execution of a given component.

They receive all the information about the execution (context, arguments, metadata), and return a boolean indicating whether the execution should proceed (`true`) or strictly stop (`false`).

## Wrapping/Merging Filters [#wrappingmerging-filters]

The framework has some utility filters that wrap or merge others, allowing you to create complex filters by combining simpler ones.

<Callout>These wrappers work "synchronously", meaning that it'll wait for each filter, in the order they were passed, before checking whether to proceed to the next.</Callout>

### AndFilter [#andfilter]

Combines multiple filters and only allows the execution if **all** filters return `true`.

```ts
new AndFilter(filter1, filter2, filter3)
```

### OrFilter [#orfilter]

Combines multiple filters and allows the execution if **at least one** filter returns `true`.

```ts
new OrFilter(filter1, filter2)
```

### NotFilter [#notfilter]

Inverts the result of a single filter, allowing the execution if the filter returns `false`.

```ts
new NotFilter(filter)
```


# Metadata (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/other/metadata)

Many parts of the framework introduce the concept of a `Metadata`, which can store metadata about a given object, or about a given execution.

## Type Safety [#type-safety]

Since a metadata object is just a record of unknown values, it's inherently unsafe by itself.

For that reason, nyx uses the [`typed-field`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/typed-field) package, which creates a unique key, and only lets you set/get with a given type.

<Callout>
The `typed-field` package is re-exported in `TypedFields.create()` method, so you don't need to install it separately.
</Callout>

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// @errors: 2345
import { TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

const meta: Record<string | symbol, unknown> = Object.create(null);

// Fields with the same description won't collide
const field = TypedFields.create<number>('someDescription');

field.set(meta, 42);
field.set(meta, 'foo');

const stored = field.get(meta);
//    ^?

// Throws if no value was set
const forced = field.get(meta, true);
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// @errors: 2345
import { TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

const meta: Record<string | symbol, unknown> = Object.create(null);

// Fields with the same description won't collide
const field = TypedFields.create<number>('someDescription');

field.set(meta, 42);
field.set(meta, 'foo');

const stored = field.get(meta);
//    ^?

// Throws if no value was set
const forced = field.get(meta, true);
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// @errors: 2345
import { TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const meta: Record<string | symbol, unknown> = Object.create(null);

// Fields with the same description won't collide
const field = TypedFields.create<number>('someDescription');

field.set(meta, 42);
field.set(meta, 'foo');

const stored = field.get(meta);
//    ^?

// Throws if no value was set
const forced = field.get(meta, true);
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Object Metadata [#object-metadata]

Most nyx objects implement a `getMeta(): ReadonlyMetadata` method. When creating your class, you can fill this with your own metadata, which can then be read by plugins or other entities to extract extra information about your object.

As a plugin developer, you may also choose to use the `TypedFields` API to create and expose a field:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

type MyPluginData = {
  someKey: string;
}
export const MyPluginDataField = TypedFields.create<MyPluginData>('myPluginData');
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

type MyPluginData = {
  someKey: string;
}
export const MyPluginDataField = TypedFields.create<MyPluginData>('myPluginData');
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/http';

type MyPluginData = {
  someKey: string;
}
export const MyPluginDataField = TypedFields.create<MyPluginData>('myPluginData');
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Then, a consumer of your plugin can use it to decorate their objects' metadata:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// @errors: 2345
import { TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
type MyPluginData = {
  someKey: string;
}
const MyPluginDataField = TypedFields.create<MyPluginData>('myPluginData');
// ---cut---
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
// @noErrors
import { MyPluginDataField } from 'my-nyx-plugin';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MyCommand extends AbstractStandaloneCommand {
  constructor() {
    super();
    MyPluginDataField.set(this.meta, { someKey: 'someValue' });

    // In case they use it wrongly, it'll error:
    MyPluginDataField.set(this.meta, 42);
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// @errors: 2345
import { TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
type MyPluginData = {
  someKey: string;
}
const MyPluginDataField = TypedFields.create<MyPluginData>('myPluginData');
// ---cut---
import { AbstractStandaloneCommand } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
// @noErrors

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---

    super();
    MyPluginDataField.set(this.meta, { someKey: 'someValue' });

    // In case they use it wrongly, it'll error:
    MyPluginDataField.set(this.meta, 42);
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// @errors: 2345

  someKey: string;

  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Which then you'll be able to read with `MyCommand#getMeta()` and your field, safely.

## Execution Metadata [#execution-metadata]

Every "executable" object includes in its arguments an instance of a `Metadata`, which is passed around to middlewares and filters, so they can share data between them, and to your executed object.

Additionally, the `TypedFields` class contains constant fields that the framework uses to store framework-specific data. 

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { Collection } from 'discord.js';
const meta: Record<string | symbol, unknown> = Object.create(null);
// ---cut---
import { TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// The bot who triggered the object (command, event, etc).
const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);
//    ^?

// The identifier of this object execution, which is a Symbol containing some debugable information.
const id = TypedFields.Id.get(meta, true);
//    ^?

// The creation date of this meta, can be used as the execution start time.
const creationDate = TypedFields.CreationDate.get(meta, true);
//    ^?

// Only for event middlewares and subscribers, whether the event was marked as handled by a subscriber.
const handled = TypedFields.EventHandled.get(meta, true);
//    ^?

// Only for event middlewares and subscribers, the EventBus that dispatched the event.
const eventBus = TypedFields.EventBus.get(meta, true);
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { Collection } from 'discord.js';
const meta: Record<string | symbol, unknown> = Object.create(null);
// ---cut---
import { TypedFields } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// The bot who triggered the object (command, event, etc).
const bot = TypedFields.Bot.get(meta, true);
//    ^?

// The identifier of this object execution, which is a Symbol containing some debugable information.
const id = TypedFields.Id.get(meta, true);
//    ^?

// The creation date of this meta, can be used as the execution start time.
const creationDate = TypedFields.CreationDate.get(meta, true);
//    ^?

// Only for event middlewares and subscribers, whether the event was marked as handled by a subscriber.
const handled = TypedFields.EventHandled.get(meta, true);
//    ^?

// Only for event middlewares and subscribers, the EventBus that dispatched the event.
const eventBus = TypedFields.EventBus.get(meta, true);
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { Collection } from 'discord.js';
const meta: Record<string | symbol, unknown> = Object.create(null);
// ---cut---

//    ^?

//    ^?

// The creation date of this meta, can be used as the execution start time.

//    ^?

// Only for event middlewares and subscribers, whether the event was marked as handled by a subscriber.
const handled = TypedFields.EventHandled.get(meta, true);
//    ^?

// Only for event middlewares and subscribers, the EventBus that dispatched the event.
const eventBus = TypedFields.EventBus.get(meta, true);
//    ^?
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Forcing these reads is safe for metadatas created inside the framework, but not for user-created metadatas, including those created by external [`EventBuses`](/use/events/buses) (since they're bot-independent).


# Middlewares (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/other/middlewares)

Middlewares are objects or callbacks that run before an execution. They can do some pre-processing logic and store it in the metadata, or even prevent the execution.

We will review some concepts before going into the usage.

## Priorities [#priorities]

The <DocsLink pkg="base" name="Priority" decorated={false} label="Priority" /> determines the order in which they are executed:

- Higher priorities are executed first.
- Monitors are specifically meant for monitoring (e.g. metrics), though that's not enforced.
  - `HighMonitor` is the first priority to be executed.
  - `LowMonitor` is the last priority to be executed.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { PriorityEnum } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// @noErrors
PriorityEnum.
//           ^|
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { PriorityEnum } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// @noErrors
PriorityEnum.
//           ^|
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { PriorityEnum } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// @noErrors
PriorityEnum.
//           ^|
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The default priority is `Normal`, it's changed by overriding the `priority` property in classes. It can't be changed for callback-based middlewares.

## Responses [#responses]

A middleware returns a <DocsLink pkg="base" name="MiddlewareResponse" decorated={false} label="MiddlewareResponse" /> that indicates whether it passes, forces to pass, or fails. If a middleware fails, the execution will stop.

Use the utility methods from the abstract middleware class to create the response:
- `true()` - The middleware passes, and the execution will continue.
- `false()` - The middleware fails, and the execution will stop.
- `forceTrue()` - The middleware forces to pass, even if other later middlewares would fail.

If you're using a callback-based middleware, you'll need to create your response manually.


# Packages (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/packages)

## Which package do I need? [#which-package-do-i-need]

You only need to install **one**: the adapter that matches how your bot connects to Discord.

| If your bot...                                                                                    | Install                 |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------|
| Uses [discord.js](https://discord.js.org)                                                         | `@nyx-discord/djs`      |
| Uses [@discordjs/core](https://discord.js.org/docs/packages/core/main)                            | `@nyx-discord/djs-core` |
| Only handles HTTP payloads instead of the gateway (e.g. on a serverless platform)                 | `@nyx-discord/http`     |

Under the hood, every adapter is built over `@nyx-discord/base`, which has the interfaces every component follows,
plus some default implementations of them. The adapters add the missing parts that connect to your Discord library.

Every component depends on interfaces rather than on the default implementations, so you can replace any of them with
your own. You can later check the [Extend](/extend) section for how.

## Interfaces and implementations [#interfaces-and-implementations]

`@nyx-discord/base` contains two kinds of objects, which you can tell apart by their names.

**Interfaces** have no prefix, like <DocsLink pkg='base' name='SubCommand' decorated={false} label={<code>SubCommand</code>} /> or <DocsLink pkg='base' name='CommandManager' decorated={false} label={<code>CommandManager</code>} />. They describe what a component does, and are what the rest of the framework expects.

**Implementations** have a prefix that tells you how to use them:

| Prefix     | Meaning                                                                                                     | Example                                                                                                                       |
|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `Abstract` | Needs to be extended to be used. You'll extend these to create your own commands, subscribers, schedules, etc. | <DocsLink pkg='base' name='AbstractSchedule' decorated={false} label={<code>AbstractSchedule</code>} />                       |
| `Basic`    | A complete, simple implementation. Use it directly, or extend it to customize it.                           | <DocsLink pkg='base' name='BasicEventBus' decorated={false} label={<code>BasicEventBus</code>} />                             |
| `Default`  | The implementation the bot uses internally. To customize it, extend it and [inject your version](/extend).  | <DocsLink pkg='base' name='DefaultCommandManager' decorated={false} label={<code>DefaultCommandManager</code>} />           |
| `Base`     | A Discord-library-agnostic foundation that the adapters build on. You won't use these directly.         | <DocsLink pkg='base' name='BaseCommand' decorated={false} label={<code>BaseCommand</code>} />                                 |

For example, your adapter's <DocsLink pkg='djs' name='AbstractStandaloneCommand' decorated={false} label={<code>AbstractStandaloneCommand</code>} /> builds on <DocsLink pkg='base' name='BaseStandaloneCommand' decorated={false} label={<code>BaseStandaloneCommand</code>} />, adding the types of your Discord library. Extend the adapter's version, not the `Base` one.

When you want to specify a type, prefer the interfaces, e.g. `consume(cmd: SubCommand)` instead
of `consume(cmd: AbstractSubCommand)`. That way your code works with any implementation, following
[Dependency inversion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dependency_inversion_principle).

## Building something for nyx [#building-something-for-nyx]

If you're developing something for nyx itself, such as a plugin, you can depend on `@nyx-discord/base` instead of an
adapter, so your component works across all of them.

`@nyx-discord/base` also lets you import each kind of object separately:

| Import                       | Contains                     |
|------------------------------|------------------------------|
| `@nyx-discord/base`          | Everything.                  |
| `@nyx-discord/base/types`    | Only the interfaces.         |
| `@nyx-discord/base/defaults` | Only the implementations.    |

Importing your types from `@nyx-discord/base/types` makes it impossible to accidentally depend on an implementation.


# Events (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/plugins/events)

<Callout type="warn">It's recommended to read the [Events Overview](../events/index) and [Event Subscribers](../events/subscribers) pages first.</Callout>

The `PluginManager` has an `EventBus` that allows you to listen to events related to plugins.

This is useful for monitoring, logging, or any other custom logic you want to execute when a plugin is added/removed.

## Events [#events]

The following events are available:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { PluginEventEnum } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// @noErrors
PluginEventEnum.
//              ^|
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { PluginEventEnum } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// @noErrors
PluginEventEnum.
//              ^|
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { PluginEventEnum } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// @noErrors
PluginEventEnum.
//              ^|
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Usage [#usage]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Subscriber creation [#subscriber-creation]

Create a subscriber that will listen to a given event, use the `PluginEventArgs` type for the arguments map. Check the [Event Subscribers](../events/subscribers) page for more information.

</Step>
<Step>
### Subscription [#subscription]

Subscribe to the event using the `PluginEventArgs`'s `subscribe()` method.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { EventSubscriber, PluginEventArgs } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const subscriber: EventSubscriber<PluginEventArgs, keyof PluginEventArgs>;
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut-end---
await bot.getPluginManager().subscribe(subscriber);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---
import { EventSubscriber, PluginEventArgs } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const subscriber: EventSubscriber<PluginEventArgs, keyof PluginEventArgs>;
import type { NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut-end---
await bot.getPluginManager().subscribe(subscriber);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut-start---

// ---cut-end---

```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>
</Step>
</Steps>


# Plugins Overview (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/plugins)

Plugins are objects that can be used to pack functionality, such as commands, events and schedules.

## Usage [#usage]

<Steps>
<Step>
### Plugin creation [#plugin-creation]

Create a class that implements <DocsLink pkg="base" name="NyxPlugin" label={<code>NyxPlugin</code>} decorated={false}/>.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { NyxPlugin, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyPlugin implements NyxPlugin {
  public static readonly Id = Symbol('my-plugin');

  public async onRegister(bot: NyxBot) {
    bot.getLogger().log('My plugin has been registered!');
  }

  public async onUnregister(bot: NyxBot) {
    bot.getLogger().log('My plugin has been unregistered!');
  }

  public getData() {
    return {
      name: 'my-plugin',
      version: '1.0.0',
      description: 'My plugin',
      // Optional
      git: 'https://github.com/...',
    }
  }

  public getId() {
    return MyPlugin.Id;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { NyxPlugin, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyPlugin implements NyxPlugin {
  public static readonly Id = Symbol('my-plugin');

  public async onRegister(bot: NyxBot) {
    bot.getLogger().log('My plugin has been registered!');
  }

  public async onUnregister(bot: NyxBot) {
    bot.getLogger().log('My plugin has been unregistered!');
  }

  public getData() {
    return {
      name: 'my-plugin',
      version: '1.0.0',
      description: 'My plugin',
      // Optional
      git: 'https://github.com/...',
    }
  }

  public getId() {
    return MyPlugin.Id;
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash

      name: 'my-plugin',
      version: '1.0.0',

  }

    return MyPlugin.Id;

```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The `getData()` method is unused by the framework, but it provides information to the plugin's consumer.

</Step>
<Step>

### Registration [#registration]

Register it to a bot's `PluginManager`:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { NyxBot, NyxPlugin } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
declare const MyPlugin: new () => NyxPlugin;
// ---cut---
await bot.getPluginManager().register(new MyPlugin());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>

  </Tab>

  </Tab>

</Step>

# Filters (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/schedules/filters)

Filters restrict the execution of a given schedule. For example:
- A [maintenance filter](#maintenance-filter) that checks if the system is in maintenance mode
- A [production filter](#production-filter) that restricts the execution to the production environment.

They receive all the information about the schedule and the execution metadata, and return a boolean indicating whether the schedule should be executed or not.

For more general information about filters, you must first read the general [Filters](/use/other/filters) guide.

## Usage [#usage]

<Steps>
<Step>

### Creation [#creation]

Either:

- Create a class that extends `AbstractScheduleFilter` and implements the `check()` method.
 <Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut---
import { AbstractScheduleFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { Schedule, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyFilter extends AbstractScheduleFilter {
  public async check(schedule: Schedule, meta: Metadata): Promise<boolean> {
    // Do some checks
    return true; // or false if the schedule should not be executed
  }
}
 ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut---
import { AbstractScheduleFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { Schedule, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyFilter extends AbstractScheduleFilter {
  public async check(schedule: Schedule, meta: Metadata): Promise<boolean> {
    // Do some checks
    return true; // or false if the schedule should not be executed
  }
}
 ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
// ---cut---
import { AbstractScheduleFilter } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { Schedule, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyFilter extends AbstractScheduleFilter {
  public async check(schedule: Schedule, meta: Metadata): Promise<boolean> {
    // Do some checks
    return true; // or false if the schedule should not be executed
  }
}
 ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

- Create a function that returns a boolean or a Promise that resolves to a boolean.
 <Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut---
import { type ScheduleFilterResolvable } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

const myFilter: ScheduleFilterResolvable = async (schedule, meta) => {
  // Do some checks
  return true; // or false if the schedule should not be executed
};
 ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
// ---cut---
import { type ScheduleFilterResolvable } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

const myFilter: ScheduleFilterResolvable = async (schedule, meta) => {
  // Do some checks
  return true; // or false if the schedule should not be executed
};
 ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash

  // Do some checks

 ```
  </Tab>

</Step>
<Step>

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSchedule } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
class MyFilter extends AbstractScheduleFilter {}
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySchedule extends AbstractSchedule {
  protected override readonly filter = new MyFilter();
}
```
  </Tab>

## Examples [#examples]

### Maintenance Filter [#maintenance-filter]

A filter that checks if the system is in maintenance mode, and prevents the schedule from running if it is.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractScheduleFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { Schedule, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MaintenanceFilter extends AbstractScheduleFilter {
  public async check(schedule: Schedule, meta: Metadata): Promise<boolean> {
    // Check if the system is in maintenance mode, e.g. from an env variable or database
    return process.env.MAINTENANCE_MODE !== 'true';
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractScheduleFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { Schedule, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MaintenanceFilter extends AbstractScheduleFilter {
  public async check(schedule: Schedule, meta: Metadata): Promise<boolean> {
    // Check if the system is in maintenance mode, e.g. from an env variable or database
    return process.env.MAINTENANCE_MODE !== 'true';
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractScheduleFilter } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { Schedule, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MaintenanceFilter extends AbstractScheduleFilter {
  public async check(schedule: Schedule, meta: Metadata): Promise<boolean> {
    // Check if the system is in maintenance mode, e.g. from an env variable or database
    return process.env.MAINTENANCE_MODE !== 'true';
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

### Production Filter [#production-filter]

A filter that restricts the execution to the production environment.

  <Tab>

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractScheduleFilter } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { Schedule, Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class ProductionFilter extends AbstractScheduleFilter {
  public async check(schedule: Schedule, meta: Metadata): Promise<boolean> {
    return process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production';
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>

# Schedules Overview (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/schedules)

`Schedules` are objects that are ticked some time in the future, and can be used as a feature complete way of scheduling events in your bot, apart from Node's `setInterval()` API.

In essence, a `Schedule` object contains its ticking logic and its interval of when it wishes to be executed, which can be in [cron](https://crontab.guru/) format, in an amount of ms (`number`), or as a `Date`.

## Quick example [#quick-example]

Let's create a schedule that updates the activity with the member count every half hour:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { type DjsBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: DjsBot;
// ---cut---
import { AbstractSchedule, TypedFields, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MemberCountSchedule extends AbstractSchedule {
  protected readonly interval = '*/30 * * * *';

  public async tick(meta: Metadata) {
    const bot = TypedFields.DjsBot.get(meta, true);
    const client = bot.getClient().getEmitter();
    if (!client.user) return;

    const memberCount = client.guilds.cache.reduce((acc, guild) => acc + guild.memberCount, 0);
    await client.user.setActivity(`Members: ${memberCount}`);
  }
}

await bot.getScheduleManager().addSchedule(new MemberCountSchedule());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { type Bot as CoreBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: CoreBot;
// ---cut---
import { AbstractSchedule, TypedFields, type Metadata } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import { ActivityType, PresenceUpdateStatus } from '@discordjs/core';

class MemberCountSchedule extends AbstractSchedule {
  protected readonly interval = '*/30 * * * *';

  public async tick(meta: Metadata) {
    // GatewayCoreBot types the client as a gateway CoreNyxClient, which presences need
    const bot = TypedFields.GatewayCoreBot.get(meta, true);
    const client = bot.getClient().getEmitter();
    const api = bot.getClient().getApi();

    // Ideally you should cache and update these, but it's a simple example
    const guilds = await api.users.getGuilds({ with_counts: true });

    const memberCount = guilds.reduce((acc, guild) => acc + (guild.approximate_member_count ?? 0), 0);

    await client.updatePresence(
      0, // Shard ID
      {
        since: null,
        activities: [{ name: `Members: ${memberCount}`, type: ActivityType.Playing }],
        status: PresenceUpdateStatus.Online,
        afk: false,
      },
    );
  }
}

await bot.getScheduleManager().addSchedule(new MemberCountSchedule());
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
Presences are set through the gateway connection, so HTTP bots can't set them. Schedules themselves work the same as
with `@discordjs/core`, as long as the process stays alive.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Given it uses the provided metadata, it'll work even if the same instance is used across multiple bots.

## Schedule Job [#schedule-job]

When a schedule is added, a job will be created for it, which is responsible for notifying the framework when it is time to run it.
It's a wrapper over a more "lower-level" component that will actually do the ticking, like a cron job, a timer, etc.

<Callout>
  How the job is created is entirely customizable.
  By default, cron strings and `Date`s use the [croner npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/croner), and millisecond intervals use a timer with millisecond precision.
</Callout>

There are multiple ways to get it, but given a schedule itself does not depend on a bot, you'll always need the bot:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { NyxBot, Schedule } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
declare const schedule: Schedule;
// ---cut---
const fromScheduler = bot.getScheduleManager().getScheduler().getJobForSchedule(schedule);
const fromSchedule = schedule.getJob(bot);
const whenBeingAdded = await bot.getScheduleManager().addSchedule(schedule);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { NyxBot, Schedule } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
declare const schedule: Schedule;
// ---cut---
const fromScheduler = bot.getScheduleManager().getScheduler().getJobForSchedule(schedule);
const fromSchedule = schedule.getJob(bot);
const whenBeingAdded = await bot.getScheduleManager().addSchedule(schedule);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import type { NyxBot, Schedule } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const bot: NyxBot;
declare const schedule: Schedule;
// ---cut---
const fromScheduler = bot.getScheduleManager().getScheduler().getJobForSchedule(schedule);
const fromSchedule = schedule.getJob(bot);
const whenBeingAdded = await bot.getScheduleManager().addSchedule(schedule);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

It's the entry point for interacting with the schedule's ticking logic, and can be used to pause or resume it externally.

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { UndestroyableScheduleJobAdapter } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const job: UndestroyableScheduleJobAdapter<unknown>;
// ---cut---
await job.pause();
await job.resume();

// A croner `Cron` for cron strings and Dates, or the current timeout for ms intervals
// Depending on this is fragile and not intended, but it doesn't change for the same major version
const rawTicker = job.getRaw();
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { UndestroyableScheduleJobAdapter } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const job: UndestroyableScheduleJobAdapter<unknown>;
// ---cut---
await job.pause();
await job.resume();

// A croner `Cron` for cron strings and Dates, or the current timeout for ms intervals
// Depending on this is fragile and not intended, but it doesn't change for the same major version
const rawTicker = job.getRaw();
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import type { UndestroyableScheduleJobAdapter } from '@nyx-discord/http';
declare const job: UndestroyableScheduleJobAdapter<unknown>;
// ---cut---
await job.pause();
await job.resume();

// A croner `Cron` for cron strings and Dates, or the current timeout for ms intervals
// Depending on this is fragile and not intended, but it doesn't change for the same major version
const rawTicker = job.getRaw();
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Metadata [#metadata]

When extending nyx with plugins, you may want to specify extra data for them. You can do so with the `Metadata` object, saved on the schedule.

<Callout>
While schedules internally save a `Metadata`, the return type of `#getMeta()` is a `ReadonlyMetadata`,
meaning that external objects can read the object, but not modify it.
</Callout>

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSchedule } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySchedule extends AbstractSchedule {
  protected override readonly meta = {
    someKey: 'someValue',
  };
}

const schedule = new MySchedule();
const meta = schedule.getMeta();
const value = meta['someKey']; // 'someValue'
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSchedule } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySchedule extends AbstractSchedule {
  protected override readonly meta = {
    someKey: 'someValue',
  };
}

const schedule = new MySchedule();
const meta = schedule.getMeta();
const value = meta['someKey']; // 'someValue'
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractSchedule } from '@nyx-discord/http';

// ---cut-start---
// @ts-expect-error Incomplete example
// ---cut-end---
class MySchedule extends AbstractSchedule {
  protected override readonly meta = {
    someKey: 'someValue',
  };
}

const schedule = new MySchedule();
const meta = schedule.getMeta();
const value = meta['someKey']; // 'someValue'
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

For a more type-safe approach, you can use `TypedFields`. Check the [Metadata](/use/other/meta) page for more information.


# Middlewares (https://nyx-discord.github.io/nyx/guide/use/schedules/middlewares)

Middlewares are objects or callbacks that run before any schedule is executed. They can do some pre-processing logic and store it in the metadata, or even prevent the subscriber from being executed.

For general information about middlewares, you must first read the general [Middlewares](/use/other/middlewares) guide.

## Usage [#usage]

<Steps>
<Step>

### Creation [#creation]

Either:
- Create a class that extends `AbstractScheduleMiddleware` and implements the `check()` method.
<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractScheduleMiddleware } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
import type { Schedule, Metadata, MiddlewareResponse } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

class MyMiddleware extends AbstractScheduleMiddleware {
  public async check(
    schedule: Schedule,
    meta: Metadata
  ): Promise<MiddlewareResponse> {
    // Do some pre-processing logic
    return this.true();
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { AbstractScheduleMiddleware } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
import type { Schedule, Metadata, MiddlewareResponse } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

class MyMiddleware extends AbstractScheduleMiddleware {
  public async check(
    schedule: Schedule,
    meta: Metadata
  ): Promise<MiddlewareResponse> {
    // Do some pre-processing logic
    return this.true();
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { AbstractScheduleMiddleware } from '@nyx-discord/http';
import type { Schedule, Metadata, MiddlewareResponse } from '@nyx-discord/http';

class MyMiddleware extends AbstractScheduleMiddleware {
  public async check(
    schedule: Schedule,
    meta: Metadata
  ): Promise<MiddlewareResponse> {
    // Do some pre-processing logic
    return this.true();
  }
}
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

- Create a function that returns a `MiddlewareResponse`.
<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { type ScheduleMiddlewareResolvable } from '@nyx-discord/djs';

const myCallbackMiddleware: ScheduleMiddlewareResolvable = async (schedule, meta) => {
  // Do some pre-processing logic
  return {
    allowed: true,
    checkNext: true,
  };
};
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import { type ScheduleMiddlewareResolvable } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';

const myCallbackMiddleware: ScheduleMiddlewareResolvable = async (schedule, meta) => {
  // Do some pre-processing logic
  return {
    allowed: true,
    checkNext: true,
  };
};
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import { type ScheduleMiddlewareResolvable } from '@nyx-discord/http';

const myCallbackMiddleware: ScheduleMiddlewareResolvable = async (schedule, meta) => {
  // Do some pre-processing logic
  return {
    allowed: true,
    checkNext: true,
  };
};
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>

### Registration [#registration]

Register it to the executor's `MiddlewareList`:

<Tabs items={['discord.js', '@discordjs/core', 'HTTP']}>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { AbstractScheduleMiddleware, ScheduleMiddlewareResolvable, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs';
declare const MyMiddleware: new () => AbstractScheduleMiddleware;
declare const myCallbackMiddleware: ScheduleMiddlewareResolvable;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
bot.getScheduleManager().getExecutor().getMiddleware().add(new MyMiddleware(), myCallbackMiddleware);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
```ts twoslash
import type { AbstractScheduleMiddleware, ScheduleMiddlewareResolvable, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/djs-core';
declare const MyMiddleware: new () => AbstractScheduleMiddleware;
declare const myCallbackMiddleware: ScheduleMiddlewareResolvable;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
bot.getScheduleManager().getExecutor().getMiddleware().add(new MyMiddleware(), myCallbackMiddleware);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Same as `@discordjs/core`, importing from `@nyx-discord/http`:

```ts twoslash
import type { AbstractScheduleMiddleware, ScheduleMiddlewareResolvable, NyxBot } from '@nyx-discord/http';

declare const myCallbackMiddleware: ScheduleMiddlewareResolvable;
declare const bot: NyxBot;
// ---cut---
bot.getScheduleManager().getExecutor().getMiddleware().add(new MyMiddleware(), myCallbackMiddleware);
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
</Steps>
